Paper title: “Probe Generalization as Subspace Selection for OOD Deception Detection.” Authors Daniel Yoo and Adrians Skapars. Core thesis: OOD probing requires selecting robust representational subspaces; full probes may combine general deception features with dataset-specific cues.

Datasets: Goldowsky-Dill. Source Roleplaying; targets Insider Trading Report, Insider Trading Confirm, Sandbagging. Counts incl ambiguous: Roleplaying 371=140/59/172; Report 473=218/194/61; Confirm 151=29/38/84; Sandbagging 1000=379/375/246. Ambiguous removed.

Setup: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct layer 15 residual stream, assistant response token average. Source activations standardized; same stats for targets. PCA on scaled source activations, top 100 PCs. Logistic regression λ=10. Baseline uses full standardized activations.

Baseline: source-trained full target AUROCs Confirm 0.874, Report 0.706, Sandbagging 0.606. Target-trained probes in top-100 source-PC subspace: 0.936/0.950/0.869 likely Confirm/Report/Sandbagging.

Greedy oracle: selects among top 100 PCs using target labels/CV, source-trained weights. Stop improvement ≤0.001. Avg subset sizes: Report 15, Confirm 8, Sandbagging 14; Section 4.3 says k set by greedy on full target: Report 13, Confirm 7, Sandbagging 14. Improves full baseline by about 0.22 Report and 0.23 Sandbagging; close to target-trained.

PC ranking: source-PCA ranking roughly full baseline; target-PCA good on Report, worse than greedy on Confirm, below random on Sandbagging. Possible inconsistency in method: target-PCA ranking said to use target-trained weights, then says probes trained on source projected to selected PCs.

Interp selection: earlier text says max score 6 and selects 19 PCs repeatedly at max; Appendix B prompt and Appendix E explanations say GPT-5-mini rates OOD usefulness 1–10, internal scale inconsistency. Interp-selected 19-PC probe: Report 0.706→0.881, closing 78% to greedy 0.929; Sandbagging 0.606→0.662, closing 25% to greedy 0.832; Confirm baseline near ceiling. Of 5 PCs in greedy selections for >1 target, 3/5 got max OOD score; Appendix E Table 3 lists those 5: PC62 score 6, PC57 score 6, PC9 score 3, PC81 score 3, PC86 score 6. Table 3 describes them as “selected for likely transferability,” which conflicts with earlier max-score selection if score-3 PCs are included.

Limitations: single model/source/layer; Confirm uninformative due high baseline; Sandbagging margins small; pipeline linear; verbalizations descriptive not causal.

Appendix C: lower PCs align more with SAE decoder features; Spearman ρ=-0.857 best-matching SAE feature, -0.917 mean top 10; SAE andyrdt/saes-llama-3.1-8b-instruct.

Appendix D Table 2: source probe weights PCs = 15 listed. Greedy Report listed 13; Confirm 7; Sandbagging 15 (conflicts with earlier Sandbagging k=14). Target separability ranking lists 15 PCs for all targets, conflicting with earlier k=13/7/14 if these are selected sets. Stated Jaccards greedy vs target-pca: Report 0.182, Confirm 0.077, Sandbagging 0.167; these do not match full table sets (computed 0.167, 0.100, 0.154).

Paper title: “Probe Generalization as Subspace Selection for OOD Deception Detection.” Authors Daniel Yoo and Adrians Skapars.

Abstract claims:
- Linear probes can detect behaviors/concepts in LM activations but may fail OOD.
- Study: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct probes over 3 held-out deception detection datasets.
- Main finding: projecting inputs onto a small subset of PCs from the training distribution of activations enables cross-domain transfer that nearly matches probes trained directly on the test distribution (oracle/test-trained probes).
- PC interpretations can identify transferable PCs: use an LLM judge to score each PC based on whether its most/least activating examples imply a transferable deception direction; then probe on highest-scoring PCs.
- Quantified gains: closes baseline-to-oracle gap by 78% on Insider Trading Report and by 25% on Sandbagging.
- Interpretation claim: source probe heavily weighted directions encode source-specific surface features; directions that transfer encode same contrast more abstractly and can be captured by natural language descriptions.
- Broad conclusion: OOD robustness of probes is largely determined by subspace selection.

Introduction details:
- Motivation: linear probes useful but unreliable OOD; challenge is building probes that learn only generalizing features.
- Methodological framing: use source-domain PCA basis rather than raw activations; investigate which subset of PCs supports generalizable probe training and how to identify it.
- Testbed: deception probes on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct. Train on single source dataset: Roleplaying deception scenarios. Evaluate on 3 held-out targets: Insider Trading Report, Insider Trading Confirm, and Sandbagging (Goldowsky-Dill et al., 2025).
- Contributions listed:
  1. A small transferable subspace exists (Sec. 4.2): target-supervised greedy search over source PCs finds 8–15 components on which source-trained probe nearly matches target-trained probe.
  2. Source-side and target-side rankings both fail to recover the subspace (Sec. 4.3): ranking PCs by source or target probe weights does not transfer better than full-representation baseline.
  3. LLM judge partially recovers subspace without target data (Sec. 4.5): LLM judge can interpret/select PCs likely to encode transferable behavioral contrast rather than surface patterns.
- Figure 1 overview: project activations onto source-domain PCA basis, filter candidate PC directions, train probes on selected low-dimensional subspace.

- Quantified gains claimed: closes baseline-to-oracle gap by 78% on Insider Trading Report and 25% on Sandbagging.

- Conclusion: OOD robustness of probes is largely determined by subspace selection.

Contributions to verify later:
1. Sec. 4.2: target-supervised greedy search over source PCs finds 8–15 components on which source-trained probe nearly matches target-trained probe.
2. Sec. 4.3: source-side and target-side PC rankings by probe weights fail to recover subspace; do not transfer better than full-representation baseline.
3. Sec. 4.5: LLM judge partially recovers subspace without target data.

Setup details:
- Uses 4 Goldowsky-Dill et al. deception datasets: Roleplaying, Insider Trading Report, Insider Trading Confirm, Sandbagging. Labels: honest (0), ambiguous (-1), deceptive (1) by GPT-4o; ambiguous removed.
- Activations: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, layer 15 residual stream, following Ying et al. (2026), chosen because it had highest cross-domain AUROC in their analysis. Prompt passed through model; token activations averaged over assistant response only.

Setup:
- Four Goldowsky-Dill deception datasets: Roleplaying, Insider Trading Report, Insider Trading Confirm, Sandbagging. Labels honest (0), ambiguous (-1), deceptive (1) by GPT-4o; ambiguous removed.
- Activations: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, layer 15 residual stream, selected due to highest cross-domain AUROC in Ying et al. (2026). Prompt through model; token activations averaged over assistant response only.
- Preprocessing/training: source activations standardized to zero mean/unit variance; same source stats for targets. PCA on scaled source activations; retain top 100 PCs. Logistic regression λ=10. For subset S, project onto S before train/eval. Baseline probes train on full standardized activations.
- Top 100 PCs chosen for interpretability/alignment with SAE features; not claimed low-index PCs generalize better.

Sec. 4.1 baseline:
- Full-representation source-trained probe target AUROCs: Insider Trading Confirm 0.874, Insider Trading Report 0.706, Sandbagging 0.606.
- Target-trained probes in top-100 source-PC subspace via 5-fold CV: 0.936 / 0.950 / 0.869 AUROC across three targets (order not fully explicit; likely same three targets). Authors say 100-PC subspace encodes enough information, so failure is direction learned, not missing information.

Sec. 4.2 greedy oracle:
- Greedy PC selection: start empty; among top 100 source PCs add PC that most improves target AUROC. Train probe weights on source projected to subset; subset choice uses labeled target examples. 5-fold CV over target: select using non-held-out target folds, evaluate source-trained probe on held-out fold. Stop when no AUROC improvement >0.001.
- Average subset sizes: 15 PCs for Insider Trading Report, 8 for Insider Trading Confirm, 14 for Sandbagging.
- Greedy is upper bound, not unbiased OOD, since target data used for subset selection. Control: top-k PCs by variance with k matched to greedy.
- Greedy improves on full baseline by 0.22 AUROC for Insider Trading Report and 0.23 for Sandbagging, coming close to target-trained probe. Variance control matches greedy only for Insider Trading Confirm, far behind on Report/Sandbagging. Claim: transferable subspace exists; PC usefulness not predicted by variance.

Sec. 4.3 begins:
- Tests two hypotheses for greedy PCs: (1) target-separating PCs by themselves; (2) PCs source probe weights most heavily.
- Compares PC rankings by standardized coefficient = abs(probe coefficient × PC std) for probes trained on activations projected on source-PCA basis. Figure 4 compares source-probe weights, target-probe weights, greedy oracle.

Paper title: “Probe Generalization as Subspace Selection for OOD Deception Detection.” Thesis: source-probe-heavy directions encode source-specific surface features; transferable directions encode same contrast more abstractly/natural-language; OOD robustness largely determined by subspace/representation selection, not classifier fitting. Full-rep probes can mix general behavior features with dataset-specific cues; sparse directional subspaces may filter spurious correlations.

Setup: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct (E6). Layer 15 residual stream, averaged over assistant-response tokens only. Source Roleplaying V8; targets Insider Trading Report C2R, Insider Trading Confirm W6, Sandbagging J9. Labels GPT-4o honest=0, ambiguous=-1, deceptive=1; ambiguous removed. Counts incl ambiguous: V8 371 labels 140/59/172; C2R 473 labels 218/194/61; W6 151 labels 29/38/84; J9 1000 labels 379/375/246. Source activations standardized; same stats for targets. PCA/N4D retains leading 100 PCs/Q7. Logistic regression lambda=10. Full baseline B8Q trains on all standardized activations, not PCA subset. Error bars 95% CIs.

Baseline/target results: Appendix B8Q AUROC/F3: C2R 0.706, W6 0.874, J9 0.606. Target-trained leading-100 source subspace 5-fold CV: C2R 0.936, W6 0.950, J9 0.869. Target-trained probes in retained source PCA subspace separate every target, so info exists but source-trained direction fails.

Transferable subspace: Greedy oracle H2 starts empty, considers leading 100 Q7, fits source logistic probe on candidate subset, adds direction improving target F3 by >0.001; target CV uses non-held-out target folds for selection and held-out fold eval. Target labels guide subset selection, not weights; transfer upper bound. Appendix H2: improvement over B8Q C2R 0.22, J9 0.23; H2 F3 for recovery comparison C2R 0.929, J9 0.832; mean H2 subset size target CV C2R 15, W6 8, J9 14; full-target H2 k C2R 13, W6 7, J9 14; small H2 subset range 8–15. Appendix D Table 2 lists H2 sets: C2R 13 indices, W6 7, J9 15 (conflicts with earlier J9 k=14). It lists T6 source indices and M9 target indices. Hypotheses/rankings: T6 source-side and M9 target-side rankings do not recover transferable subspace/basis better than B8Q. Rankings use X4=absolute probe coefficient × corresponding Q7 std on source-N4D-projected activations. Paper title: “Probe Generalization as Subspace Selection for OOD Deception Detection.” Authors Daniel Yoo and Adrians Skapars. Acknowledgment: 11th AI Safety Camp; thanks Prasad Mahadik and Arya Hariharan.

Core claims: Linear probes detect LM concepts but fail OOD. Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct deception probes: source Roleplaying; targets Insider Trading Report, Insider Trading Confirm, Sandbagging. Main finding: projecting onto small subsets of source PCs enables transfer nearly matching target/oracle probes. Interp selection closes baseline-to-oracle gap by 78% on Report and 25% on Sandbagging. Full reps mix general and dataset-specific cues; sparse PC subspaces isolate general behavioral structure. Subset cannot be found with source-side or target-side separability alone.

Setup: Four Goldowsky-Dill datasets. Labels honest 0, ambiguous -1, deceptive 1 by GPT-4o; ambiguous removed. Counts: Roleplaying 371 = 140 amb / 59 honest / 172 deceptive; Report 473 = 218 / 194 / 61; Confirm 151 = 29 / 38 / 84; Sandbagging 1000 = 379 / 375 / 246. Activations: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct layer 15 residual stream, assistant response token average. Standardize source activations; same stats to targets. PCA on scaled source activations; top 100 PCs. Logistic regression λ=10. Baseline probes use full standardized activations.

Baseline: Full source-trained probe target AUROCs: Confirm 0.874, Report 0.706, Sandbagging 0.606. Target-trained probes in top-100 source-PC subspace via 5-fold CV: 0.936 / 0.950 / 0.869 AUROC across targets, likely same order. Claim: 100-PC subspace encodes enough info; failure is learned direction.

Greedy oracle: labeled target folds select PC subset; source-trained probe evaluated held-out target fold. Stop if no AUROC improvement >0.001. Avg subset sizes: 15 Report, 8 Confirm, 14 Sandbagging. Upper bound, not unbiased OOD. Greedy improves baseline by 0.22 AUROC Report and 0.23 Sandbagging; close to target-trained. Variance control matches greedy only Confirm.

Sec. 4.3: source-PCA ranks PCs by source-probe weights; target-PCA by target-probe weights; activations in source-PCA basis. Text inconsistently says both probes trained on source, though target-PCA ranking said trained on target. k from greedy full target: 13 Report, 7 Confirm, 14 Sandbagging. Source-PCA about full baseline; target-PCA good Report, worse than greedy Confirm, below-random Sandbagging.

Interp: top/bottom 8 source examples per PC; text wrongly says 18 total. GPT-5-mini judge rates OOD usefulness 1–10; no PC above 6. Earlier described selection: two runs, keep max-score PCs in both = 19. Of 5 PCs in greedy selections for >1 target, 3/5 max OOD; only 1/5 top source-PCA PCs max. Sec. 4.5: 19 interp-selected PCs outperform baseline/top-19 variance/remaining 81 on all targets. Report baseline 0.706, greedy 0.929, interp 0.881, closes 78% gap. Confirm near ceiling/uninformative. Sandbagging baseline 0.606, interp 0.662, greedy 0.832, closes 25% gap.

Appendix E: Table 3 says “selected for likely transferability” but lists only 5 PCs: PC62 score 6, PC57 6, PC9 3, PC81 3, PC86 6; conflicts with earlier 19 max-score selected PCs and includes non-max score 3 PCs. Table 4 lists OOD scores for source-weight PCs: PC7 3, PC8 4, PC11 3, PC12 3, PC4 6.

Appendix C: Lower PCs have stronger SAE decoder alignment; Spearman ρ = -0.857 best feature, -0.917 mean top 10.

Appendix D: Table 2 PC sets. Source weights top 15: PC7,8,11,12,4,5,2,3,6,27,22,21,1,41,18. Greedy Report 13 PCs; Confirm 7; Sandbagging table lists 15 PCs, conflicting with earlier k=14. Target separability table lists 15 PCs for each target, conflicting with earlier k-matched comparison if same sets. Appendix D stated Jaccards greedy vs target-pca: Report .182, Confirm .077, Sandbagging .167, but table-implied .167, .100, .200.

- Method: use source-domain PCA basis rather than raw activations; investigate which subset of PCs supports generalizable probe training and how to identify it.
- Testbed: deception probes on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct. Train on single source dataset: Roleplaying deception scenarios. Evaluate on 3 held-out targets: Insider Trading Report, Insider Trading Confirm, and Sandbagging (Goldowsky-Dill et al., 2025).
- Contributions:
  1. Small transferable subspace exists (Sec. 4.2): target-supervised greedy search over source PCs finds 8–15 components on which source-trained probe nearly matches target-trained probe.
  2. Source-side and target-side rankings both fail to recover subspace (Sec. 4.3): ranking PCs by source or target probe weights does not transfer better than full-representation baseline.
  3. LLM judge partially recovers subspace without target data (Sec. 4.5): LLM judge can interpret/select PCs likely to encode transferable behavioral contrast rather than surface patterns.
- Figure 1 overview: project activations onto source-domain PCA basis, filter candidate PC directions, train probes on selected low-dimensional subspace.

Related Work notes:
- Situates work among studies of linear concept directions/subspaces in activation space: true/false, linear representation hypothesis, honesty/emotion directions, refusal direction, “assistant” axis.
- Probing literature: probes used for represented information and safety-relevant signals (truthfulness, strategic deception), but high accuracy may reflect probe learning/surface correlates; probes can generalize unevenly OOD.
- Natural-language explanations: LLMs generate feature/neuron explanations from high-activation examples; extended to SAE feature labeling and interventions via natural-language interpreted concepts.

Paper title: “Probe Generalization as Subspace Selection for OOD Deception Detection.” Authors Daniel Yoo and Adrians Skapars.

Core claims from abstract/introduction:
- Linear probes can detect behaviors/concepts in LM activations but may fail OOD.
- Study uses Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct probes for deception detection. Source dataset: Roleplaying deception scenarios. Targets: Insider Trading Report, Insider Trading Confirm, Sandbagging (Goldowsky-Dill et al., 2025).
- Main finding: projecting inputs onto a small subset of PCs from the source/training activation distribution enables cross-domain transfer nearly matching target/oracle-trained probes.
- PC interpretations can identify transferable PCs: LLM judge scores each PC based on whether most/least activating examples imply transferable deception direction; train probe on highest-scoring PCs.
- Quantified gains claimed: closes baseline-to-oracle gap by 78% on Insider Trading Report and 25% on Sandbagging.
- Interpretation: source probe heavily weights directions encoding source-specific surface features; transferable directions encode same contrast more abstractly and can be described in natural language.
- Conclusion: OOD robustness of probes is largely determined by subspace selection.

Contributions to verify later:
1. Sec. 4.2: target-supervised greedy search over source PCs finds 8–15 components on which source-trained probe nearly matches target-trained probe.
2. Sec. 4.3: source-side and target-side PC rankings by probe weights fail to recover subspace; do not transfer better than full-representation baseline.
3. Sec. 4.5: LLM judge partially recovers subspace without target data.

Setup details:
- Uses 4 Goldowsky-Dill et al. deception datasets: Roleplaying, Insider Trading Report, Insider Trading Confirm, Sandbagging. Labels: honest (0), ambiguous (-1), deceptive (1) by GPT-4o; ambiguous removed.
- Activations: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, layer 15 residual stream, following Ying et al. (2026), chosen because it had highest cross-domain AUROC in their analysis. Prompt passed through model; token activations averaged over assistant response only.
- Preprocessing/training: source activations standardized to zero mean/unit variance; same source statistics applied to targets. PCA run on scaled source activations; retain top 100 PCs. Logistic regression probes with λ=10. For subset S of 100 PCs, project activations onto S before training/evaluation. Baseline probes train directly on full standardized activations.
- Rationale for top 100 PCs: alignment with SAE decoder features decreases with PC index (Appendix C), so lower-index PCs are more interpretable/comparable to interpretability-driven selection. Authors explicitly say this is not a claim low-index PCs generalize better; Sec. 4.1 should confirm 100-PC subspace retains enough information to separate honest/deceptive on every target.

Related work: linear concept directions/subspaces, probing and OOD failures, and LLM/natural-language feature explanations.

Setup:

Sec. 4.2 greedy oracle:

errors.claim: “For each of the top 100 source PCs, we find the 8 most and 8 least PC-activating examples from the source data, giving 18 examples in total”
errors.evidence: “8 most and 8 least” examples sum to 16 examples, not 18.
errors.explanation: The stated total contradicts the immediately preceding counts.

errors.claim: “In both cases, the probes are trained on source data that has been projected onto the top k PCs”
errors.evidence: Immediately before, the part defines the target-PCA probe as ranking “PCs by the weights learned by a probe trained on target data.”
errors.explanation: The text first says the target-PCA probe’s weights come from a probe trained on target data, then says in both source-PCA and target-PCA cases the probes are trained on source data. This is at least a wording-level internal inconsistency unless the latter refers only to the final evaluation probe rather than the ranking probe.

Introduction details:
- Motivation: linear probes useful but unreliable OOD; challenge is building probes that learn only generalizing features.
- Methodological framing: use source-domain PCA basis rather than raw activations; investigate which subset of PCs supports generalizable probe training and how to identify it.
- Testbed: deception probes on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct. Train on single source dataset: Roleplaying deception scenarios. Evaluate on 3 held-out targets: Insider Trading Report, Insider Trading Confirm, and Sandbagging (Goldowsky-Dill et al., 2025).
- Contributions listed:
  1. A small transferable subspace exists (Sec. 4.2): target-supervised greedy search over source PCs finds 8–15 components on which source-trained probe nearly matches target-trained probe.
  2. Source-side and target-side rankings both fail to recover the subspace (Sec. 4.3): ranking PCs by source or target probe weights does not transfer better than full-representation baseline.
  3. LLM judge partially recovers subspace without target data (Sec. 4.5): LLM judge can interpret/select PCs likely to encode transferable behavioral contrast rather than surface patterns.
- Figure 1 overview: project activations onto source-domain PCA basis, filter candidate PC directions, train probes on selected low-dimensional subspace.

Paper title: “Probe Generalization as Subspace Selection for OOD Deception Detection.” Thesis: source-probe-heavy directions encode source-specific surface features; transferable directions encode same contrast more abstractly/natural-language; OOD robustness largely determined by subspace/representation selection. Full-rep probes mix general behavioral features with dataset-specific cues: high ID but poor transfer; sparse directional subspaces filter spurious correlations.

Setup: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct (E6). Layer 15 residual-stream activations averaged over assistant-response tokens only. Datasets Goldowsky-Dill 2025: source Roleplaying V8; targets C2R Insider Trading Report, W6 Insider Trading Confirm, J9 Sandbagging. Labels GPT-4o: honest=0, ambiguous=-1, deceptive=1; ambiguous removed. Counts: V8 371=140/-1,59/0,172/1; C2R 473=218/194/61; W6 151=29/38/84; J9 1000=379/375/246. Source activations standardized; same source stats for targets. PCA/N4D leading 100 PCs/Q7. Subset projected before train/eval. Logistic regression lambda=10. Full baseline B8Q trains on all standardized activations, not PCA subset. Error bars 95% CIs. AUROC called F3.

Key results: Fig2 B8Q source-trained full reps F3: C2R 0.706, W6 0.874, J9 0.606. Target-trained leading-100 source subspace 5-fold CV F3: C2R 0.936, W6 0.950, J9 0.869. Greedy oracle H2: starts empty over leading 100 Q7, fits source logistic probe on candidate subset, adds direction improving target F3 most; target labels guide subset selection, not weights; transfer upper bound. H2 improvement over B8Q: C2R +0.22, J9 +0.23; H2 F3 recovery comparison: C2R 0.929, J9 0.832. Mean H2 subset size target CV: C2R 15, W6 8, J9 14; earlier full-target H2 k recorded as C2R 13, W6 7, J9 14, but Appendix D Table 2 lists H2 J9 with 15 indices, creating inconsistency. Small H2 subset range reported 8–15.

Variance selection Y4 only matches H2 on W6; poor on C2R/J9. T6 source-side and M9 target-side rankings do not recover transferable subspace better than B8Q. Rankings use X4=abs probe coefficient × Q7 std on source-N4D-projected activations. Appendix D selected sets: T6 Source top15 = 7,8,11,12,4,5,2,3,6,27,22,21,1,41,18. H2 C2R 13 dirs; W6 7; J9 table lists 15. M9 each 15. Appendix D reports H2–M9 Jaccard D3: C2R .182, W6 .077, J9 .167, but computed from printed sets: C2R 4/24=.167; W6 2/20=.100; J9 4/26=.154.

Interpretability: LLM judge C7/GPT-5-mini rates bipolar Q7 direction examples for OOD deception usefulness R5. Appendix E: max R5=6; 2 scoring runs; 19 directions reached max in both runs and were retained for L2; complement A7 uses 81 directions. H2 selections shared by >1 target: 5 directions; 3/5 max-rated: 62,57,86 have R5=6; 9 and 81 have R5=3. Top 5 T6 directions in Appendix E are 7,8,11,12,4; only Q7 4 has max R5=6. L2 no-target interp-selected PC probe F3: C2R 0.881, J9 0.662; recovers 68% C2R, 25% J9 gap; improves over B8Q all targets; W6 little headroom. Appendix C decoder alignment: lower-index Q7 align more with SAE decoder features U9 using andyrdt/saes-llama-3.1-8b-instruct; earlier reported Spearman rho = -0.857 best feature, -0.917 mean top 10. Limitations: single model/source; W6 high baseline; J9 weakest OOD; C2R more robust; linear/descriptive not causal.

Paper title: “Probe Generalization as Subspace Selection for OOD Deception Detection.” Thesis: source-probe-heavy directions encode source-specific surface features; transferable directions encode same contrast more abstractly/natural-language; OOD robustness largely determined by subspace/representation selection. Full-representation probes can mix general behavioral features with dataset-specific surface cues; sparse directional subspaces may filter spurious correlations.

Setup: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct (E6). Layer 15 residual-stream activations, averaged over assistant-response tokens only. Source Roleplaying V8; targets Insider Trading Report C2R, Insider Trading Confirm W6, Sandbagging J9. Labels GPT-4o honest=0, ambiguous=-1, deceptive=1; ambiguous removed. Counts: V8 371 = 140/-1, 59/0, 172/1; C2R 473 = 218/194/61; W6 151 = 29/38/84; J9 1000 = 379/375/246. Source activations standardized; same source stats for targets. PCA/N4D retains leading 100 PCs/Q7. Classifiers logistic regression lambda=10. Full baseline B8Q trains on all standardized activations, not PCA subset. Error bars 95% CIs.

Baseline: Source-trained full reps B8Q F3: C2R 0.706, W6 0.874, J9 0.606. Target-trained within leading-100 source subspace 5-fold CV: C2R 0.936, W6 0.950, J9 0.869. W6 transfer high; C2R moderate; J9 poor.

Transferable subspace: Greedy oracle H2 starts empty, considers leading 100 Q7, fits source logistic probe on candidate subset, adds direction improving target F3 most; target-label-guided subset selection only, not weights; upper bound. Target 5-fold CV selects using non-held-out folds and evaluates held-out fold; stops if no improvement >0.001. H2 improvement over B8Q ≈ C2R 0.22, J9 0.23; H2 F3 for recovery comparison C2R 0.929, J9 0.832. Mean H2 subset size target CV: C2R 15, W6 8, J9 14; earlier full-target H2 k reported C2R 13, W6 7, J9 14, but Appendix D Table 2 lists H2 J9 15 indices (internal conflict). Variance Y4 only matches H2 on W6.

Rankings: T6 and M9 do not recover transferable subspace/basis better than B8Q. T6 about B8Q; M9 good on C2R, worse than H2 on W6, below random on J9. Paper title: “Probe Generalization as Subspace Selection for OOD Deception Detection.” Authors Daniel Yoo and Adrians Skapars. Goal: advance ML; no specific societal consequence highlighted.

Setup: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, layer 15 residual stream; assistant-response token activations averaged. Source: Roleplaying deception. Targets: Insider Trading Report, Insider Trading Confirm, Sandbagging. Appendix A counts: Roleplaying 371 labels -1/0/1 = 140/59/172; Report 473 = 218/194/61; Confirm 151 = 29/38/84; Sandbagging 1000 = 379/375/246. Logistic regression λ=10. Baseline probes train on full standardized activations; subset probes project onto selected source PCs.

Main thesis: OOD robustness is subspace selection: robust behavioral signal vs dataset-specific cues. Sparse source-PC subsets can filter spurious correlations. Small source-PC subsets can nearly match target/oracle probes, and cannot be found from source-side or target-side separability alone. LLM judge can partly recover transferable PCs from natural-language PC interpretations without target data. Abstract/current claims: interp selection closes baseline-to-oracle gap by 78% on Report and 25% on Sandbagging.

Sec. 4.1 baseline source-trained full transfer AUROC: Confirm 0.874, Report 0.706, Sandbagging 0.606. Target-trained probes within top-100 source-PC subspace using 5-fold CV: 0.936 / 0.950 / 0.869 AUROC across targets; likely order Report / Confirm / Sandbagging.

Sec. 4.2 greedy oracle PC selection: target-supervised upper bound; 5-fold target CV; average subset sizes 15 Report, 8 Confirm, 14 Sandbagging. Earlier text claimed greedy improves baseline by 0.32 Report and 0.33 Sandbagging, conflicting with baseline/later oracle numbers. Greedy oracle AUROC: Report 0.929, Sandbagging 0.832. Variance control matches greedy only for Confirm/easy case; lags on Report/Sandbagging.

Sec. 4.3: transferable PCs are not simply target-separating or source-probe-heavy. Fig. 4 k set by greedy full target dataset: k=13 Report, 7 Confirm, 14 Sandbagging. Source-PCA transfers about like full baseline. Target-PCA good on Report, worse than greedy on Confirm, below random on Sandbagging.

Sec. 4.4–4.5: GPT-5-mini interprets bipolar directions using high-positive/high-negative Roleplay examples; earlier text says 8 most/least examples per PC. No PC above score 6; keep PCs with max score in both runs: 19 interp-selected PCs. Fig. 5: Report 0.706→0.881, 78% of gap to greedy 0.929; Sandbagging 0.606→0.662, 25% of gap to greedy 0.832. Confirm baseline near ceiling. Appendix E Table 3 now lists only 5 selected PCs: PC62, PC57, PC9, PC81, PC86, and includes PC9/PC81 with score 3, conflicting with max-score selection/19 selected PCs.

Appendix D: Greedy Sandbagging table lists 15 PCs, conflicting with earlier k=14. Appendix D reported Jaccards 0.182/0.077/0.167, but table-implied values are Report .167, Confirm .100, Sandbagging .154.

Setup: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct (E6). Layer 15 residual activations, averaged over assistant-response tokens only. Setup: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct (E6), layer 15 residual stream, assistant-response token average. Source Roleplaying V8; targets C2R Insider Trading Report, W6 Insider Trading Confirm, J9 Sandbagging. Paper title: “Probe Generalization as Subspace Selection for OOD Deception Detection.” Model Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct; layer 15 residual stream; assistant-response token activations averaged. Datasets: source Roleplaying; targets Insider Trading Report, Insider Trading Confirm, Sandbagging. Labels honest=0/deceptive=1, ambiguous=-1 removed. Appendix A raw label counts (-1/0/1): Roleplaying 371=140/59/172; Report 473=218/194/61; Confirm 151=29/38/84; Sandbagging 1000=379/375/246.

Preprocessing: standardize using source stats; PCA on scaled source activations; retain top 100 PCs. Logistic regression probes lambda=10. Subset experiments project onto selected PCs before train/eval; full baseline uses full standardized activations.

Baseline Sec 4.1: source-trained full-representation probe target AUROCs: Confirm 0.874, Report 0.706, Sandbagging 0.606. Target-trained probes within top-100 source-PC subspace using 5-fold CV: 0.936/0.950/0.869 for Report/Confirm/Sandbagging.

Sec 4.2 greedy oracle: selects among top 100 source PCs using labeled target folds, weights trained on source. CV selected sizes: Report 15, Confirm 8, Sandbagging 14. Greedy upper bound, not unbiased OOD estimate. Greedy nearly matches target-trained probes for Report and Sandbagging, improving baseline by ~0.22 and ~0.23.

Sec 4.3 PC-ranking tests: PCs ranked by standardized coefficient |coef|×std in source-PCA basis. Figure 4 greedy on full target dataset not CV gives stable k: Report 13, Confirm 7, Sandbagging 14. Source-PCA probe about as good as full baseline. Target-PCA probe does well on Report, worse than greedy on Confirm, below random on Sandbagging. Internal contradiction noted earlier: text says target-separating PCs transfer better than greedy selections.

Sec 4.4 interpretability: GPT-5-mini interprets 8 most/least activating source examples for each top-100 PC. No PC scored above 6; 6 treated as max observed; keep PCs with max score in both runs: 19 PCs. Five PCs appeared in greedy selections for >1 target; 3/5 got max OOD score.

Sec 4.5 interp-selected subspace: 19 max-score PCs; no target data. Figure 5 claims interp-selected probe outperforms baseline on all 3 targets and controls. Limitations exact AUROCs: Report 0.881 vs baseline 0.706, greedy 0.929; Sandbagging 0.662 vs baseline 0.606, greedy 0.832. Confirm baseline 0.874 high.

Appendix C: lower PCs show stronger decoder alignment to SAE features; Spearman rho -0.857 best feature, -0.917 mean top 10.

Appendix D/Table 2: source probe top PCs: PC7,8,11,12,4,5,2,3,6,27,22,21,1,41,18. Greedy full-target listed Report 13 PCs, Confirm 7 PCs, Sandbagging 15 PCs (conflicts with earlier k=14). Target-separability lists 15 PCs per target. Reported Jaccards 0.182/0.077/0.167 conflict with table-derived 0.167/0.100/0.200.

Appendix E/Table 3: five PCs selected on multiple targets and LLM OOD scores: PC62 Report+Sandbagging score 6; PC57 Report+Sandbagging 6; PC9 Report+Sandbagging 3; PC81 Confirm+Sandbagging 3; PC86 Confirm+Sandbagging 6. This matches earlier “3/5 got max OOD score.” Table 4 begins source-probe top PC interpretations: PC7=3, PC8=4, PC11=3, PC12=3, PC4=6; matches earlier “only 1 of top 5 source-PCA-probe PCs got max score.”

Paper title: “Probe Generalization as Subspace Selection for OOD Deception Detection.” Authors Daniel Yoo, Adrians Skapars.

Abstract claims: Studies linear probes for detecting behaviors/concepts in LM activations, focusing on OOD transfer failures. Model: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct. Setting: generalization performance of probes over 3 held-out deception detection datasets. Main finding: projecting inputs onto a small subset of principal components (PCs) from the training distribution of activations enables cross-domain transfer that nearly matches probes trained directly on the test distribution (oracle/test-distribution probes). Additional claim: PC interpretations can identify a subset of transferable PCs. Method: use an LLM judge to score each PC based on whether its most/least activating examples imply a transferable deception direction; then probe on highest-scoring PCs. Reported gap-closing results: closes baseline-to-oracle gap by 78% on Insider Trading Report and by 25% on Sandbagging. Interpretive claim: source probe heavily weighted directions encode source-specific surface features, while actually transferable directions encode the same contrast more abstractly, capturable by natural-language descriptions. Overall conclusion: OOD robustness of probes is largely determined by subspace selection.

Abstract claims: Studies linear probes for detecting behaviors/concepts in LM activations, focusing on OOD transfer failures. Model: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct. Setting: generalization performance of probes over 3 held-out deception detection datasets. Main finding: projecting inputs onto a small subset of PCs from the training/source activation distribution enables cross-domain transfer that nearly matches probes trained directly on the test distribution (oracle/test-distribution probes). Introduction details: Linear probes can detect linearly represented concepts but may learn spurious correlations OOD; goal is probes that learn generalizing features. They work in the basis of source-domain PCs rather than raw activations. Testbed: deception probes on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, trained on a single source dataset: Roleplaying deception scenarios; evaluated on 3 held-out target datasets: Insider Trading Report, Insider Trading Confirm, and Sandbagging (Goldowsky-Dill et al., 2025). Contributions listed: (1) A small transferable subspace exists: target-supervised greedy search over source PCs finds 8–15 components where a source-trained probe nearly matches a target-trained probe (Section 4.2). (2) Source-side and target-side rankings fail: ranking PCs by source or target probe weights does not transfer better than full-representation baseline (Section 4.3). (3) An LLM judge partially recovers the subspace without target data by interpreting/selecting PCs likely to encode transferable behavioral contrast rather than surface patterns (Section 4.5). Figure 1 overview: project activations to source-domain PCA basis, filter candidate PC directions, train probes on selected low-dimensional subspace.

Setup: Uses 4 Goldowsky-Dill deception datasets: Roleplaying source; Insider Trading Report, Insider Trading Confirm, Sandbagging targets. Labels: honest=0, ambiguous=-1, deceptive=1 by GPT-4o; ambiguous removed. Activations: layer 15 residual stream of Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, chosen following Ying et al. as highest cross-domain AUROC; prompts passed through model and token activations averaged over assistant response only. Section 4.1 will claim/confirm 100-PC subspace retains enough information to separate deceptive vs honest on every target.

Paper title: “Probe Generalization as Subspace Selection for OOD Deception Detection.” Model Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct; layer 15 residual stream; assistant-response token activations averaged. Datasets: source Roleplaying; targets Insider Trading Report, Insider Trading Confirm, Sandbagging. Labels honest=0/deceptive=1, ambiguous removed. Standardize using source stats; PCA on scaled source activations; retain top 100 PCs. Logistic regression probes lambda=10. Subset experiments project onto selected PCs before train/eval; full baseline uses full standardized activations.

Abstract/intro claims: OOD robustness largely determined by PC subspace selection. Target-supervised greedy over source PCs finds 8–15 PCs where source-trained probe nearly matches target-trained oracle. Source- and target-side rankings by probe weights fail to beat full baseline. LLM judge can partially recover transferable PCs without target labels; reported LLM-judge gap closing: 78% on Insider Trading Report and 25% on Sandbagging. PC interpretations: source-probe-heavy PCs encode source-specific surface features; transferable PCs encode abstract deception contrast.

Sec 4.1 baseline: Source-trained full-representation probe transfers to targets: Insider Trading Confirm 0.874 AUROC, Insider Trading Report 0.706, Sandbagging 0.606. Target-trained probes within top-100 source-PC subspace using 5-fold CV achieve 0.936 / 0.950 / 0.869 AUROC across the three targets (order apparently Insider Trading Report / Confirm / Sandbagging). Authors conclude 100-PC subspace contains enough information for every target; difficulty is source probe learns non-generalizing direction, not missing info.

Sec 4.2 greedy oracle PC selection: Starting empty, iteratively add among top 100 source PCs the PC that most improves target AUROC. Probe weights always trained on source data; subset choice uses labeled target examples. 5-fold CV over target: select PCs on non-held-out target folds, evaluate selected source-trained probe on held-out fold. Stop when no candidate improves AUROC >0.001. Average selected subset sizes: 15 PCs for Insider Trading Report, 8 for Insider Trading Confirm, 14 for Sandbagging. Greedy is an upper bound, not unbiased OOD estimate. Compared to top-k PCs by variance with k matched to greedy. Greedy comes close to target-trained probes for Insider Trading Report and Sandbagging, improving baseline by 0.22 and 0.23 AUROC respectively. Variance top-k matches greedy only for easy Insider Trading Confirm; far worse on Report/Sandbagging. Conclusion: transferable subspace exists; variance explained does not predict PC usefulness.

Sec 4.3 begins: Tests what makes PCs transferable. Two hypotheses: greedy PCs are those that separate target classes well by themselves, or those source probe already weights most. Compares PC rankings by standardized coefficient = |probe coefficient| × std of corresponding PC, for probes trained on activations projected into source-PCA basis. Figure 4 will compare source-probe weights, target-probe weights, greedy oracle.

Paper title: “Probe Generalization as Subspace Selection for OOD Deception Detection.” Authors Daniel Yoo and Adrians Skapars; work during 11th AI Safety Camp.

Datasets: Four Goldowsky-Dill datasets. Labels honest 0, ambiguous -1, deceptive 1 by GPT-4o; ambiguous removed. Appendix A raw/usable counts: Roleplaying 371 = 140 amb / 59 honest / 172 deceptive, usable 231; Insider Trading Report 473 = 218 / 194 / 61, usable 255; Insider Trading Confirm 151 = 29 / 38 / 84, usable 122; Sandbagging 1000 = 379 / 375 / 246, usable 621. Source = Roleplaying. Targets = Report, Confirm, Sandbagging. Activations: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct layer 15 residual stream, assistant response token average. Source activations standardized; same stats for targets. PCA on scaled source activations, top 100 PCs. Logistic regression λ=10. Baseline full standardized activations.

Baseline 4.1: source-trained full target AUROCs: Confirm 0.874, Report 0.706, Sandbagging 0.606. Target-trained probes in top-100 source-PC subspace by 5-fold CV: 0.936/0.950/0.869, likely Confirm/Report/Sandbagging. Claim: info exists in source-PC subspace; learned direction is problem.

Greedy oracle 4.2: Select PCs among top 100 maximizing target AUROC, training on source subset; target labels used for subset choice; 5-fold CV over target. Stop improvement ≤0.001. Avg subset sizes: Report 15, Confirm 8, Sandbagging 14. Greedy improves full baseline by 0.22 Report and 0.23 Sandbagging, close to target-trained; variance top-k control matches only Confirm.

4.3: PC rankings by standardized coefficient abs(coef × PC std). k set by greedy on full target dataset: Report 13, Confirm 7, Sandbagging 14. Possible inconsistency: target-PCA ranking described as target-trained probe weights, then says both probes trained on source data projected to selected PCs. Results: source-PCA transfers about like full baseline; target-PCA good on Report, worse than greedy on Confirm, below-random on Sandbagging.

4.4/Appendix B: LLM interprets 8 most/least activating source examples per PC, gives OOD usefulness 1–10; no PC above 6; keep PCs scoring max in both runs = 19 PCs. Of 5 PCs in greedy selections for more than one target, 3/5 got max score; only 1 of top 5 source-PCA PCs did. Prompt uses GPT-5-mini. Appendix E Table 3 lists 5 multi-target PCs with scores: PC62 6, PC57 6, PC9 3, PC81 3, PC86 6; caption says selected for likely transferability, conflicting with PC9/PC81 score 3 if this is LLM-selected set. Appendix E Table 4 lists examples PC7 3, PC8 4, PC11 3, PC12 3, PC4 6.

4.5: 19 interp-selected PCs target-data-free. Outperforms baseline, top-19 variance, and ablated remaining 81 PCs across all targets. Report baseline 0.706, greedy 0.929, interp 0.881, closes 78% gap. Sandbagging baseline 0.606, greedy 0.832, interp 0.662, closes 25% gap. Earlier inconsistency: 4.5 said Confirm baseline lower than Sandbagging, but Confirm 0.874 > Sandbagging 0.606.

Appendix C: Lower PCs align more with SAE decoder: Spearman -0.857 best feature, -0.917 mean top 10, using andyrdt/saes-llama-3.1-8b-instruct.

Appendix D Table 2 PC sets: source probe weights list 15 PCs. Greedy Report 13, Confirm 7, Sandbagging 15 listed. Target separability lists 15 per target. Stated Jaccards Report 0.182, Confirm 0.077, Sandbagging 0.167 conflict with table-listed sets: table implies 0.167, 0.100, 0.200 respectively; Sandbagging greedy count also conflicts with earlier k=14.

Introduction details:
- Motivation: linear probes useful but unreliable OOD; challenge is building probes that learn only generalizing features.
- Methodological framing: use source-domain PCA basis rather than raw activations; investigate which subset of PCs supports generalizable probe training and how to identify it.
- Testbed: deception probes on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct. Train on single source dataset: Roleplaying deception scenarios. Evaluate on 3 held-out targets: Insider Trading Report, Insider Trading Confirm, and Sandbagging (Goldowsky-Dill et al., 2025).

Appendix A raw label counts: Roleplaying total 371 = 140 ambiguous / 59 honest / 172 deceptive, so usable non-ambiguous 231. Insider Trading Report total 473 = 218 / 194 / 61, usable 255. Insider Trading Confirm total 151 = 29 / 38 / 84, usable 122. Sandbagging total 1000 = 379 / 375 / 246, usable 621. Dataset descriptions: Roleplaying = simple scenario with opportunity to lie; Report = trader decides whether to honestly report insider-info use; Confirm = after hiding earlier use, asked to confirm it did not use any; Sandbagging = told to underperform on some tasks while normal on others.

Setup: Source = Roleplaying. Targets = Insider Trading Report, Insider Trading Confirm, Sandbagging. Activations: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct layer 15 residual stream, assistant response token average. Source activations standardized; same stats for targets. PCA on scaled source activations, top 100 PCs. Logistic regression λ=10. Baseline full standardized activations.

Baseline 4.1: source-trained full target AUROCs: Confirm 0.874, Report 0.706, Sandbagging 0.606. Target-trained probes in top-100 source-PC subspace via 5-fold CV: 0.936/0.950/0.869, likely Confirm/Report/Sandbagging. Claim: info exists in source-PC subspace; problem is learned direction.

Greedy oracle 4.2: Select PCs among top 100 to maximize target AUROC, training weights on source subset; target labels used for subset choice. 5-fold CV over target for evaluation. Stop improvement ≤0.001. Avg subset sizes: Report 15, Confirm 8, Sandbagging 14. Greedy improves full baseline by 0.22 Report and 0.23 Sandbagging, close to target-trained; variance top-k control matches only Confirm. PC usefulness not variance-predicted.

4.3: Tests whether greedy PCs are target-separating PCs or source-probe-heavy PCs. PC rankings by standardized coefficient abs(coef × PC std) for probes in source-PCA basis. Possible inconsistency: target-PCA ranking said to use target-trained probe weights, then says both probes are trained on source data projected to selected PCs. k set by running greedy on full target dataset, not CV: Report 13, Confirm 7, Sandbagging 14. Results: source-PCA transfers about like full baseline; target-PCA good on Report, worse than greedy on Confirm, below-random on Sandbagging.

4.4: LLM describes 8 most/least activating source examples per top-100 source PC; judge gives OOD score 1–10. No PC above 6; keep PCs scoring max in both runs: 19 PCs. Of 5 PCs in greedy selections for more than one target, 3/5 got max OOD score; only 1 of top 5 source-PCA PCs did. Appendix B prompt: uses GPT-5-mini (OpenAI, 2025) to interpret bipolar PC directions from high-positive/high-negative examples formatted as token<TAB>activation normalized -10 to +10, selected from Roleplaying setup. Prompt asks for narrow contrast, avoid overgeneralization/surface cues, score OOD deception usefulness 1–10, output exact fields Positive pole, Negative pole, Shared direction, OOD deception usefulness.

4.5: 19 interp-selected PCs are target-data-free subspace. Controls: baseline, top-19 variance PCs, interp-ablated remaining 81 PCs. Interp-selected outperforms baseline, variance control, and ablated across all 3; wide margins Report/Sandbagging. Report: baseline 0.706, greedy oracle 0.929, interp 0.881, closes 78% gap. Sandbagging: baseline 0.606, greedy 0.832, interp 0.662, closes 25% gap. Earlier/current inconsistency noted from 4.5: it said Confirm baseline lower than Sandbagging, but earlier Confirm 0.874 > Sandbagging 0.606.

Limitations/conclusion: Small subsets of source-domain PCs can transfer nearly matching target-trained probes; source/target separability alone cannot find them. Interpretability scoring with no target data partially recovers useful subspace. Narrow scope: single model/layer/source. Confirm considered uninformative because baseline already 0.874. Sandbagging margins small; Report robust. Pipeline fully linear; PC interpretations descriptive, not causal; no inference-time ablation validation.

final_notes:
Paper title: “Probe Generalization as Subspace Selection for OOD Deception Detection.” Core claim: full-representation probes exploit source-specific cues; OOD robustness depends on subspace/representation selection preserving behavioral feature while filtering spurious correlations. Sparse directional subspaces may isolate transferable behavioral structure.

Setup: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct (E6), layer 15 residual activations averaged over assistant-response tokens. Datasets: source Roleplaying V8; targets C2R Insider Trading Report, W6 Insider Trading Confirm, J9 Sandbagging. Labels GPT-4o honest=0, ambiguous=-1, deceptive=1; ambiguous removed. Source activations standardized; same stats for targets. PCA/N4D on source, retain leading 100 PCs/Q7. Logistic regression lambda=10. Full baseline B8Q trains on all standardized activations, not PCA subset. Error bars 95% CIs.

Key results: §4.1 baseline transfer: W6 high/good, C2R moderate, J9 poor. Target-trained classifiers within leading-100 source subspace separate all targets, so info is present but source-trained direction fails. Appendix AUROC/F3: B8Q C2R 0.706, W6 0.874, J9 0.606; target-trained 5-fold CV C2R 0.936, W6 0.950, J9 0.869.

§4.2 H2 greedy oracle: target-label-guided subset selection over 100 source PCs, source-trained logistic weights; upper bound, not unbiased OOD. Small subspaces nearly match target-trained probes, especially C2R/J9. Variance selection Y4 only matches H2 on W6, far behind C2R/J9. Appendix H2 improvement over B8Q: C2R 0.22, J9 0.23; H2 F3 C2R 0.929, J9 0.832. Mean H2 target-CV subset size C2R 15, W6 8, J9 14; full-target H2 selected indices: C2R 13, W6 7, J9 15. Internal issue: “Small H2 subset range 8–15” conflicts with full-target W6 k=7.

§4.3: T6 source-PCA ranking and M9 target-PCA ranking do not recover transferable subspace/basis better than B8Q; M9 good C2R, worse than H2 W6, below random J9. X4 standardized coefficient = abs probe coefficient * Q7 std dev on source-N4D-projected activations. Appendix D: H2–M9 claimed Jaccards C2R .182, W6 .077, J9 .167, but listed sets imply C2R 4/24=.167, W6 2/20=.100, J9 4/26=.154. T6 top indices: 7,8,11,12,4,5,2,3,6,27,22,21,1,41,18.

§4.4/4.5/App B/E: C7 LLM interpreter uses high-positive/high-negative source examples per bipolar Q7 direction, activation integers -10 to +10; GPT-5-mini (P2), OpenAI 2025 rates OOD-deception usefulness R5 1–10, warning against surface cues. Max observed R5 was 6; 2 scoring runs; L2 retains 19 directions reaching max in both runs; complement A7 has 81. H2 selections shared by >1 target: 5 directions (62,57,9,81,86), of which 3 max-rated (62,57,86). Top-5 T6 ratings: 7=3, 8=4, 11=3, 12=3, 4=6, so 1 of top 5 max-rated. L2 improves over B8Q/variance, especially C2R/J9; exceeds complement A7. Appendix L2 F3: C2R 0.881, J9 0.662; baseline-H2 gap recovered C2R 78%, J9 25%. Internal issue: §4.5 said W6 baseline lower than J9, contradicting W6 B8Q=0.874 vs J9=0.606.

§5 limitations: single model/source; W6 already-high baseline uninformative; J9 weakest/most OOD; C2R improvement more robust. Linear pipeline only; direction “encode” claims descriptive, not causal. Appendix C: lower-index Q7 align more strongly with SAE decoder features U9, measured by best-matching and mean top-10 alignment, using andyrdt/saes-llama-3.1-8b-instruct.

Full-representation probes can mix general behavioral features with dataset-specific surface cues, high ID accuracy but harming transfer; sparse directional subspaces may isolate more general behavioral structure. OOD probing = representation/subspace selection + classifier fitting to preserve intended behavioral feature and filter spurious correlations.

Terminology: N4D = PCA transformation; Q7 = principal components/directions, retaining leading 100. Setup: Model Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct (E6). Use layer 15 residual-stream activations, averaged over assistant-response tokens only. Datasets from Goldowsky-Dill et al. 2025: source Roleplaying (V8); targets Insider Trading Report (C2R), Insider Trading Confirm (W6), Sandbagging (J9). Labels GPT-4o: honest=0, ambiguous=-1, deceptive=1; ambiguous removed. Source activations standardized; same source stats used on targets. PCA/N4D retains leading 100 source PCs/Q7. Subset S projection before training/eval. Logistic regression lambda=10. Full baseline B8Q trains on all standardized activations, not PCA subset. 100 PCs for interpretability comparability, not claimed superior. Error bars 95% CIs.

Experiments: §4.1 baseline says W6 transfer reasonably good/high, C2R moderate, J9 poor; target-trained classification within retained source subspace separates every target, so info present but source-trained direction fails. Fig2: target F3 for source-trained full reps (blue), source-trained leading 100 Q7 (orange), target-trained leading 100 source Q7 (green, 5-fold CV).

§4.2: H2 greedy oracle shows small source-trained subspaces nearly match target-trained probes, especially C2R/J9. Variance selection Y4 only matches H2 on easy W6; far behind on C2R/J9. Search starts empty over 100 Q7 directions, fits source logistic regression for candidate subsets, adds direction maximizing target F3. Target 5-fold CV selection on non-held-out target folds, evaluate selected source-trained probe on held-out fold; stop if improvement <=0.001. Target labels guide subset selection, not probe weights; transfer upper bound not unbiased OOD.

§4.3: T6 source-PCA ranking and M9 target-PCA ranking do not recover transferable subspace/basis better than B8Q. T6 about B8Q; M9 good on C2R, worse than H2 on W6, below random on J9. Ranking uses X4 standardized coefficient = abs probe coefficient * corresponding Q7 std dev on source-N4D-projected activations. Both evaluated probes train source data on top-k ranked directions. H2 supplies stable set and k; numbers differ slightly from CV.

§4.4/4.5: C7 LLM interpreter sees 8 most/least activating source examples per leading source direction, writes pole/whole-direction descriptions, assigns OOD/generalization score R5; retain intersection of directions reaching observed max in both scoring runs. L2 = interp-selected PC probe; controls A7 complement and Y4 equal-dimensional top-variance subset. Claims L2 improves over B8Q on all targets and over variance control, widely C2R/J9; exceeds A7 everywhere. Recovery: C2R substantially closes baseline-H2 gap, J9 partially. Internal conflict already noted: §4.5 says W6 baseline transfer lower than J9, contradicting §4.1 and §5 where W6 baseline is high and J9 weakest.

§5 Limitations: Claims narrow: single model/source; W6 already-high baseline makes W6 uninformative. J9 weakest result and most OOD; modest improvement likely distribution shift; C2R improvement more robust. Pipeline fully linear: N4D projection plus logistic regression; nonlinear probes/readout locations open. Direction “encode” claims descriptive from extreme examples/C7 verbalizations, not causal; high-rated directions not ablated during inference.

Paper title: “Probe Generalization as Subspace Selection for OOD Deception Detection.” Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct deception detection. Source Roleplaying; targets Insider Trading Report, Confirm, Sandbagging. Labels honest=0, ambiguous=-1, deceptive=1 by GPT-4o; ambiguous removed. Layer 15 residual stream, assistant-response token activations averaged. Source activations standardized; same stats applied to targets. PCA on scaled source activations; retain top 100 PCs. Logistic regression λ=10. Baseline probes train on full standardized activations. Top 100 PCs chosen for interpretability/alignment with SAE decoder features, not because low-index PCs assumed to generalize.

Sec. 4.1: source-trained full transfer AUROC: Confirm 0.874, Report 0.706, Sandbagging 0.606. Target-trained probes within top-100 source-PC subspace using 5-fold CV: 0.936 / 0.950 / 0.869 across targets, likely Confirm/Report/Sandbagging. Conclusion: 100-PC subspace contains enough info; source probe direction does not generalize.

Sec. 4.2: greedy target-supervised subspace search adds top-100 source PCs improving target AUROC; source-trained logistic probe, 5-fold held-out target eval; stop if improvement ≤0.001. Average selected PCs: 15 Report, 8 Confirm, 14 Sandbagging. Upper bound/oracle because uses target labels. Greedy improves over full baseline by 0.22 Report and 0.23 Sandbagging, nearly target-trained. Variance-matched top-k control only matches greedy for Confirm; lags Report/Sandbagging.

Sec. 4.3: PC rankings by standardized coefficient = abs(probe coefficient) × SD of PC. Source-PCA ranks by source-trained weights; target-PCA by target-trained weights. k set by greedy on full target dataset: k=13 Report, 7 Confirm, 14 Sandbagging. Results Figure 4: source-PCA about full baseline; target-PCA strong on Report but worse than greedy on Confirm and below-random on Sandbagging. Target-separating PCs not necessarily source-weighted transferable PCs.

Sec. 4.4/App. B: GPT-5-mini interpreted PCs from 8 most/least activating Roleplaying examples, scored OOD deception usefulness 1–10. No PC >6; 6 max observed. Two runs; retain PCs scoring max in both = 19 PCs. Among 5 PCs in greedy selections for >1 target, 3/5 got max OOD score; only 1 of top 5 source-PCA PCs got max.

Sec. 4.5: 19 interp-selected PCs used without target data. Interp-selected probe beats baseline, top-19 variance control, remaining-81 ablation on all targets. Report: 0.881, closes 78% gap baseline 0.706 to greedy oracle 0.929. Confirm baseline 0.874 near ceiling. Sandbagging: 0.606 to 0.662, closes 25% gap to greedy 0.832.

Appendix C: lower PCs show stronger SAE decoder alignment: Spearman ρ=-0.857 best-matching feature, -0.917 mean top 10; SAE andyrdt/saes-llama-3.1-8b-instruct.

Appendix D: Table 2 lists selected PC sets for source weights, greedy, target separability. Internal errors found: stated Jaccard overlaps do not match listed sets; Sandbagging greedy list has 15 PCs, conflicting with earlier k=14 if same set.

Appendix E: Table 3 caption says PCs selected for likely transferability by LLM judge, but lists only five PCs with scores: PC62 6, PC57 6, PC9 3, PC81 3, PC86 6, with “Selected On” target pairs. This conflicts with earlier selection rule if these are interpretation-selected PCs, since retained PCs should score max 6 in both runs. Table 4 lists PC7 3, PC8 4, PC11 3, PC12 3, PC4 6 with interpretations.

Paper title: “Probe Generalization as Subspace Selection for OOD Deception Detection.” Authors Daniel Yoo and Adrians Skapars. Impact Statement: says goal is to advance ML and no societal consequences need highlighting.

Core claims: Linear probes can fail OOD; Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct deception probes trained on Roleplaying source and evaluated on Insider Trading Report, Insider Trading Confirm, Sandbagging. Conclusion frames OOD probing as representation/subspace selection. Full-representation probes may mix general behavioral features with dataset-specific cues; sparse PC subspaces may isolate more general structure. Small source-PC subsets nearly match target-trained probes; source-side or target-side separability alone cannot find them. PC interpretations can partially recover transferable subspace without target data. Text reports baseline-to-interp gap closure: 78% Report, 25% Sandbagging.

Setup: Four Goldowsky-Dill datasets; labels honest 0, ambiguous -1, deceptive 1 by GPT-4o; ambiguous removed. Counts incl ambiguous: Roleplaying 371 (-1/0/1=140/59/172); Insider Trading Report 473 (218/194/61); Confirm 151 (29/38/84); Sandbagging 1000 (379/375/246). Activations: layer 15 residual stream, assistant response token average. Source activations standardized; same stats for targets. PCA on scaled source activations, top 100 PCs. Logistic regression λ=10. Baseline full standardized activations.

Baseline 4.1: source-trained full target AUROCs: Confirm 0.874, Report 0.706, Sandbagging 0.606. Target-trained probes in top-100 source-PC subspace via 5-fold CV: 0.936/0.950/0.869, likely Confirm/Report/Sandbagging.

Greedy oracle 4.2: Select PCs among top 100 to maximize target AUROC, training weights on source subset; target labels used for subset choice. 5-fold CV over target for evaluation. Stop improvement ≤0.001. Avg subset sizes: Report 15, Confirm 8, Sandbagging 14. Greedy improves full baseline by about 0.22 Report and 0.23 Sandbagging, close to target-trained; variance top-k control matches only Confirm.

4.3: Tests whether greedy PCs are target-separating PCs or source-probe-heavy PCs. PC rankings by standardized coefficient abs(coef × PC std). Possible inconsistency: target-PCA ranking described as target-trained probe weights, then says both probes are trained on source data projected to selected PCs. k set by greedy on full target dataset, not CV: Report 13, Confirm 7, Sandbagging 14. Results: source-PCA transfers about like full baseline; target-PCA good on Report, worse than greedy on Confirm, below-random on Sandbagging.

Appendix D Table 2 PC sets: source probe weights: PC7,8,11,12,4,5,2,3,6,27,22,21,1,41,18. Greedy Report 13 PCs: 6,89,62,66,26,14,57,25,93,9,70,97,78. Greedy Confirm 7: 71,53,28,86,32,81,77. Greedy Sandbagging table lists 15 PCs: 37,62,54,41,46,9,57,44,51,43,19,48,86,81,33 (conflicts with earlier 14). Target separability rankings list 15 PCs per target. Appendix D Jaccards claimed: Report .182, Confirm .077, Sandbagging .167; these do not match listed full sets (computed .167, .100, .200 respectively).

4.4/Appendix E: LLM interprets PCs using 8 high/low source examples; judge gives OOD score 1–10. Appendix B prompt uses GPT-5-mini. No PC scored above 6; two runs; keep PCs scoring max both: 19 PCs. Of 5 PCs appearing in greedy selections for more than one target, 3/5 received max OOD score. Appendix E Table 3 lists these overlapping PCs/scores: PC62 Report+Sandbagging 6, PC57 Report+Sandbagging 6, PC9 Report+Sandbagging 3, PC81 Confirm+Sandbagging 3, PC86 Confirm+Sandbagging 6. Appendix E Table 4 lists source-probe PCs with scores: PC7 3, PC8 4, PC11 3, PC12 3, PC4 6.

4.5: 19 interp-selected PCs target-data-free probe. Report: 0.706 to ~0.881 vs greedy 0.929, closes 78%. Confirm baseline near ceiling. Sandbagging: 0.606 to 0.662/0.663 vs greedy 0.832, closes 25%.

Limitations: single model/source/layer 15; Confirm uninformative; Sandbagging modest; no causal validation. Earlier contradiction: despite all experiments using layer 15 and linear PCA+logistic pipeline, it claims findings hold for nonlinear probes and every residual-stream layer.

Appendix C: lower PCs have stronger decoder alignment to SAE features, best-matching and mean top-10, Spearman ρ=-0.857 and -0.917; SAE: andyrdt/saes-llama-3.1-8b-instruct.

Paper title: “Probe Generalization as Subspace Selection for OOD Deception Detection.” Core claim: source-probe-heavy directions encode source-specific surface features; transferable directions encode same contrast more abstractly/natural-language; OOD robustness largely determined by subspace/representation selection, not just classifier fitting. Sparse directional subspaces may isolate more general behavioral structure.

Setup: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct only. Layer 15 residual-stream activations, averaged over assistant-response tokens only. Source Roleplaying/V8; targets Insider Trading Report C2R, Insider Trading Confirm W6, Sandbagging J9. Labels GPT-4o honest=0, ambiguous=-1, deceptive=1; ambiguous removed. Source activations standardized; same stats for targets. PCA/N4D retains leading 100 PCs/Q7. Classifiers logistic regression lambda=10. Full baseline B8Q trains on all standardized activations, not PCA subset. Error bars 95% CIs.

Dataset counts incl. ambiguous: V8 371 = 140/-1, 59/0, 172/1. C2R 473 = 218/-1, 194/0, 61/1. W6 151 = 29/-1, 38/0, 84/1. J9 1000 = 379/-1, 375/0, 246/1.

Baseline/target-trained: B8Q F3 C2R .706, W6 .874, J9 .606. Target-trained in leading-100 source subspace 5-fold CV: C2R .936, W6 .950, J9 .869. W6 easy/high baseline; J9 poor/most OOD.

H2/oracle source-trained subspaces nearly match target-trained probes. H2 uses target labels to select source-PC subset but source logistic weights not target-trained; target 5-fold CV selection/eval; upper bound not unbiased OOD estimate. H2 improvement over B8Q: C2R .22, J9 .23; H2 F3 for recovery: C2R .929, J9 .832. Mean H2 subset size target CV: C2R 15, W6 8, J9 14; earlier full-target H2 k noted C2R 13, W6 7, J9 14, but Appendix D Table 2 lists H2 sizes C2R 13, W6 7, J9 15.

T6 source-side and M9 target-side rankings do not recover transferable subspace better than B8Q. T6 about as good as B8Q; M9 good on C2R, worse than H2 on W6, below random on J9. Rankings use X4=abs probe coefficient × PC std.

LLM judge C7 uses GPT-5-mini prompt to score direction OOD/general deception relevance R5. Appendix E: maximum observed R5 is 6; 2 scoring runs; 19 directions reached max in both runs and retained for L2; A7 uses 81 complement directions. L2 language-only interp-selected PC probe improves over B8Q on all targets; L2 F3 C2R .881, J9 .662; recovers baseline–H2 gap C2R 78%, J9 25%. Appendix E says 5 directions selected by H2 for more than one target; 3/5 are max-rated: indices 62, 57, 86 have R5=6, while 9 and 81 have R5=3. Max-rated among top T6 selections: 1 of top 5; table shows index 4 R5=6, indices 7/8/11/12 R5 3/4/3/3.

Decoder alignment Spearman rho earlier: best feature -0.857; mean top 10 -0.917. Appendix C says lower-index Q7 align more strongly with SAE decoder features U9, using andyrdt/saes-llama-3.1-8b-instruct.

Appendix D gives H2–M9 Jaccard D3 values C2R .182, W6 .077, J9 .167, but these do not match Table 2 sets: computed from printed indices C2R 4/24=.167, W6 2/20=.100, J9 4/26=.154. Table 2 sets: T6 source 15 indices; H2 C2R 13, W6 7, J9 15; M9 each 15.

Limitations: Claims narrow; single-model, single-source; W6 high baseline uninformative. Earlier limitation text stated pipeline fully linear N4D+logreg, but also claimed findings hold for nonlinear probes and every residual-stream layer—potential conflict with setup using only layer 15/logreg.

Paper title: “Probe Generalization as Subspace Selection for OOD Deception Detection.” Authors Daniel Yoo and Adrians Skapars. Work during 11th AI Safety Camp.

Setup: Linear probes for deception detection may fail OOD; projecting onto selected source-PCA PCs improves transfer. OOD probing framed as representation/subspace selection. Experiments: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, layer 15 residual stream, averaged over assistant response tokens; source dataset Roleplaying deception. Targets: Insider Trading Report, Insider Trading Confirm, Sandbagging. Ambiguous removed. Cross-domain/dataset, not cross-model-family.

Dataset counts (-1/0/1): Roleplaying 371=140/59/172; Report 473=218/194/61; Confirm 151=29/38/84; Sandbagging 1000=379/375/246. Standardize source activations and apply same stats to targets. PCA on scaled source; top 100 PCs retained. Logistic regression λ=10. Baseline probes use full standardized activations.

Results: Full source-trained target AUROCs: Confirm 0.874, Report 0.706, Sandbagging 0.606. Target-trained probes in top-100 source-PC subspace via 5-fold CV: 0.936/0.950/0.869 AUROC, so top-100 source-PC subspace contains target information.

Greedy oracle: Uses labeled target examples, oracle/upper bound. CV selects using non-held-out target folds, evaluates source-trained probe on held-out target fold. Stop if no AUROC gain >0.001. CV avg subset sizes: Report 15 PCs, Confirm 8, Sandbagging 14. Greedy improves full baseline by ~0.22 AUROC on Report and ~0.23 on Sandbagging; close to target-trained. Variance-matched top-k only matches greedy for Confirm. Figure 4/selection comparison used full target data for greedy, not per-fold CV: stable k Report 13, Confirm 7, Sandbagging 14; greedy oracle AUROCs Report 0.929, Sandbagging 0.832.

Section 4.3: Ranking by standardized coefficient = abs(probe coefficient × PC std), probes trained on source-PCA basis. Source-PCA ranking transfers about like full baseline; target-PCA ranking works on Report but worse than greedy on Confirm and below-random on Sandbagging. Conclusion: subset not findable by source-side or target-side separability alone.

Interpretability: GPT-5-mini interpreted each top-100 source PC using 8 most/8 least source examples and rated OOD deception usefulness 1–10. Scoring run twice; keep PCs with max score in both runs: 19 interp-selected PCs. 5 PCs appeared in greedy selections for >1 target; 3/5 got max OOD score. Only 1 of top 5 source-PCA PCs got max OOD score. 19-PC interp-selected probe outperforms full baseline on all 3 targets, variance-selected control, and interp-ablated PC probe. Report 0.706→0.881, closing 78% of gap to greedy 0.929. Sandbagging 0.606→0.662, closing 25% of gap to greedy 0.832. Confirm baseline 0.874 near ceiling/uninformative.

Appendix C: Lower PCs show stronger decoder alignment with SAE features using andyrdt/saes-llama-3.1-8b-instruct; Spearman ρ=-0.857 best feature, -0.917 mean top 10.

Appendix D Table 2 lists source probe weight PCs; greedy PCs for Report 13, Confirm 7, Sandbagging 15; target separability top-15 lists. Text reports greedy-vs-target-pca Jaccards 0.182/0.077/0.167, but these do not match table arithmetic.

Appendix E: Table 3 lists PCs PC62, PC57, PC9, PC81, PC86 as “selected for likely transferability” / “Selected On” target pairs, with OOD scores 6,6,3,3,6. This conflicts with earlier interpretability-selection rule if these are meant to be LLM-selected transferable PCs, since selected PCs should have max OOD score. Table 4 gives example PC OOD scores/interps: PC7=3, PC8=4, PC11=3, PC12=3, PC4=6.

Source activations standardized; targets use source stats. PCA/N4D on source; leading 100 PCs/Q7 retained. Logistic regression lambda=10. Fig 2/baselines: B8Q F3: C2R 0.706, W6 0.874, J9 0.606. Target-trained 5-fold CV inside leading-100 source subspace: C2R 0.936, W6 0.950, J9 0.869.

Paper title: “Probe Generalization as Subspace Selection for OOD Deception Detection.” Authors Daniel Yoo and Adrians Skapars.

Abstract claims:
- Linear probes can detect behaviors/concepts in LM activations but may fail OOD.
- Study: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct probes over 3 held-out deception detection datasets.

Introduction details:

final_notes:
Title: “Probe Generalization as Subspace Selection for OOD Deception Detection.” Model E6=Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct; layer 15 residual stream averaged over assistant tokens. Source V8=Roleplaying. Targets: C2R=Insider Trading Report, W6=Insider Trading Confirm, J9=Sandbagging. Labels GPT-4o K8 honest=0, ambiguous=-1, deceptive=1; ambiguous removed. Source activations standardized by source stats, same stats for targets. PCA/N4D on standardized source activations; retain leading 100 Q7. Subsets project before LR. Baseline B8Q trains on all standardized activations, not PCA subset. Error bars 95% CIs.

Baseline transfer: W6 good, C2R moderate, J9 poor. Target-trained probes in retained source subspace separate all targets. Fig 2: B8Q blue, leading-100 source probe orange, target-trained leading-100 green with 5-fold CV.

H2=greedy oracle/full-target selection over leading 100 source PCs; source LR trained on candidate subset, adds direction improving target F3; stop improvement <=0.001. In target 5-fold CV selection uses non-held-out target folds, evaluates source-trained probe on held-out fold; target labels guide selection, so upper bound. H2 small source-trained subspaces nearly match target-trained esp. C2R/J9. Y4 variance selection matched to H2 only works W6.

Rankings: T6=source-PCA probe ranking; M9=target-PCA probe ranking; X4 magnitude=abs coeff * Q7 std. Neither source nor target ranking recovers transferable subspace; T6 about B8Q; M9 good C2R, worse than H2 W6, below random J9.

Interpretability: C7 judge sees 8 most/least activating source examples per direction, writes descriptions and OOD/generalization R5. L2=interp-selected PC probe, intersection reaching observed max across two runs; noisy. Appendix E: maximum observed R5=6; two scoring runs; 19 directions reached max in both runs and retained for L2; complement A7 has 81 directions. H2 selections shared by >1 target: 5 directions, 3/5 max-rated. Shared H2 directions shown: 62,57,9 shared C2R+J9; 81,86 shared W6+J9; R5s 6,6,3,3,6. Top T6 selections table: 7,8,11,12,4 with R5s 3,4,3,3,6, so 1 of top 5 max-rated.

Appendix A labels: V8 371=140/59/172 (-1/0/1); C2R 473=218/194/61; W6 151=29/38/84; J9 1000=379/375/246. Numbers: B8Q F3 C2R .706, W6 .874, J9 .606; target-trained CV .936/.950/.869; H2 F3 C2R .929, J9 .832; L2 F3 C2R .881, J9 .662. Mean H2 subset target CV 15/8/14; full-target H2 k previously stated 13/7/14, but Table 2 H2 sets have C2R 13, W6 7, J9 15 (conflict for J9).

Appendix C: lower-index Q7 align more strongly with SAE decoder vectors; best-match Spearman rho -0.857, mean top-10 -0.917.

Appendix D Table 2 sets: T6 Source 15 indices; H2 C2R 13, W6 7, J9 15; M9 each 15. Reported H2–M9 Jaccards C2R .182, W6 .077, J9 .167 conflict with Table 2 calculations: .167, .100, .154 respectively.

Related Work (part 2): cites prior work claiming true/false, honesty, emotion, refusal, and assistant-like behavior have simple/linear activation directions, supporting mechanistic understanding/intervention while leaving stable concepts vs context-dependent correlations unresolved. Paper title: “Probe Generalization as Subspace Selection for OOD Deception Detection.” Abstract claims: directions heavily weighted by a source probe encode source-specific surface features; transferable directions encode the same contrast more abstractly and can be captured in natural language; probe OOD robustness is largely determined by subspace selection. Method framing: selection problem is to find dimensions permitting generalizing rather than spurious source-trained classification. Labels by GPT-4o (K8): honest=0, ambiguous=-1, deceptive=1; ambiguous removed. Source activations standardized to zero mean/unit variance; same source stats standardize targets. PCA transformation N4D retains leading 100 PCs/directions (Q7). For subset S, project before training/evaluation. Classifiers: logistic regression, lambda=10. U9/Bricken: lower PC indices more natural-language interpretable; 100 retained for interpretability/comparability, not claimed best.

Part 4 experiments/results and method labels: 4.1 baseline says W6 transfer reasonably good, C2R moderate, J9 poor. Target-trained probes within retained source subspace separate honest/deceptive on every target; info present. It also claims source probe favored directions causally increase E6 deception on target responses (note for later: intervention evidence should support this). Fig 2: target F3 for source-trained full repr B8Q (blue), source-trained leading 100 Q7 (orange), target-trained leading 100 source Q7 (green) with 5-fold CV.

4.2 H2=greedy oracle/full-target selection. Starting empty, considers leading 100 source Q7 directions; at each step trains source logistic regression on candidate subset and adds direction most improving target F3. Target 5-fold CV selects using non-held-out target folds and evaluates selected source-trained probe on held-out fold; stop if no improvement >0.001. Target labels guide subset selection, not weight fitting; upper bound, not unbiased OOD estimate. Result claim: small source-trained subspaces nearly match target-trained probes, esp. C2R/J9. Variance selection Y4 matched to H2 works only easy W6, far worse on C2R/J9; explained variance not predictive. Fig 3: B8Q blue, Y4 teal, H2 purple.

4.3 tests rankings. T6=source-PCA probe ranking; M9=target-PCA probe ranking; both use X4 magnitude = abs probe coefficient * corresponding Q7 std on source-N4D-projected activations, then source probes trained on top-k ranked directions. M9 good on C2R, worse than H2 on W6, below random on J9; target-class separation and transfer under source-fitted weights pick different directions. Fig 4: T6 red, M9 pink, H2 purple.

C7 LLM judge gets 8 most- and 8 least-activating source examples per leading source direction; writes positive/negative/whole-direction descriptions and OOD/generalization rating R5. Selection retains directions reaching observed maximum in both scoring runs; noisy. L2=interp-selected PC probe, retained intersection. Controls: A7=complement/interp-ablated PC probe; Y4=equal-dimensional top-k by variance. All trained as source probes. Result: L2 improves over B8Q on all targets and over Y4/A7; wide gains C2R/J9, little W6 headroom; C2R closes much baseline-H2 gap, J9 partial.

final_notes:
Paper title: “Probe Generalization as Subspace Selection for OOD Deception Detection.” Model: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct only, layer 15 residual stream; single source Roleplaying; targets Insider Trading Report, Insider Trading Confirm, Sandbagging. Labels honest=0, ambiguous=-1, deceptive=1; ambiguous removed. Counts incl ambiguous: Roleplaying 371 (140/-1, 59/0, 172/1); Report 473 (218/-1, 194/0, 61/1); Confirm 151 (29/-1, 38/0, 84/1); Sandbagging 1000 (379/-1, 375/0, 246/1). Activations: assistant-response token activations averaged; source standardization applied to targets. PCA on scaled source activations, top 100 PCs retained. Logistic regression probes lambda=10. Baseline full standardized activations unless subset experiments project to selected source PCs.

errors.evidence: The experiments described evaluate probe AUROC on fixed activations: “Probe weights are always fit on source data, but the choice of PC subsets is guided by performance on labeled examples from the target dataset,” and Figure 3 is “Probe AUROC across the three targets...”
