errors.claim: “A second script checks that every numeric token in this manuscript matches a value derived from the stored results.”
errors.evidence: Notes record an earlier inconsistency: “earlier notes said 15,840 pre-registered; Sec.6 says 18,480 pre-registered ... realised grid 6 objectives, 1,320 cells, 15,840 specs.”
errors.explanation: The manuscript has reported two different values for the pre-registered grid/spec count: 15,840 and 18,480. Both cannot be the same checked manuscript quantity, so the blanket claim that every numeric token matches stored results is contradicted by the paper’s own inconsistent reporting.

errors.claim: “Across factor-four binnings | 0.70 to 0.77”
errors.evidence: The factor-four threshold binnings listed are “all thresholds × 0.5” through “all thresholds × 2”, with F values 0.7448, 0.7435, 0.7394, 0.7289, 0.7314, 0.7308, and 0.7232.
errors.explanation: Those listed factor-four binnings range from 0.7232 to 0.7448, not 0.70 to 0.77. The 0.70 and 0.77 endpoints appear to come from other binning schemes, “equal thirds” and “deciles,” not the factor-four threshold binnings.

errors.claim: “A6N samples the full edge population with R=1,000 null multiverses; its degeneracy occurs above 1,000 edges.”
errors.evidence: The same section’s Table 7 shows A6N F = 0.0000 and A6N classes = 1 at size 1,000, as well as at 2,000, 5,000, and 10,000. The prose immediately below also says: “A6N collapses at and above 1,000 edges.”
errors.explanation: The degeneracy does not occur only above 1,000 edges; according to the table and later prose, it already occurs at 1,000 edges.

errors.claim: “Thus 2,692 of 7,561 specifications contribute no flips; instability lives entirely below 2,000 edges.”
errors.evidence: Table 7 shows discovered F = 0.5714 with 3 classes at size 2,000, n = 312. Discovery collapses only at 5,000 and 10,000, whose n values sum to 625 + 2,067 = 2,692.
errors.explanation: The 2,692 no-flip specifications are the 5,000- and 10,000-edge rows. But instability is not entirely below 2,000 edges, because the 2,000-edge row itself has nonzero instability and multiple classes.

errors.claim: “Every reported number traces to configuration, seed and environment fingerprint” and “Another checks every manuscript numeric token against stored-result derivations.”
errors.evidence: Earlier notes record numerical/textual inconsistencies: “factor-four binnings 0.70 to 0.77” misstates the threshold multiplier range, which was .7232-.7448; and the A6N description said it degenerates only above 1000, while Table 7 shows A6N zero at 1000+.
errors.explanation: The paper previously contained reported numeric/range claims that conflict with its own tables/results. That contradicts the blanket reproducibility claim that every manuscript numeric token is checked against stored-result derivations.

errors.claim: “Across factor-four binnings | 0.70 to 0.77”
errors.evidence: The factor-four threshold binnings in Table 1 appear to be the multiplicative thresholds from ×0.5 through ×2, whose F values run from 0.7232 to 0.7448. The 0.70 and 0.77 endpoints come from “equal thirds” = 0.7018 and “deciles” = 0.7719, not the factor-four binnings.

errors.claim: “Seven objectives, seven operators, four corruption distributions nested within the five operators reading them, four metrics, three thresholds, two prompt variants, five seeds: 1,540 discovery cells, 18,480 pre-registered specifications.”
errors.evidence: Earlier §4 formalism defined a specification as eight axes: “s=(o,a,d,m,τ,P,r,g): discovery objective, ablation operator, corruption distribution, evaluation metric, size threshold, prompt variant, seed, granularity.”

Paper title: “Explanation Multiplicity: Circuit-Level Interpretability / Evidence Does Not Survive Defensible Analytic Variation” by Ajay Pravin Mahale, dated 12 Aug 2026.

Core: EU AI Act documentation/explanation framing; mech interp useful only if second analyst using same system/tool would file compatible explanation. Authors argue current evidence fails filing standard, not interpretability as a field.

Methods/model/task: GPT-2 small on IOI. Edge attribution patching/integrated edge gradients, Miller et al. library; Conmy lineage; corruptions from Wang. Pre-reg grid: 18,480 specs / 1,540 cells, but one of seven documented/exported discovery objectives failed all 220 cells due runtime MSE/integral target bug; realised grid 6 objectives, 1,320 cells, 15,840 specs. Earlier conflict: “pre-registered specs=15,840.” Seed axis = prompt/eval variability, not nondeterminism. Spec tuple s=(o,a,d,m,τ,P,r,g), 8 axes despite earlier “7 analytic axes.”

Exclusions: Threshold admits no circuit for 8,279/15,840 specs (52.3%), leaving 7,561 claims. Kept/discarded: comprehensiveness 3,947/13; KL 1,467/2,493; logit difference 1,270/2,690; sufficiency 877/3,083. Surviving pool 52% comprehensiveness vs 25% by design.

Claim map φ deterministic/pre-registered/published code, not LLM. φ_overseer based on Annex IV 2(e)/3 and Art.14(4)(c): dominant layer band, size class, ranked segment. φ_affected based on Art.86(1), leads with input segment. Size bins committed calibration; Table 1 committed F=0.7316; no-size COARSE 0.5733. Error: text says six alternatives higher than committed, table shows four.

Main F/filability: F=0.7316, π*=0.4109; not filable for 0.95/0.90/0.80 modal share. Nine overseer-medium classes include early distributed 3107/.4109 and late sparse 2153/.2848. Layer shares early 47.9%, late 43.6%, middle 8.5%. All addressee/granularity variants fail α=.20.

Verification script recomputes headline quantities: 36 checks, 0 failures, F by three routes incl. brute-force pairwise. Claims every numeric token matches stored results and all tables emitted directly; this conflicts with earlier numeric inconsistencies. Test suite 343 tests.

Paper title: “Explanation Multiplicity: Circuit-Level Interpretability / Evidence Does Not Survive Defensible Analytic Variation” by Ajay Pravin Mahale, dated 12 Aug 2026.

Abstract key setup: EU AI Act high-risk systems require technical documentation explaining decisions. Mechanistic interpretability/circuit discovery framed as evidence source. Research question: whether evidence survives when two competent analysts use same system/tool but different defensible settings.

Methods/definitions to check later: pre-registered crossed grid of 7 analytic axes; every level taken from a published implementation. Each discovered circuit mapped through deterministic claim map to structured Annex IV statement. Model/task: GPT-2 small on indirect object identification (IOI). Total pre-registered specifications: 15,840; specifications producing a claim: 7,561. “Flip rate” is across specification pairs for derived statements; modal claim share reported.

Main abstract results: derived statement flips across 73.2% of specification pairs, 95% CI 0.725–0.738. Modal claim commands 41.1% of the space. Evidence fails a filability criterion at every tolerance a conformity assessment body would plausibly accept.

Robustness/ablation claims: Standardising the single most influential choice, the evaluation metric, leaves flip rate at 59.4%. Removing circuit size from the claim entirely and holding it fixed leaves 27.1%, 95% CI 0.255–0.286, still above pre-registered threshold.

Circuit comparison claims: circuits underlying claims are structurally near-disjoint, median pairwise Jaccard overlap 4%; functionally uncorrelated at Cohen’s kappa 0.015. Therefore instability is claimed not to be one mechanism described in different words.

Other abstract claims: filability criterion provided as standalone protocol. One of the seven documented discovery objectives does not execute at all on the library’s own canonical task. Scope limitation: one model and one task; whether conclusion holds at scale is untested.

errors.evidence: Earlier notes record numeric contradictions in the manuscript: “Earlier notes recorded ‘Total pre-registered specifications: 15,840,’ conflicting with §6’s 18,480 pre-registered/15,840 realised,” and “Text inconsistently says instability entirely below 2,000 though row 2,000 F=.5714.”
errors.explanation: If every numeric token in the manuscript matched derived stored results, the manuscript should not contain a numeric token giving the pre-registered specification total as 15,840 when §6 gives 18,480 pre-registered and 15,840 realised. The claim also sits uneasily with a textual numeric boundary claim contradicted by a reported row at 2,000.

grade.reason: The reviewer flagged the same sentence in item 3 but challenged a different contradiction (presence of flips at 2,000 edges) rather than the specific numeric mismatch (2,792 vs 2,692) shown by Table 7's counts.

errors.claim: “Across factor-four binnings | 0.70 to 0.77”
errors.evidence: The factor-four threshold binnings listed are “all thresholds × 0.5” through “all thresholds × 2”, with F values 0.7448, 0.7435, 0.7394, 0.7289, 0.7314, 0.7308, and 0.7232.
errors.explanation: Those listed factor-four binnings range from 0.7232 to 0.7448, not 0.70 to 0.77. The 0.70 and 0.77 endpoints appear to come from other binning schemes, “equal thirds” and “deciles,” not the factor-four threshold binnings.

errors.claim: “A6N samples the full edge population with R=1,000 null multiverses; its degeneracy occurs above 1,000 edges.”
errors.evidence: Table 7 shows A6N F = 0.0000 and A6N classes = 1 at size 1,000, and also at 2,000, 5,000, and 10,000. The following sentence also says: “A6N collapses at and above 1,000 edges.”
errors.explanation: The table and adjacent prose indicate A6N degeneracy begins at 1,000 edges, not above 1,000 edges.

errors.claim: “Thus 2,792 of 7,561 specifications contribute no flips”
errors.evidence: Table 7 says discovery collapses only at 5,000 and 10,000 edges, with n = 625 and n = 2,067 respectively; 625 + 2,067 = 2,692, not 2,792.
errors.explanation: The stated count of no-flip discovery specifications is off by 100 relative to the table.

errors.claim: “instability lives entirely below 2,000 edges.”
errors.evidence: Table 7 shows at size 2,000: Discovered F = 0.5714 and Classes = 3.
errors.explanation: Discovery instability is present at 2,000 edges, so it is not entirely below 2,000 edges.

errors.claim: “a 924-cell grid identical on every axis except three rather than five seed levels”
errors.location: this part, §9 Limitations, One model, one task
errors.evidence: Earlier notes: “Realised: 6 objectives, 1,320 discovery cells ...” and the current claim says the only grid change is seed levels from five to three.
errors.explanation: If the grid were identical except for reducing seed levels from 5 to 3, the cell count should scale from 1,320 to 792, not 924. final_notes:
Paper title: “Explanation Multiplicity: Circuit-Level Interpretability”; subtitle/claim: “Evidence Does Not Survive Defensible Analytic Variation.” Core claim: circuit-derived regulatory evidence fails Y3W across plausible tolerances; same model/tool yields incompatible statements under defensible settings. Applicability beyond one model/task untested; no scale claim.

Formalism/spec: s=(o,a,d,m,τ,P,r,g). Q7V graph: |E|=32,491; 144 attention heads + 12 MLPs = 156 components. Instability D=1-Jaccard. Jbar=mean Jaccard. Claim instability F=unbiased Gini-Simpson disagreement probability. Conditional Fwithin pair-weighted by groups. Claim map G7U/φ deterministic preregistered/published code, not LLM. Granularities E7R=coarse, K8Z=medium, V2H=fine.

Methods: GPT-2 small Q7V, IOI task Z4K. Realised: 6 objectives, 1,320 discovery/confirmatory cells, 15,840 specs after one objective failed; empty discarded 8,279; kept specs=7,561. Metric kept/discarded: T9V 3,947/13, H2W 1,467/2,493, N6C 1,270/2,690, U4J 877/3,083. Bootstrap B=10,000 over specs only.

Y3W protocol: for filed circuit-derived claim c, declare defensible analytic space S and deterministic φ; compute π*=max_c n_c/N over S and F; evidence passes Y3W at tolerance α iff π*≥1−α; report π*, F, discard rate per axis level, and within-group decomposition of every pooled statistic. Filing unable to state π* is asserted, not audited.

Earlier sensitivity/internal error: “factor-four binnings 0.70 to 0.77” actually mixes equal thirds/deciles; factor-four threshold multipliers are 0.7232–0.7448.

Registered results: Table 3: Jbar=0.1396 [0.1377,0.1418]; X4R F=0.7316 [0.7247,0.7380]; Q2F random null separated; Z8N functional gap=0.3344 [0.3297,0.3394]. Structural diagnostics: 7,561 specs, 3,218 distinct circuits, 28,580,580 pairs; median D=0.960; median shared-edge fraction 4%; median size 200. D9P K8Z counts: early distributed 3107, late sparse 2153, late moderate 657, late distributed 489, early sparse 477, middle moderate 283, middle sparse 269, middle distributed 90, early moderate 36. Table 5 all fail Y3W even at α=.20.

Part 9 results: Axis-standardization residual F: metric .5939 removes .1377; ablation .7014; objective .7018; threshold .7070; corruption .7092; prompt .7232; seed .7307. REML log10 size variance: ablation-corruption interaction 78.8%, residual 11.5%, ablation 4.4%, threshold 4.1%, metric 0.7%. Maximum pressure size-free fixed-size F=.2706 [0.2550,.2859]. Random baseline: pooled discovered F .7316 vs A6N .6774; fixed-size K8Z .2746 vs .4230; fixed-size E7R .2706 vs .3822. Functional diagnostics: pooled agreement .6028, functional instability .3972, smallest-circuit .4777, kappa .0146; pooled gap carried by 500–2000 edges.

Limitations/discussion: one model/task; M9B Pythia-160m second-model plan unrun, same task, claimed 924-cell grid with 3 not 5 seeds—internal error because 1320×3/5=792. Size is outcome not axis; threshold-selected size distorts F, null direction, gap sign; within-size decompositions reported. C4Y optimal ablation excluded, so F lower bound vs field. Discard rate high/uneven. Bootstrap invalid for one family with tiny conditioning groups; intervals replaced by point estimates/diagnostics. No single knob suffices; failed objective documented/exported but not canonical executable.

Reproducibility: public timestamped commit tag `prereg-p1-confirmatory`; one environment across all 1,320 cells; archive comparison recovered commit, 22/22 files identical; no GPU needed. Headline script asserts 36 checks, 0 failures, F via three routes including brute-force pairs. Manuscript numeric-token checker; tables emitted directly; suite has 343 tests.

Paper title: “Explanation Multiplicity: Circuit-Level Interpretability: Evidence Does Not Survive Defensible Analytic Variation” by Ajay Pravin Mahale, dated 12 Aug 2026.

Legal framing: EU AI Act high-risk providers must file technical documentation describing decision process; mech interp/circuit discovery framed as evidence. Annex IV 2(b), 2(e), Article 86(1). Source: consolidated text amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, CELEX 02024R1689-20260727.

Design/grid inconsistency: earlier said pre-registered crossed grid of seven analytic axes/every level, total 15,840 specs; formalism s=(o,a,d,m,τ,P,r,g) appears 8 choices incl granularity. Method later said seven objectives, seven ablations, four corruptions nested within five operators, four metrics, three thresholds, two prompts, five seeds = 1,540 discovery cells and 18,480 specs pre-registered; one objective fails, realised grid six objectives, 1,320 cells, 15,840 specs. Sec 9 says second-model replication is pre-registered but not run: 924-cell Pythia-160m grid, identical except seed axis has 3 not 5 levels; matches 1,540 prereg cells scaled by 3/5, not 1,320 realised cells.

Execution/exclusions: one discovery objective fails in all 220 cells due runtime error; not repaired. Threshold admits no circuit for 8,279/15,840 specs; 7,561 claims; discard rate 52.3%. Table 2 kept/discarded: comprehensiveness 3,947/13; KL 1,467/2,493; logit diff 1,270/2,690; sufficiency 877/3,083.

Circuit graph: |E|=32,491. Circuits touch 144 attention heads + 12 MLPs = 156 components; output receives from all 157 non-terminal sources.

Claim map φ deterministic, published code, not LLM. φ_overseer keyed by dominant layer band, size class, ranked input segment; φ_affected leads with input segment. Three granularities nested. Flip rate F = unbiased Gini–Simpson; modal share π*. Filability iff π* ≥ 1-α.

Main results: Table 3 P0 mean J=0.1396; H2 F=.7316 confirmed; H3 rejected because separated from random null; H4 F-(1-agreement)=.3344. 7,561 specs, 3,218 distinct circuits. Median Jaccard 4%; median circuit size 200. π*=.4109, not filable at tolerances .95/.90/.80. Overseer MEDIUM modal class early distributed 3107 (.4109), late sparse 2153 (.2848). Robustness contradiction: earlier text said standardising evaluation metric leaves F=49.4%, but Table 6 says residual F=0.5939. §10 says metric removes 0.1377 of 0.7316, consistent with .5939 residual but inconsistent with 49.4%. Table 6 residuals: metric .5939, ablation .7014, objective .7018, threshold .7070, corruption .7092, prompt .7232, seed .7307.

Size: circuit size is outcome of threshold, not axis; Sec 9 says it distorted F, null-comparison direction, and functional-gap sign. Size-held F: .2706 CI .2550-.2859 generally/coarse, and .2746 for medium. Reproducibility §11 claims prereg commit tag prereg-p1-confirmatory before sweep; every number traces to config/seed/environment; sweep ran single environment across all 1,320 cells; 22/22 files identical; analysis no GPU. Verification recomputes headlines: 36 checks, 0 failures; second script checks every numeric token; tables emitted directly; 343 tests. These broad claims conflict with the earlier documented numeric/grid inconsistencies.

Paper title: “Explanation Multiplicity: Circuit-Level Interpretability”; core claim: circuit-derived regulatory evidence fails Y3W across plausible tolerances; same model/tool yields incompatible statements under defensible settings. Scope limited: one model/one task; no scale claim. Limitations: unrun second-model Pythia-160m 924-cell plan and unrun second task.

Formalism: s=(o,a,d,m,τ,P,r,g). Q7V graph |E|=32,491; 144 heads + 12 MLPs = 156 components. Instability D=1-Jaccard; Jbar=mean Jaccard. Claim instability F=unbiased Gini-Simpson disagreement probability; Fwithin pair-weighted by groups. Claim map φ deterministic preregistered/published code, not LLM. D9P overseer: layer band, size class, ranked segment. L3X affected: leads with input segment. Granularities E7R coarse, K8Z medium, V2H fine.

Methods: GPT-2 small Q7V, IOI task Z4K. Designed 1,540 discovery cells/18,480 specs; one objective failed 220 cells, no repair. Realised 6 objectives, 1,320 cells, 15,840 specs. Empty circuits discarded 8,279 (52.3%); kept 7,561. Kept/discarded: T9V 3,947/13, H2W 1,467/2,493, N6C 1,270/2,690, U4J 877/3,083. Bootstrap B=10,000 over specs only; invalid for one family due to tiny conditioning groups 2–5 specs, intervals replaced by point estimates/diagnostics.

Y3W: for filed claim c, declare S and deterministic φ; compute π*=max n_c/N and F. Pass iff π*≥1−α. Must report π*, F, discard rate per axis level, within-group decomposition of every pooled statistic.

Earlier sensitivity: D9P K8Z observed F=.7316; ceiling .8889. Threshold multiplier Fs: ×0.5 .7448, ×0.8 .7435, ×0.9 .7394, ×1.1 .7289, ×1.25 .7314, ×1.5 .7308, ×2 .7232; equal thirds .7018; deciles .7719; no size/D9P E7R .5733. Internal error: paper called “factor-four binnings 0.70 to 0.77,” but factor-four multipliers are .7232–.7448.

Registered outcomes Table 3: J6D Jbar=.1396 CI [.1377,.1418], premise holds; X4R F=.7316 [.7247,.7380], confirmed; Q2F random null separated, rejected; Z8N functional gap=.3344 [.3297,.3394], supported. Structural: 7,561 specs, 3,218 circuits, 28,580,580 pairs; median D=.960; median shared-edge 4%; 1% pairs J>0.8; median size 200.

D9P K8Z counts: early distributed 3107, late sparse 2153, late moderate 657, late distributed 489, early sparse 477, middle moderate 283, middle sparse 269, middle distributed 90, early moderate 36. Table 5 all fail Y3W α=.20: L3X E7R F=.3950 π*=.7291; L3X K8Z .6597/.4875; L3X V2H .6744/.4786; D9P E7R .5733/.4788; D9P K8Z .7316/.4109; D9P V2H .7681/.4109.

Axis-standardized residual F: metric .5939, ablation .7014, objective .7018, threshold .7070, corruption .7092, prompt .7232, seed .7307; no single knob suffices. REML variance dominated by ablation-corruption 78.8%, residual 11.5%. Metric-standardised disagreement 49.4%.

Size is outcome not axis; threshold-selected size distorts F, null-comparison direction, functional-gap sign. Size conditioning reduces instability most; max pressure size-free/fixed-size dominant-layer F=.2706 CI .2550–.2859. Random baseline: pooled discovered .7316 vs A6N .6774; fixed size K8Z .2746 vs .4230; fixed size E7R .2706 vs .3822. Discussion: complete metric standardisation exceeds conformity procedure; one-axis standardisation insufficient. Failed objective documented/exported but cannot execute on library canonical task; discard rate tooling maturity issue. Reproducibility claims: public commit `prereg-p1-confirmatory`; one environment across 1,320 cells; 22/22 archive files identical; no GPU needed; one script asserts 36 headline checks, 0 failures, F through three routes; another checks every manuscript numeric token; tables emitted directly; 343 tests. This numeric-token claim conflicts with earlier erroneous “factor-four binnings 0.70 to 0.77.”

final_notes:
Paper title: “Explanation Multiplicity: Circuit-Level Interpretability / Evidence Does Not Survive Defensible Analytic Variation” by Ajay Pravin Mahale, dated 12 Aug 2026. Core: EU AI Act documentation/explanation requirements; circuit discovery as evidence source. Standard: second analyst using same system/tool should file compatible statement. Authors do not propose better circuit discovery or say interpretability worthless; argue current evidence fails filing standard. Discussion says evidentiary weight should be measured, not assumed.

Methods/definitions: Earlier text says pre-registered crossed multiverse over 7 analytic axes, but formal tuple s=(o,a,d,m,τ,P,r,g) has 8 axes incl granularity. φ deterministically maps discovered circuits to Annex IV claims; pre-registered code, not LLM. Model/task: GPT-2 small on IOI. §6 grid: 7 objectives, 7 ablations, 4 corruptions nested within 5 operators, 4 metrics, 3 thresholds, 2 prompts, 5 seeds = 1,540 discovery cells and 18,480 specs pre-registered. One objective fails: 220 cells runtime error; realised grid = 6 objectives, 1,320 cells, 15,840 specs. Earlier inconsistency: one part called “Total pre-registered specifications: 15,840,” conflicting with §6’s 18,480 pre-registered / 15,840 realised. Surviving pool: 7,561 specs producing claims. Seed selects prompt/eval-set variability, not nondeterminism. Four metrics total. Table 2 discard: comprehensiveness 3947/13/.003; KL 1467/2493/.630; logit diff 1270/2690/.679; sufficiency 877/3083/.779. Total discarded 8,279/15,840=52.3%; surviving pool 52% comprehensiveness vs 25% by design. No p-values; bootstrap B=10,000.

Results: Table 1 committed bin F=.7316; alternatives .7018–.7719; no-size-term COARSE F=.5733. |E|=32,491; 156 components. D=1−Jaccard; F=unbiased Gini–Simpson. Filable iff π*≥1−α. H2 F=.7316 [.7247,.7380] confirmed; H3 random null rejected/separated; H4 pooled gap .3344 supported. 7,561 specs; 3,218 circuits; median D=.960; only 1% pairs J>.8. Table 4 layer shares: early 47.9%, late 43.6%, middle 8.5%; top class early distributed 3107/.4109. All Table 5 addressee/granularity variants fail α=.20; overseer coarse F=.5733 π=.4788; medium F=.7316 π=.4109.

Axis/size analyses: Table 6 residual F after standardising: metric .5939 removes .1377 (discussion calls metric biggest lever); ablation .7014; objective .7018; threshold .7070; corruption .7092; prompt .7232; seed .7307. REML size variance: ablation-corruption interaction 78.8%, residual 11.5%, ablation 4.4%, threshold 4.1%, metric .7%; metric largest claim-variance driver. Maximum pressure dominant layer band + size fixed F=.2706. Random null pooled: discovered .7316 vs null .6774; size-held reverses: medium discovered .2746 vs null .4230; coarse .2706 vs .3822. H4 gap fails size-fixed: fails .10 threshold at 6/10 sizes, negative at 5; pooled H4 carried by 500–2,000 edge band. Prior inconsistency: prose said instability lives entirely below 2,000 despite discovered F=.5714 at 2,000; prose says null degenerate above 1,000 though table/caption says at and above 1,000. Functional agreement .6028, instability .3972, gap to claim flip .3344; κ=.0146; κ .016–.047 by size while raw agreement .52–.92 and accuracy .51–.95.

Limitations: one model/task; Pythia-160m replication pre-registered not run (924-cell, same task, seed 3 levels); second task designed not run. Circuit size outcome/threshold-selected; distorts F/null/H4; fixing size drops F .7316→.2746. Multiverse limited to implemented library; optimal ablation not included, measured F lower bound vs full defensible field. Discard high/uneven. Bootstrap invalid for one family with groups of 2–5 specs; point estimates diagnostic only.

Reproducibility: preregistration timestamped commit tagged prereg-p1-confirmatory before sweep. Current part claims every reported number traces to config/seed/environment; confirmatory sweep single environment across all 1,540 cells, archive-verified, code recovered by content-addressed comparison, 22/22 files identical. Analysis layer no GPU. Verification recomputes headline quantities: 36 checks, 0 failures; F derived three ways including brute-force pairwise. Second script checks numeric tokens against stored results; tables emitted directly; test suite 343 tests.

grade.reason: Report 2 flags the 1,540-cell count versus the realised 1,320-cell grid after exclusion, which identifies the same contradiction as the planted claim.

errors.claim: “Across factor-four binnings | 0.70 to 0.77”
errors.evidence: The factor-four threshold binnings listed are “all thresholds × 0.5” through “all thresholds × 2”, with F values 0.7448, 0.7435, 0.7394, 0.7289, 0.7314, 0.7308, and 0.7232.
errors.explanation: Those listed factor-four binnings range from 0.7232 to 0.7448, not 0.70 to 0.77. The 0.70 and 0.77 endpoints appear to come from other binning schemes, “equal thirds” and “deciles,” not the factor-four threshold binnings.

errors.claim: “A6N samples the full edge population with R=1,000 null multiverses; its degeneracy occurs above 1,000 edges.”
errors.evidence: The same section’s Table 7 shows A6N F = 0.0000 and A6N classes = 1 at size 1,000, as well as at 2,000, 5,000, and 10,000. The prose immediately below also says: “A6N collapses at and above 1,000 edges.”
errors.explanation: The degeneracy does not occur only above 1,000 edges; according to the table and later prose, it already occurs at 1,000 edges.

errors.claim: “Thus 2,692 of 7,561 specifications contribute no flips; instability lives entirely below 2,000 edges.”
errors.evidence: Table 7 shows discovered F = 0.5714 with 3 classes at size 2,000, n = 312. Discovery collapses only at 5,000 and 10,000, whose n values sum to 625 + 2,067 = 2,692.
errors.explanation: The 2,692 no-flip specifications are the 5,000- and 10,000-edge rows. But instability is not entirely below 2,000 edges, because the 2,000-edge row itself has nonzero instability and multiple classes.

errors.claim: “Another checks every manuscript numeric token against stored-result derivations.”
errors.evidence: Notes record earlier internal numeric misstatements: “factor-four binnings 0.70 to 0.77” misstates the multiplier range, which was .7232–.7448; and claims about A6N/size rows conflicted with Table 7, where A6N degenerates at 1000+ and discovered instability is nonzero at 2000 (.5714).
errors.explanation: If every manuscript numeric token were checked against stored-result derivations, these earlier numeric-text claims should not disagree with the paper’s own reported tables/results. The existence of those internal numeric conflicts contradicts the blanket reproducibility claim.

Paper title: “Explanation Multiplicity: Circuit-Level Interpretability”; claim: circuit-derived regulatory evidence fails Y3W across defensible analytic variation; same model/tool gives incompatible statements. No broader scale claim.

Formalism: spec s=(o,a,d,m,τ,P,r,g). Q7V graph |E|=32,491; 144 attention heads + 12 MLPs = 156 components. Instability D=1-Jaccard; Jbar=mean Jaccard. Claim instability F=unbiased Gini-Simpson disagreement probability; conditional Fwithin pair-weighted by groups. Claim map deterministic preregistered, not LLM. D9P overseer: layer band, size class, ranked segment. L3X affected: leads with input segment. Granularities: E7R coarse, K8Z medium, V2H fine.

Methods: GPT-2 small Q7V, IOI task Z4K. Original grid 1,540 discovery/confirmatory cells, 18,480 specs; one objective failed 220 cells, no repair. Realised 6 objectives, 1,320 cells, 15,840 specs. Empty circuits discarded: 8,279; kept specs=7,561. Metric kept/discarded: T9V 3,947/13, H2W 1,467/2,493, N6C 1,270/2,690, U4J 877/3,083. Bootstrap B=10,000 over specs only.

Sensitivity: D9P K8Z observed F=.7316; threshold multiplier range .7232-.7448; equal thirds .7018; deciles .7719; no size/D9P E7R .5733. Earlier internal error: “factor-four binnings 0.70 to 0.77” misstates multiplier range.

Results: registered outcomes fixed 6 Aug 2026. Table 3: Jbar=.1396, X4R F=.7316, Q2F random null separated, Z8N functional gap=.3344. Structural: 7,561 specs, 3,218 distinct circuits, 28,580,580 pairs; D quantiles 1%=.196, 25%=.788, median=.960, 75%=.998; median shared edge fraction 4%; 1% pairs Jaccard>.8; median size 200; random median-size overlap .0031; observed/chance ~45x.

D9P K8Z counts: early distributed 3107, late sparse 2153, late moderate 657, late distributed 489, early sparse 477, middle moderate 283, middle sparse 269, middle distributed 90, early moderate 36. Aggregated early/late/middle=47.9/43.6/8.5. Table 5 all fail Y3W at α=.20: L3X E7R .3950 π*=.7291; L3X K8Z .6597/.4875; L3X V2H .6744/.4786; D9P E7R .5733/.4788; D9P K8Z .7316/.4109; D9P V2H .7681/.4109.

Axis standardised residual F: metric .5939 removes .1377; ablation .7014; discovery objective .7018; threshold .7070; corruption .7092; prompt .7232; seed .7307. REML size variance: ablation-corruption 78.8%, residual 11.5%, ablation 4.4%, threshold 4.1%, metric .7%. Size-free fixed-size dominant-layer F=.2706, described as 27%.

Random baseline: pooled discovered F .7316 vs A6N .6774; fixed-size K8Z discovered .2746 vs A6N .4230; fixed-size E7R discovered .2706 vs A6N .3822. A6N R=1,000. Table 7 rows include discovered nonzero at 2000 (.5714) and A6N zero at 1000+. Earlier errors: A6N degenerates at, not only above, 1000; instability not entirely below 2000 because 2000 row nonzero.

Functional diagnostic: pooled agreement .6028; functional instability .3972; smallest-circuit .4777; kappa .0146; raw agreement 60%; kappa every size .016-.047; raw agreement .52-.92; accuracy .51-.95; 6/10 sizes fail gap threshold; 5 negative gaps; pooled gap carried by 500–2000 edges.

§8 Y3W: file claim c, defensible analytic space S and deterministic published claim map φ; π*=max_c n_c/N and F; pass α iff π*≥1−α; report π*, F, discard rate per axis level, and within-group decomposition of every pooled statistic.

§9 limitations: one model/task; planned M9B/Pythia-160m unrun; circuit size outcome not axis; threshold-selected size distorts F, null direction, functional-gap sign; size conditioning reduces instability more than registered-axis standardisation. Multiverse narrower; C4Y optimal ablation excluded, so F lower bound. Discard high/uneven. Bootstrap invalid for small conditioning groups; intervals replaced by points/diagnostics.

§10: standardising one axis insufficient; failed objective documented/exported but cannot execute on canonical task; discard rate indicates tooling maturity. Regulator takeaway: weight evidence measured cheaply.

§11 reproducibility: commit tag prereg-p1-confirmatory; archive says one environment across all 1,540 cells, 22/22 files identical, no GPU. Script asserts 36 headline checks, 0 failures, F via 3 routes. Claims every numeric token checked; this conflicts with earlier internal numeric inconsistencies. Suite 343 tests.

Paper title: “Explanation Multiplicity: Circuit-Level Interpretability”; thesis: circuit-derived regulatory evidence fails Y3W across defensible analytic variation; same model/tool yields incompatible circuit-level claims, not a broader scale claim.

Formalism: spec s=(o,a,d,m,τ,P,r,g). Q7V graph |E|=32,491; 144 attention heads + 12 MLPs = 156 components. Instability D=1-Jaccard; Jbar=mean Jaccard. Claim instability F=unbiased Gini-Simpson disagreement probability; conditional Fwithin pair-weighted by groups. Deterministic preregistered claim map (not LLM). D9P overseer: layer band, size class, ranked segment. L3X affected: leads with input segment. Granularities: E7R coarse, K8Z medium, V2H fine.

Methods: GPT-2 small Q7V, IOI task Z4K. Realised 6 objectives, 1,320 confirmatory cells, 15,840 specs. Empty circuits discarded: 8,279; kept specs=7,561. Metric kept/discarded: T9V 3,947/13, H2W 1,467/2,493, N6C 1,270/2,690, U4J 877/3,083. Bootstrap B=10,000 over specs only.

Key results: D9P K8Z 9 classes, ceiling F≤0.8889, observed F=.7316 =82.3% ceiling. Threshold multiplier F .7448 to .7232; equal thirds .7018; deciles .7719; no size/D9P E7R .5733. Error noted: “factor-four binnings 0.70 to 0.77” misstates multiplier range. Table 3: Jbar=.1396 [.1377,.1418], premise holds; X4R F=.7316 [.7247,.7380], confirmed; Q2F random null separated, rejected; Z8N functional gap=.3344 [.3297,.3394], supported. Structural: 7,561 specs, 3,218 distinct circuits, 28,580,580 pairs; median Jaccard .040 (D median .960); median size 200; observed/chance ~45x.

D9P K8Z counts: early distributed 3107, late sparse 2153, late moderate 657, late distributed 489, early sparse 477, middle moderate 283, middle sparse 269, middle distributed 90, early moderate 36. Table 5 all fail Y3W at α=.20: L3X E7R F=.3950 π*=.7291; L3X K8Z .6597/.4875; L3X V2H .6744/.4786; D9P E7R .5733/.4788; D9P K8Z .7316/.4109; D9P V2H .7681/.4109. Error noted: §8 says E7R D9P more stable than E7R L3X, but D9P has higher F/lower π*.

Axis sensitivity: metric standardisation lowers F most but only to .5939 (removes .1377); ablation .7014; discovery objective .7018; threshold .7070; corruption .7092; prompt .7232; seed .7307. REML size variance: ablation-corruption 78.8%, residual 11.5%, ablation 4.4%, threshold 4.1%, metric .7%. Fixed-size dominant-layer F=.2706. Random baseline: pooled discovered F .7316 vs A6N .6774; fixed-size K8Z discovered .2746 vs A6N .4230; fixed-size E7R discovered .2706 vs A6N .3822. Errors noted: A6N degenerates at, not only above, 1000; instability not entirely below 2000 because 2000 row nonzero.

Functional diagnostic: pooled agreement .6028; functional instability .3972; smallest-circuit .4777; kappa .0146; pooled gap carried by 500–2000 edges.

Y3W protocol: declare axes/levels; deterministic published φ, not LLM; compute π*=max n_c/N and F; pass α iff π*≥1−α; report π*, F, discard rate by axis level, and within-group decomposition.

Limitations: one model/task; size outcome not axis; threshold-selected size distorts F, null comparison direction, functional-gap sign; conditioning on size reduces instability more than any registered axis; every pooled statistic has within-size decomposition. C4Y optimal ablation not in instrument space, so measured F lower bound vs full defensible literature. High uneven discard rate not adjusted. Bootstrap invalid for one family: tiny conditioning groups retain dominating self-pairs; intervals replaced by point estimates/diagnostics. Error: M9B says 924-cell grid identical except 3 not 5 seed levels, but 1,320 cells implies 792 if only seed levels changed.

Discussion: metric standardisation exceeds plausible conformity demand but still insufficient; interpretability evidence not worthless, evidentiary weight should be measured cheaply relative to sweep.

Reproducibility: public commit tagged prereg-p1-confirmatory; one environment across all 1,320 confirmatory cells; archive comparison recovers commit, 22/22 files identical. One script asserts 36 headline checks, 0 failures, F via three routes including brute-force pairs. Numeric-token checker compares manuscript tokens to stored derivations; tables emitted directly; suite has 343 tests.

Paper title: “Explanation Multipity: Circuit-Level Interpretability / Evidence Does Not Survive Defensible Analytic Variation” by Ajay Pravin Mahale, dated 12 Aug 2026.

Core framing: EU AI Act high-risk systems require technical documentation/explanations: Annex IV point 2(b) “general logic” and 2(e) interpretation measures; Art. 86(1) right to clear/meaningful explanations. Circuit discovery framed as evidence source. Filing valuable only if second analyst using same system/tool would file compatible statement. Authors do not propose better circuit discovery or say interpretability worthless; argue current evidence does not meet filing standard. Empirical scope: GPT-2 small on IOI; limitation says one model/one task, larger models could change F. Planned but not run: Pythia-160m replication, 924-cell grid, same task, identical axes except seed has 3 not 5 levels; second task designed/not run.

Methods/definitions: Earlier parts said pre-registered crossed multiverse/grid over 7 analytic axes, but formal tuple s=(o,a,d,m,τ,P,r,g) has 8 axes incl. granularity (possible inconsistency). φ maps circuit deterministically to structured Annex IV claim; pre-registered code, not LLM-generated. §6 grid: 7 objectives, 7 ablations, 4 corruptions nested within 5 relevant operators, 4 metrics, 3 thresholds, 2 prompt variants, 5 seeds = 1,540 discovery cells and 18,480 specs pre-registered. One objective fails: all 220 cells runtime error; realised grid = 6 objectives, 1,320 cells, 15,840 specs. Discussion: one of seven documented/publicly exported discovery objectives does not run on library’s canonical task; reported as discard/tool maturity observation, not headline. Internal error: a prior “Total pre-registered specifications: 15,840” conflicts with §6’s 18,480 pre-registered / 15,840 realised, and §11 claim that every numeric token matches stored results. Surviving pool: 7,561 specs producing claims; discard rate 8,279/15,840=52.3%, high/uneven and metric imbalanced. Seed selects prompt/eval-set variability, not nondeterminism.

Claim map §5: two addressees, three granularities. Size bins from calibration rule. Table 1 committed bin F=.7316; alternatives .7018–.7719; no size term COARSE F=.5733.

Formalism/results: |E|=32,491; circuits touch 144 attention heads + 12 MLPs =156 components. D=1−Jaccard; F=unbiased Gini–Simpson. Filable iff π*≥1−α. H2 F=.7316 [.7247,.7380] confirmed; H3 random null rejected/separated; H4 gap .3344 supported pooled. 7,561 specs; 3,218 circuits; all-pairs 28,580,580. Pairwise median D=.960; only 1% pairs J>.8. Table 4 nine overseer-medium classes. All Table 5 variants fail α=.20; overseer coarse F=.5733 π=.4788; medium F=.7316 π=.4109.

Metric standardisation removes most F (.1377 of .7316); seed almost none (.0009). REML structural size variance: ablation-corruption 78.8%, residual 11.5%, ablation 4.4%, threshold 4.1%, metric 0.7%; metric largest driver of claim variance. Circuit size is outcome chosen by threshold, not axis; limitation says it distorts F, null comparison direction, functional-gap sign. Fixing size drops F .7316→.2746; max pressure layer+size fixed F=.2706. Random null pooled discovered .7316 vs null .6774; size-held reverses: medium discovered .2746 vs null .4230; coarse .2706 vs .3822. H4 gap fails size-held: fails 0.10 at 6/10 sizes and negative at 5; pooled carried by 500–2,000 edge band. Prior inconsistencies: prose says instability entirely below 2,000 despite discovered F=.5714 at 2,000; prose says null degenerate above 1,000 though table/caption says at and above 1,000. Functional agreement .6028, instability .3972, gap to claim flip .3344; κ=.0146.

§8 protocol: declare S and levels; deterministic φ; compute π*, F; filable at α iff π*≥1−α; report π*, F, discard rate, decomposition. §8 overclaims protocol “establishes all high-risk AI systems fail filability,” conflicting with empirical scope. §11: prereg commit prereg-p1-confirmatory before sweep; single environment across 1,320 cells; 36 checks 0 failures; 343 tests.

Paper title: “Explanation Multiplicity: Circuit-Level Interpretability / Evidence Does Not Survive Defensible Analytic Variation” by Ajay Pravin Mahale, dated 12 Aug 2026.

Abstract key setup: EU AI Act high-risk systems require technical documentation explaining decisions. Mechanistic interpretability/circuit discovery framed as evidence source. Research question: whether evidence survives when two competent analysts use same system/tool but different defensible settings.

Methods/definitions to check later: pre-registered crossed grid of 7 analytic axes; every level taken from a published implementation. Each discovered circuit mapped through deterministic claim map to structured Annex IV statement. Model/task: GPT-2 small on indirect object identification (IOI). Main abstract results: derived statement flips across 73.2% of specification pairs, 95% CI 0.725–0.738. Modal claim commands 41.1% of the space. Evidence fails a filability criterion at every tolerance a conformity assessment body would plausibly accept.

Robustness/ablation claims: Standardising the single most influential choice, the evaluation metric, leaves flip rate at 59.4%. Removing circuit size from the claim entirely and holding it fixed leaves 27.1%, 95% CI 0.255–0.286, still above pre-registered threshold.

Circuit comparison claims: circuits underlying claims are structurally near-disjoint, median pairwise Jaccard overlap 4%; functionally uncorrelated at Cohen’s kappa 0.015. Therefore instability is claimed not to be one mechanism described in different words.

Other abstract claims: filability criterion provided as standalone protocol. One of the seven documented discovery objectives does not execute at all on the library’s own canonical task. Scope limitation: one model and one task; whether conclusion holds at scale is untested.

Mechanistic interpretability/circuit discovery framed as possible evidence source. Audit/filing valuable only if a second analyst using same system/tool would file something compatible. Authors do not propose better circuit discovery or argue interpretability is worthless; argue current evidence does not meet filing standard.

Methods/definitions: pre-registered crossed multiverse/grid over 7 analytic axes of circuit discovery; every level drawn from a published implementation. Same system/tool but different defensible settings. Each discovered circuit deterministically mapped to structured Annex IV statement/claim. Model/task: GPT-2 small on indirect object identification (IOI). Total pre-registered specifications: 15,840; specifications producing a claim: 7,561. “Flip rate” is across specification pairs for derived statements; modal claim share reported. Filability criterion: π* ≥ 1 − α for conformity procedure. Seed axis: seed selects which prompts are sampled, i.e. evaluation-set variability rather than nondeterminism. Four evaluation metrics total, including sufficiency and comprehensiveness; discard rate reported per metric rather than silently pooled.

Removing circuit size from claim entirely and holding it fixed leaves 27.1%, 95% CI 0.255–0.286, above threshold. Part 3 similarly says at fixed circuit size discovered circuits are more stable than a size-matched random null, 0.2746 vs 0.4230, so they carry information. Introduction claims instability survives “most aggressive controls available”: standardising any single axis, removing circuit size from claim, and holding size fixed. Need check support for “any single axis.”

Functional instability reported in Part 3: 0.3972 pooled and 0.4777 at smallest circuits. Authors deny that filings differ where mechanisms do not, or that discovery samples one mechanism and dresses it differently. Related work says phantom specialisation/equivalent subgraphs strongest objection; Section 7.6 allegedly uses functional measurement and finds circuits are not functionally interchangeable.

Other claims: One of seven documented discovery objectives does not execute at all on the library’s own canonical task. Scope limitation repeated: one model and one task; no claim about scale. Introduction adds methodological multiverse result: when specifications select objects of different sizes, pooled statistics can invert; they show three such inversions.

[8] released library/tooling as stress test by tooling’s own definitions; variance-as-estimation by Méloux et al. [7] treated as companion; auditability motivation from Lan et al. [4], Sharkey et al. [10], Mueller et al. [9]; multiverse/specification-curve methods from Steegen/Simonsohn/Simmons; Hsia et al. [3] show sufficiency/comprehensiveness can be inflated without changing predictions/explanations.

Paper title: “Explanation Multiplicity: Circuit-Level Interpretability”; supported scope: circuit-derived regulatory evidence fails Y3W across defensible analytic variation for one GPT-2 small/IOI circuit setup; same model/tool gives incompatible statements. No broader scale claim supported earlier. §8 nevertheless states protocol establishes all high-risk AI systems fail Y3W—flagged as overbroad internal contradiction.

Formalism: spec s=(o,a,d,m,τ,P,r,g). Q7V graph |E|=32,491; 144 attention heads + 12 MLPs = 156 components. Instability D=1-Jaccard; Jbar=mean Jaccard. F=unbiased Gini-Simpson disagreement probability; Fwithin pair-weighted by groups. Claim map deterministic preregistered, not LLM. D9P overseer: layer band, size class, ranked segment. L3X affected: leads with input segment. Granularities: E7R coarse, K8Z medium, V2H fine.

Methods: GPT-2 small Q7V, IOI task Z4K. Original grid 1,540 discovery cells/18,480 specs; one objective failed 220 cells, no repair. Realised 6 objectives, 1,320 cells, 15,840 specs. Empty circuits discarded: 8,279; kept specs=7,561. Metric kept/discarded: T9V 3,947/13, H2W 1,467/2,493, N6C 1,270/2,690, U4J 877/3,083. Bootstrap B=10,000 over specs only.

Sensitivity: D9P K8Z 9 classes, ceiling F≤0.8889, observed F=.7316 =82.3% ceiling. Threshold multiplier F: ×0.5 .7448, ×0.8 .7435, ×0.9 .7394, ×1.1 .7289, ×1.25 .7314, ×1.5 .7308, ×2 .7232; equal thirds .7018; deciles .7719; no size/D9P E7R .5733. Error already noted: “factor-four binnings 0.70 to 0.77” misstates multiplier range.

Results: registered outcomes fixed 6 Aug 2026. Table 3: Jbar=.1396 [.1377,.1418], premise holds; X4R F=.7316 [.7247,.7380], confirmed; Q2F random null separated, rejected; Z8N functional gap=.3344 [.3297,.3394], supported. Structural: 7,561 specs, 3,218 distinct circuits, 28,580,580 pairs; D quantiles 1%=.196, 25%=.788, median=.960, 75%=.998; median shared edge fraction 4%; 1% pairs Jaccard>.8; median size 200; random median-size overlap .0031; observed/chance ~45x.

D9P K8Z counts: early distributed 3107, late sparse 2153, late moderate 657, late distributed 489, early sparse 477, middle moderate 283, middle sparse 269, middle distributed 90, early moderate 36. Table 5 all fail Y3W at α=.20: L3X E7R .3950 π*=.7291; L3X K8Z .6597/.4875; L3X V2H .6744/.4786; D9P E7R .5733/.4788; D9P K8Z .7316/.4109; D9P V2H .7681/.4109.

§9 limitations: one model/task; second-model plan M9B and second task unrun. Circuit size is outcome not axis; threshold-selected size can distort F/null/gap; conditioning on size reduces instability most; pooled stats reportedly have within-size decomposition. Multiverse limited; C4Y excluded, so measured F lower bound. Discard high/uneven, retained metric imbalance not adjusted. Bootstrap invalid for groups of 2–5 specs; unusable intervals replaced by point estimates.

§11 reproducibility: public tag prereg-p1-confirmatory; one environment across 1,320 confirmatory cells; 22/22 archive files identical; analysis no GPU; headline recompute script has 36 checks/0 failures, F via 3 routes including brute force; numeric-token checker; tables emitted directly; 343 tests.

Core claim: audit valuable only if two auditors using same system/tool reach compatible conclusions; circuit-level evidence must be stable across defensible analytic specifications. Scope caveat says “nothing at all about scale. Methods: preregistered multiverse. Formalism has 8-tuple incl. granularity, but grid has seven dimensions excluding granularity: 7 objectives, 7 ablations, 4 corruptions nested within 5 operators, 4 metrics, 3 thresholds, 2 prompts, 5 seeds = 1,540 discovery cells and 18,480 specs preregistered. Seed selects sampled prompts/eval-set variability, not nondeterminism.

grade.reason: Review item 0 directly flags the abstract's overbroad claim of cross-family and cross-task generality by noting the empirical study was only on GPT-2 small and a single task, which matches the planted error's contradiction with later limitations.

sol_grade.reason: The second reported error identifies the abstract’s cross-family, cross-task, and deployment-scale claim as contradicted by the paper’s explicit limitation to one model, one task, and no evidence about scale.

errors.claim: “No scale claim is made.”
errors.location: this part, §3 What this paper is not claiming
errors.evidence: Earlier notes from the abstract record the claimed scope as: “Failure of Y3W holds across model families, tasks and deployment scale.”
errors.explanation: A claim that the paper makes no scale claim conflicts with the abstract’s stated scope that the Y3W failure holds across deployment scale.

errors.claim: “Across factor-four binnings | 0.70 to 0.77”
errors.evidence: The factor-four threshold binnings listed in Table 1 appear to be “all thresholds × 0.5” through “all thresholds × 2”, whose F values range from 0.7232 to 0.7448, not 0.70 to 0.77. The values 0.7018 and 0.7719 come from “equal thirds” and “deciles,” which are separate alternatives, not factor-four threshold binnings.
errors.explanation: The stated sensitivity range for factor-four binnings does not match the table entries for those binnings; it instead matches the broader set including equal thirds and deciles.

errors.claim: “Thus 2,692 of 7,561 specifications contribute no flips; instability lives entirely below 2,000 edges.”
errors.evidence: Table 7 shows discovered instability at size 2,000: “2,000 | 312 | 0.5714 | 3” and collapse only at “5,000 | 625 | 0.0000 | 1” and “10,000 | 2,067 | 0.0000 | 1.”
errors.explanation: The table indicates that discovered circuits still have nonzero disagreement and 3 classes at exactly 2,000 edges. Therefore instability does not live entirely below 2,000 edges; it extends through 2,000 and disappears only at 5,000 and 10,000.

errors.claim: “One model, one task.”
errors.evidence: Notes from earlier parts: Abstract claims “failure across model families/tasks/deployment scale,” while §6 studied “GPT-2 small, IOI.”
errors.explanation: This limitation states the paper has only one model and one task, contradicting the abstract’s broader claim of evidence across model families and tasks.

Paper title: “Explanation Multiplicity: Circuit-Level Interpretability”; claim: evidence does not survive defensible analytic variation. Core: circuit-derived regulatory evidence fails Y3W across tolerances; same tool/model yields incompatible Annex IV/Art.86 statements; standardisation/size controls do not rescue. Applicability beyond GPT-2 small/IOI untested.

Formalism: spec s=(o,a,d,m,τ,P,r,g). Claim map G7U maps circuit C(s)⊆E to Annex IV statements φ(C). Y3W/filability=agreement among claims, not truth. Q7V graph |E|=32,491; components 144 attention heads+12 MLPs=156. D=1-Jaccard; Jbar mean Jaccard. F=unbiased Gini-Simpson pair disagreement. Conditional Fwithin pair-weighted by groups. §8 Y3W protocol: declare analytic space S and deterministic published φ (not LM); compute π*=max claim count/N and F; passes α iff π*≥1−α; report π*, F, discard rate per axis level, within-group decomposition of every pooled statistic; filing unable to state π* is asserted not audited.

Internal errors noted: (1) sensitivity text “Across factor-four binnings 0.70 to 0.77” conflicts with factor-four multipliers ×0.5–×2 range 0.7232–0.7448; 0.70/0.77 from equal thirds/deciles. (2) §7.5 says “instability lives entirely below 2,000 edges,” but Table 7 has discovered F=0.5714/classes=3 at 2,000 edges; collapse only at 5,000/10,000.

Methods/results: GPT-2 small on IOI. Grid initially 7 objectives, 7 operators, 4 corruptions nested in 5 operators, 4 metrics, 3 thresholds, 2 prompts, 5 seeds=1,540 discovery cells/18,480 specs; 2 operators ignore corruption. One objective failed; realised objectives=6; realised discovery cells=1,320; realised specs=15,840. No circuit specs=8,279; kept claim-producing specs=7,561. Metric retention: T9V 3,947; H2W 1,467; N6C 1,270; U4J 877. Table 3 Jbar=.1396; F=.7316 [.7247,.7380]; functional gap=.3344 pooled. Structural: 7,561 specs, 3,218 distinct circuits, pairs=28,580,580; D median=.960; median shared-edge fraction 4%; median circuit size 200. D9P K8Z claim counts: early distributed 3107/.4109; late sparse 2153/.2848; size-aggregated early/late/middle=47.9/43.6/8.5. Table 5 all addressee-granularity combos fail α=.20.

Standardisation Table 6 residual F: metric .5939; operator .7014; objective .7018; threshold .7070; corruption .7092; prompt .7232; seed .7307. No single-axis standardisation suffices. REML size variance: ablation-corruption 78.8%, residual 11.5%, ablation 4.4%, threshold 4.1%, metric .7%.

Size/free/null/functional: fixed-size dominant-layer F=.2706 CI .2550-.2859, still >.20. Random baseline pooled discovered F=.7316 vs A6N .6774; fixed-size K8Z discovered .2746 vs A6N .4230; E7R .2706 vs .3822. Table7 discovered F nonzero sizes 10–2000, zero at 5000/10000; A6N zero from 1000 upward. Functional pooled agreement .6028, instability .3972, kappa .0146; size kappa .016-.047; raw agreement .52-.92; accuracy .51-.95; 6/10 sizes fail gap, 5 negative; pooled gap carried by 500–2000.

Limitations/discussion/repro: one model/task; unrun M9B Pythia-160m 924-cell plan (3 seeds); second task unrun. Circuit size outcome distorts F/null/gap; conditioning reduces instability most. Multiverse excludes unsupported C4Y optimal ablation, so F lower bound. Discard high/uneven; bootstrap invalid for groups 2–5 specs. Failed objective documented/exported but cannot execute. Regulator takeaway: evidence not worthless; evidentiary weight measurable. Reproducibility: public timestamped commit tag `prereg-p1-confirmatory`; archive verifies one environment across all 1,320 confirmatory cells; 22/22 files identical; analysis no GPU. Scripts assert headline quantities (36 checks, 0 failures; F via 3 routes incl. brute-force pairs), check manuscript numeric tokens against derivations; tables emitted directly; suite 343 tests.

Paper title: “Explanation Multipity: Circuit-Level Interpretability / Evidence Does Not Survive Defensible Analytic Variation” by Ajay Pravin Mahale, dated 12 Aug 2026. Framing: EU AI Act high-risk documentation/explanation requirements; circuit discovery as possible evidence source. Claim: current circuit evidence does not meet filing/audit standard; not proposing better discovery or saying interpretability worthless.

Methods/definitions: Pre-registered crossed multiverse over analytic axes from published implementations. Formal tuple s=(o,a,d,m,τ,P,r,g)=8 axes, though elsewhere “7 axes” (possible inconsistency). φ maps circuits deterministically to Annex IV statements, not LLM. GPT-2 small IOI. Original grid: 7 objectives, 7 ablations, 4 corruption distributions nested in 5 operators, 4 metrics, 3 thresholds, 2 prompt variants, 5 seeds = 1,540 discovery cells/18,480 specs. One objective failed: 220 cells runtime error; realised grid = 6 objectives, 1,320 cells, 15,840 specs. Surviving claim pool: 7,561. Table 2 kept/discarded/rate: comprehensiveness 3947/13/.003; KL 1467/2493/.630; logit diff 1270/2690/.679; sufficiency 877/3083/.779. Total discarded 8,279/15,840=52.3%; surviving pool 52% comprehensiveness vs 25% design.

Claim map: overseer based on layer band, size class, ranked segment; affected leads with input segment. Three nested granularities. Size bins from committed calibration. Table 1 committed bin F=0.7316; no size term coarse F=0.5733. Formal: C(s)⊆E; |E|=32,491; circuits touch 144 heads+12 MLPs=156 components. D=1−Jaccard; F=1−Σnc(nc−1)/N(N−1); π*=max share; filable iff π*≥1−α. Nine observed claim classes; ceiling F≤0.8889.

Results: Table 3 P0 Jbar 0.1396; H2 F=0.7316 confirmed; H3 random null separated intervals disjoint=rejected; H4 F−(1−agreement)=0.3344 supported. §7.1 7,561 specs, 3,218 distinct circuits; median Jaccard 4%; arithmetic error: k=200 formula gives .0031 not .031. §7.2 π*=.4109, fails α .05/.10/.20. Modal class early distributed 3107/.4109; early 47.9%, late 43.6%, middle 8.5%; overseer coarse modal .4788. Table 5 all fail α=.20. §7.3 metric largest F lever; Discussion says standardising metric removes 0.1377 of 0.7316 flip rate and no single knob solves. final_notes:
Paper: “Dropout: A Simple Way to Prevent Neural Networks from Overfitting” (JMLR 15, 2014), Srivastava et al.

Core dropout: train by independently retaining units with probability p; test by full net with outgoing weights scaled by p (or inverted dropout train activations ×1/p). Backprop through sampled subnetwork. Helpful: high LR/momentum, L2, max-norm ||incoming weights||≤c. Pretrained weights scaled by 1/p before dropout.

Overall/Table 1: dropout improved generalization on all listed classification datasets vs no-dropout NNs: MNIST, TIMIT, CIFAR-10/100, SVHN, ImageNet, Reuters-RCV1, Alternative Splicing.

Key results: MNIST Table 2 no-dropout logistic 1.60; dropout logistic 1.35; dropout ReLU 1.25; dropout+max-norm ReLU variants to 0.95; maxout 0.94; DBN+dropout 0.92; DBM+dropout 0.79. MNIST p=0.5 hidden, p=0.8 input. Appendix B.1: 60k train/10k test, held out 10k validation to tune, then recombined; 1M updates; final momentum .95, max-norm c=2; tested larger 4096/8192 nets, 2-layer improved, 3-layer worse unless more dropout.

SVHN Table 3: dropout FC 3.02; dropout all layers 2.55; maxout 2.47; human 2.0. Text says non-dropout conv nets best 3.95, but table has stochastic pooling 2.80 apparently no dropout. Appendix B.2: ~600k train/26k test; validation 6000 not recombined; RGB zero mean/unit variance; no benefit from contrast normalization/ZCA. Best architecture: conv 96/128/256 5×5 stride1, each with 3×3 max-pool stride2; then two 2048 FC; ReLUs; dropout all layers p=(0.9,0.75,0.75,0.5,0.5,0.5); max-norm c=4; momentum .95.

CIFAR Table 4: dropout FC 14.32/41.26; dropout all layers 12.61/37.20; maxout 11.68/38.57. Appendix B.3: CIFAR-10/100 50k train/10k test; 5k validation then recombined; preprocessing global contrast normalization per color channel then ZCA whitening. Data augmentation included translations/rotations? Current part says network architecture and dropout rates same as SVHN, except smaller input-layer learning rates.

ImageNet: ILSVRC-2010 Conv Net+dropout 37.5/17.0. ILSVRC-2012 avg 5 Conv Nets+dropout val 38.1/16.4, test top-5 16.4; won ILSVRC-2012. TIMIT Table 7: NN 6-layer 23.4; Dropout NN 6-layer 21.8; DBN-pretrained 4/6/8 baselines 22.7/22.4/20.7; mcRBM-DBN 20.5; DBN-pretrained 4- and 8-layer+dropout 19.7. Internal error: text says 8-layer reduces from 20.5 to 19.7, but table’s 8-layer baseline is 20.7; 20.5 is 5-layer mcRBM. Appendix B.4: Kaldi log-filter banks; monophone forced alignment; 21-frame windows; no speaker-dependent ops; inputs mean centered/unit variance; p=.8 input/.5 hidden; max-norm c=4; momentum .95 LR .1 decayed as ε0(1+t/T)^−1; DBN pretraining RBMs CD-1, Gaussian RBM variance fixed 1; finetuning DBN+dropout best LR ~.01, max-norm no improvement.

Reuters: no-dropout 31.05%, dropout 29.62%. Appendix B.5: RCV1 >800k docs/103 classes; subset 402,738 docs, vocab 2000, 50 categories, one class/doc, equal train/test; dropout improved all tried architectures but modestly due to >200k train examples.

Alternative Splicing Table 8: dropout NN 567, Bayesian NN 623 (higher better), so Bayesian > dropout. Appendix B.6: 3665 cassette exons, 1014 RNA features, 4 tissue types from 27 mouse tissues; target 4 softmax units, each 3 states inc/exc/nc; metric Code Quality formula; two-layer dropout net 1024 each; p=.5 hidden/.7 input; max-norm and high decaying LRs; averaged over same 5 folds as Xiong et al.

Other notes: Sec 6.5 Table 9 regularizers MNIST best Dropout+Max-norm 1.05. Sec 7: dropout features sparser; p flat 0.4–0.8 best ~0.6; no gain with tiny data; MC averaging ~50 sampled nets matches weight scaling. Sec 8 RBM dropout: internal equation bias swap (joint aᵀh+bᵀv but conditionals use b hidden/a visible). Sec 9 marginalized dropout adaptive ridge; Table 10 Gaussian slightly better than Bernoulli. Sec 10 Gaussian noise mean 1 variance (1-p)/p; conclusion claims SOTA on SVHN/ImageNet/CIFAR-100/MNIST; training 2–3× longer. Appendix heuristics: dropout net at least n/p units; LR 10–100× standard, momentum .95–.99; c typically 3–4; hidden p .5–.8, real-valued input ~.8.

Introduction: Deep nets with multiple nonlinear hidden layers are expressive but overfit with limited data due to fitting sampling noise. Existing anti-overfitting methods include early stopping, L1/L2 penalties, and soft weight sharing. With unlimited computation, best regularization for fixed-size model is averaging predictions over all possible parameter settings weighted by posterior probability given the training data; feasible sometimes for small/simple models, but authors seek cheaper approximation. They propose approximating an equally weighted geometric mean of predictions of exponentially many learned models sharing parameters.

Model combination usually improves performance, but averaging many separately trained large nets is too expensive; diversity would require different architectures or training data subsets, both difficult/costly, and test-time use of many large nets can be infeasible.

Dropout is presented as addressing overfitting and efficient approximate combination of exponentially many architectures. “Dropout” means temporarily removing units (hidden and visible) plus incoming/outgoing connections. Each unit retained independently with fixed probability p; p can be validated or set to 0.5, said close to optimal for many networks/tasks. For input units, optimal retention probability is usually closer to 1 than 0.5.

Paper: “Dropout: A Simple Way to Prevent Neural Networks from Overfitting” (JMLR 15, 2014, pp. 1929–1958), authors Srivastava, Hinton, Krizhevsky, Sutskever, Salakhutdinov.

Core claims so far: Dropout addresses overfitting in large deep nets by randomly dropping units (hidden and visible) and their incoming/outgoing connections during training, preventing co-adaptation. Each unit retained independently with probability p; p can be validated or set to 0.5, said close to optimal for many networks/tasks; for input units optimal p is usually closer to 1. Training samples from an exponential number of “thinned” networks with shared weights; a net with n units corresponds to 2^n possible thinned nets. Total parameter count remains O(n^2) or less. errors.claim: ImageNet dimensionality is “65536 (256 × 256 color)”
errors.evidence: A 256 × 256 color image has three color channels, so its dimensionality would be 256 × 256 × 3 = 196608, whereas 65536 equals only 256 × 256.
errors.explanation: The row internally conflicts: the stated dimensionality matches a single-channel 256×256 image, not a color image.

errors.claim: “Similarly, for an 8-layer net the error reduces from 20.5% to 19.7%.”
errors.location: this part, Section 6.2 Results on TIMIT
errors.evidence: Table 7 lists “DBN-pretrained NN (8 layers) (Mohamed et al., 2010)” with phone error rate 20.7, while 20.5 belongs to “mcRBM-DBN-pretrained NN (5 layers) (Dahl et al., 2010).”
errors.explanation: The text says the 8-layer net improves from 20.5% to 19.7%, but the table’s 8-layer baseline is 20.7%; 20.5% is for a different 5-layer model.

errors.claim: In the Dropout RBM conditional, “P(h_j = 1 | r_j, v) = 1(r_j = 1) σ(b_j + Σ_i W_ij v_i)” and “P(v_i = 1 | h) = σ(a_i + Σ_j W_ij h_j).”
errors.evidence: The same section defines the RBM joint distribution as “exp(v^T W h + a^T h + b^T v)” and says “θ = {W, a, b}”. In that parameterization, a is the hidden-unit bias vector and b is the visible-unit bias vector.
errors.explanation: The conditional distributions swap the biases: hidden-unit conditional probabilities should use the hidden bias a_j, while visible-unit conditionals should use the visible bias b_i. This conflicts with the joint distribution given immediately before.

errors.claim: “The CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 data sets consists of 50,000 training and 10,000 test images each.”

Paper: JMLR 15 (2014) 1929–1958, “Dropout: A Simple Way to Prevent Neural Networks from Overfitting.” Dropout drops units during training; test averaging approximated by unthinned net with outgoing weights multiplied by retention p. Inverted form: scale retained activations by 1/p at train, no test scaling. Common p=0.5 hidden, input closer to 1. Pretraining: scale pretrained weights up by 1/p before dropout finetuning. Claims improvements across vision, speech, document classification, computational biology.

Dataset Table 1: MNIST 784 60K/10K; SVHN 3072 600K/26K; CIFAR-10/100 3072 60K/10K; ImageNet row says 65536 (256×256 color), 1.2M/150K—possible issue because 256×256 color = 196608; TIMIT 2520 1.1M/58K frames; Reuters 2000 200K/200K; Alternative Splicing 1014 2932/733. Appendix B.3 says CIFAR-10/100 have 50K training/10K test, conflicting with Table 1’s 60K/10K.

Vision: MNIST Table 2 best non-pretrained dropout maxout 0.94; DBN+dropout 0.92; DBM+dropout 0.79 best permutation-invariant. Appendix B.1: MNIST used 10K validation then recombined; p=0.5 hidden, p=0.8 input, momentum 0.95, max-norm c=2; Fig.4 used 2/3/4 layers × 1024/2048. SVHN Table 3 best dropout all layers 2.55, maxout 2.47, human 2.0. Appendix B.2: SVHN validation 6000, conv filters 96/128/256 plus two 2048 FC, p=(0.9,0.75,0.75,0.5,0.5,0.5), c=4, momentum .95. CIFAR Table 4: +dropout all layers 12.61/37.20; maxout 11.68/38.57. ImageNet: Table 5 ILSVRC-2010 ConvNet+dropout 37.5/17.0 top-1/top-5. Table 6 ILSVRC-2012: standard vision features test top-5 27.3/26.2; ConvNet+dropout val 40.7/18.2; avg 5 ConvNets+dropout val 38.1/16.4, test top-5 16.4. Text/conclusion: dropout conv nets won ILSVRC-2012; top-5 about 16% vs 26%; methods using dropout achieve SOTA on SVHN, ImageNet, CIFAR-100, MNIST.

Section 8 Dropout RBMs: joint uses a hidden bias, b visible bias; internal error: conditionals swap biases. Section 9: Gaussian dropout Table 10: MNIST Bernoulli 1.08±0.04, Gaussian 0.95±0.04; CIFAR-10 Bernoulli 12.6±0.1, Gaussian 12.5±0.1. Conclusion: dropout increases training time 2–3×. Appendix heuristics: wider layers, LR 10–100×, momentum 0.95–0.99, max-norm c 3–4, hidden p 0.5–0.8, real input p≈0.8.

Paper: JMLR 15 (2014) 1929–1958, “Dropout: A Simple Way to Prevent Neural Networks from Overfitting” by Srivastava, Hinton, Krizhevsky, Sutskever, Salakhutdinov. Abstract claims: deep nets overfit; large nets slow at test time, making ensembles difficult; dropout randomly drops units and their connections during training to prevent co-adaptation. Dropout samples an exponential number of thinned networks during training. At test time, averaging predictions of all thinned networks can be approximated using a single unthinned network with smaller weights. Claimed to significantly reduce overfitting and improve over other regularization methods, with supervised learning improvements in vision, speech recognition, document classification, computational biology, and state-of-the-art results on many benchmarks.

Intro: Deep neural networks with multiple nonlinear hidden layers are expressive but can overfit limited data by learning sampling noise. Existing anti-overfitting methods include early stopping, L1/L2 regularization, and soft weight sharing. It starts to say with unlimited computation, best regularization for fixed-sized model is averaging predictions over all parameter settings weighted by something (continues later).

Figure 1: illustrates standard neural net with 2 hidden layers and a thinned version after dropout; crossed units have been dropped.

Intro: Deep nets with multiple nonlinear hidden layers are expressive but overfit limited data. Existing regularization: early stopping, L1/L2, soft weight sharing. Bayesian gold standard for fixed-size model would average over all parameter settings weighted by posterior probability given training data; possible for simple/small models, but too costly. Dropout aims to approximate an equally weighted geometric mean of predictions from exponentially many learned models sharing parameters.

Model combination usually improves performance, but averaging many separately trained large nets is prohibitively expensive; diverse nets need different architectures or data subsets, both costly/data-hungry; using many large nets at test time infeasible when fast responses needed.

Dropout addresses both overfitting and efficient approximate combination of exponentially many architectures. “Dropout” means temporarily removing units (hidden and visible) and all incoming/outgoing connections. Simplest dropout: each unit retained independently with fixed probability p, chosen by validation or set to 0.5, said close to optimal for many networks/tasks. For input units, optimal retention probability usually closer to 1 than 0.5.

Figure 1: standard net with 2 hidden layers and a thinned dropout version; crossed units dropped. Figure 2: during training a unit is present with probability p and has outgoing weights w; at test time it is always present and weights are multiplied by p, so the test-time output is the same as the expected training-time output.

Paper: JMLR 15 (2014) 1929–1958, “Dropout: A Simple Way to Prevent Neural Networks from Overfitting” by Srivastava et al. Abstract/intro: dropout randomly drops units/connections during training to prevent co-adaptation; samples exponentially many thinned networks; at test time averaging predictions of all thinned networks approximated by one unthinned network with scaled-down weights; improves supervised learning in vision, speech, document classification, computational biology; state-of-art on many benchmarks. Bayesian/model averaging motivation: dropout approximates equally weighted geometric mean/model combination for exponentially many shared-parameter nets, avoiding cost of training/evaluating many separate nets.

Dropout definition: temporarily remove hidden and visible units and their connections. Each unit retained independently with probability p, often p=0.5 for hidden units; input retention usually closer to 1. Current related-work section says dropping 20% input units and 50% hidden units often optimal; DAE noise typically 5%, but dropout’s test-time weight scaling permits higher noise. A net with n units corresponds to 2^n thinned networks; weights shared, so parameters remain O(n^2) or less. For each presentation of each training case, sample a new thinned network; each thinned network trained rarely if at all.

Test-time approximation: explicit averaging infeasible. Use single unthinned net without dropout; if a unit retained with probability p in training, multiply outgoing weights by p at test time (Fig. 2). Makes expected training-time hidden output equal test-time output. Current Sec. 4 formalizes: standard net has L hidden layers, y(0)=x, W(l), b(l); for l in {0,...,L−1}, z_i^(l+1)=w_i^(l+1)y^l+b_i^(l+1), y_i^(l+1)=f(z_i^(l+1)). Dropout: sample r_j^(l) ~ Bernoulli(p), set \tilde y^(l)=r^(l)*y^(l), then z_i^(l+1)=w_i^(l+1)\tilde y^l+b_i^(l+1), y_i=f(z_i). r^(l) independent Bernoulli variables with prob p of 1; applied at each layer; backprop through sampled sub-network. At test time W_test^(l)=p W^(l), use no dropout.

Motivation analogies: sexual reproduction favors mixability, discourages complex co-adaptations; hidden units must work with random other units. Units still learn different things; copying units is poor (replica-code analogy). Multiple smaller co-adaptations more robust than one large conspiracy.

Related work: dropout as stochastic regularization/noise on hidden units. Denoising autoencoders add noise to input and reconstruct clean input; dropout extends noise to hidden layers, model averaging, supervised learning, and neuron architectures like Boltzmann Machines. Deterministic counterpart via marginalizing dropout noise; paper will show simple cases yield deterministic regularizers. Related: van der Maaten et al. 2013 deterministic regularizers incl. “blankout” noise, but only inputs/no hidden layers; Wang & Manning 2013 marginalizing dropout for speed; Chen et al. 2012 marginalized DAEs. Adversarial dropping work (Globerson & Roweis 2006; Dekel et al. 2010) minimizes loss under worst-case dropped units with fixed max number, not stochastic distribution and no hidden units.

Paper scope: includes dropout RBM and experiments vs standard RBM; sections on previous work, formal model, training, experiments, analysis/hyperparameters, Dropout RBM, marginalizing dropout, practical guide.

Paper: JMLR 15 (2014) 1929–1958, “Dropout: A Simple Way to Prevent Neural Networks from Overfitting” by Srivastava et al. Dropout randomly drops hidden/visible units during training; samples exponentially many thinned networks; test-time averaging approximated by one unthinned network with outgoing weights multiplied by retention probability p. Improves supervised learning in vision, speech, document classification, computational biology; claims state-of-art on many benchmarks. Bayesian/model averaging motivation: approximates equally weighted geometric mean/model combination for exponentially many shared-parameter nets.

Definition/formalism: each unit retained independently with probability p, often p=0.5 hidden; input retention usually closer to 1. Related-work section says dropping 20% input units and 50% hidden units often optimal. Net with n units corresponds to 2^n thinned networks; parameters remain shared. For each presentation of each training case, sample a new thinned network. Sec. 4 standard net has y(0)=x, W(l), b(l); dropout samples r_j^(l) ~ Bernoulli(p), uses \tilde y^(l)=r^(l)*y^(l), forward/backprop only through sampled subnetwork. At test time W_test^(l)=p W^(l), no dropout.

Motivation/related work: discourages complex co-adaptations; units must work with random subsets. Dropout differs from denoising autoencoders by applying noise to hidden layers, model averaging, supervised learning, and architectures like Boltzmann Machines. Deterministic counterpart/marginalizing dropout noise later; related work includes van der Maaten blankout inputs only, Wang & Manning marginalized dropout, Chen marginalized DAEs, adversarial dropping worst-case fixed number/no hidden units.

Training (Sec. 5.1): train by SGD like standard nets, but for each training case in mini-batch sample thinned network; gradients averaged over cases; parameters unused by a case get zero gradient contribution. Momentum, annealed learning rates, L2 weight decay useful. Especially useful: max-norm regularization constrains incoming weight vector at each hidden unit ||w||2 ≤ c, projecting onto ball radius c when exceeded; c chosen by validation. Dropout plus max-norm, large decaying learning rates, high momentum gives significant boost over dropout alone; rationale: max-norm permits huge learning rates without weight blow-up and dropout noise explores weight space.

Unsupervised pretraining (Sec. 5.2): nets can be pretrained using RBMs, autoencoders, DBMs. Dropout can finetune pretrained nets; pretraining unchanged, but pretrained weights should be scaled up by 1/p so expected output under dropout matches pretraining output. Large finetuning learning rates can wipe out pretrained information; smaller learning rates retained it and improved final generalization vs finetuning without dropout.

Experiments intro (Sec. 6): trained dropout neural nets for classification across domains; claims dropout improved generalization on all tested datasets vs no-dropout neural nets. Datasets listed: MNIST, TIMIT, CIFAR-10/100, SVHN, ImageNet, Reuters-RCV1, Alternative Splicing. Key results in section; detailed descriptions in Appendix B.

errors.evidence: The same section defines the RBM joint distribution as “exp(v^T W h + a^T h + b^T v)” and says “θ = {W, a, b}”. In that parameterization, a is the hidden-unit bias vector and b is the visible-unit bias vector.
errors.explanation: The conditional distributions swap the biases: hidden-unit conditional probabilities should use the hidden bias a_j, while visible-unit conditionals should use the visible bias b_i. This conflicts with the joint distribution given immediately before.

Inverted form: scale retained activations by 1/p at train, no test scaling. Common p=0.5 hidden, input closer to 1. Pretraining: scale pretrained weights up by 1/p before dropout finetuning. Claims improvements across vision, speech, document classification, computational biology.

Dataset Table 1: MNIST 784 60K/10K; SVHN 3072 600K/26K; CIFAR-10/100 3072 60K/10K; ImageNet row says 65536 (256×256 color), 1.2M/150K—possible issue because 256×256 color = 196608; TIMIT 2520 1.1M/58K frames; Reuters 2000 200K/200K; Alternative Splicing 1014 2932/733. Appendix B.3 says CIFAR-10/100 have 50K training/10K test, conflicting with Table 1’s 60K/10K.

Vision: MNIST Table 2 best non-pretrained dropout maxout 0.94; DBN+dropout 0.92; DBM+dropout 0.79 best permutation-invariant. Appendix B.1: MNIST used 10K validation then recombined; p=0.5 hidden, p=0.8 input, momentum 0.95, max-norm c=2; Fig.4 used 2/3/4 layers × 1024/2048. SVHN Table 3 best dropout all layers 2.55, maxout 2.47, human 2.0. Appendix B.2: SVHN validation 6000, conv filters 96/128/256 plus two 2048 FC, p=(0.9,0.75,0.75,0.5,0.5,0.5), c=4, momentum .95. CIFAR Table 4: +dropout all layers 12.61/37.20; maxout 11.68/38.57. ImageNet: Table 5 ILSVRC-2010 ConvNet+dropout 37.5/17.0 top-1/top-5. Table 6 ILSVRC-2012: standard vision features test top-5 27.3/26.2; ConvNet+dropout val 40.7/18.2; avg 5 ConvNets+dropout val 38.1/16.4, test top-5 16.4. Text/conclusion: dropout conv nets won ILSVRC-2012; top-5 about 16% vs 26%; methods using dropout achieve SOTA on SVHN, ImageNet, CIFAR-100, MNIST.

TIMIT: NN 6 layers 23.4, dropout 6 layers 21.8; DBN-pretrained 4/6/8 layers 22.7/22.4/20.7; mcRBM-DBN 5 layers 20.5; DBN-pretrained 4+dropout 19.7; DBN-pretrained 8+dropout 19.7. Internal error found: prose says 8-layer reduces from 20.5 to 19.7, but table gives 8-layer baseline 20.7; 20.5 is 5-layer mcRBM. Reuters: best no-dropout NN 31.05%; dropout 29.62%.
