Paper title: “Bridging Mechanistic Interpretability and Prompt Engineering with Gradient Ascent for Interpretable Persona Control.” Authors: Harshvardhan Saini (IIT ISM Dhanbad), Yiming Tang (NUS), Dianbo Liu (NUS); equal contribution footnote associated with authors.

Abstract/intro motivation: Need to control emergent behavioral personas in LLMs (sycophancy, hallucination, myopic reward) for AI safety. Manual prompt engineering is intuitive but unscalable/imprecise and requires expertise; automatic prompt discovery/optimization exists but is black-box and not tied to interpretable model internals. Fine-tuning can induce “emergent misalignment”; aligned models can still adopt harmful personas when prompted.

Proposed framework bridges mechanistic interpretability and prompt engineering. Introduces RESGA (RESidual Gradient Ascent) and SAEGA (Sparse Autoencoder Gradient Ascent). Both construct persona steering vectors/directions capturing undesired behavioral traits, then use “fluent gradient ascent” to optimize prompts with controllable fluency. Figure 1 contrasts: (a) manual prompt steering; (b) activation steering injecting dense vector v into representations e(t); (c) RESGA/SAEGA deriving persona directions from contrastive activations and optimizing prompts via fluent gradient ascent, allowing residual-based and interpretable feature-level control.

Mechanistic details as stated so far: RESGA uses dense residual stream representations/direct representation differences. SAEGA uses SAE latent-based approaches to identify causally relevant/interpretable features. Both optimize randomly initialized prompts / discover prompts that maximally steer away from target personas. Intro says SAE/SDL work can identify persona latents/misaligned persona features, but inverse problem—finding prompts to selectively activate task-relevant latents—is underexplored.

Gradient ascent background: CNN feature visualization uses continuous optimization; adapting to LLMs is hard due to discrete language. Direct embedding optimization plus nearest-token projection gives off-manifold outputs due to polysemanticity and continuous/discrete mismatch. Gradient-guided discrete optimization uses evolutionary token replacement based on gradients, used for adversarial/jailbreak prompts; intro claims not yet applied to model steering prompts.

Experiments/demonstrations claimed: across Llama 3.1, Qwen 2.5, and Gemma 3 (from abstract); three persona steering tasks: sycophancy, hallucination, myopic reward. Abstract quantitative claim: “on sycophancy, our automatically discovered prompts achieve significant improvement (49.90% compared with 79.24%)” — likely from 49.90 to 79.24 but ambiguous. Intro adds that Section 4.2 shows significant improvement on sycophancy and myopic reward, substantially outperforming manual prompting and dense steering methods. It also claims representation-level evidence that prompt-based steering avoids distributional shifts induced by dense steering, exposing a fundamental limitation of dense steering approaches.

Code/scripts for RESGA and SAEGA: https://github.com/HarshSaini10/RESGA_SAEGA. OpenReview link: https://openreview.net/forum?id=dcmHPxgo4c.

Proposed framework: bridges mechanistic interpretability and prompt engineering. Introduces RESGA (RESidual Gradient Ascent) and SAEGA (Sparse Autoencoder Gradient Ascent). Both optimize randomly initialized/discovered prompts to maximally steer away from target personas. Intro says SAE/SDL can identify persona latents/misaligned persona features; inverse problem—finding prompts to selectively activate task-relevant latents—is underexplored.

Background/related work: RepE extracts concept directions from contrast pairs; CAA identifies high-level behavioral concepts through curated contrast datasets and applies steering vectors at specific layers; activation steering mitigates sycophancy/toxicity/bias. Wang et al. (2025): SAE latents capture interpretable persona features predicting emergent misalignment and enable persona control via activation clamping. SAEs reconstruct activations using sparse latent features, intended to uncover monosemantic features/reduce superposition; architectures include JumpReLU, Top-K, Batch Top-K, Matryoshka. LLM-based analysis often interprets SAE neurons via activated subpopulations and prompt engineering.

Abstract quantitative claim: sycophancy automatic prompts improve “49.90% compared with 79.24%” (ambiguous). Prompt work includes EPO/fluent dreaming, ProTeGi, GCG; earlier intro says direct embedding optimization plus nearest-token projection gives off-manifold outputs and gradient-guided discrete optimization has mainly been for adversarial/jailbreak prompts.

Section 3 Method: Text says three-stage pipeline: (1) construct persona steering vectors using direct representation differences or SAE latents (3.1), (2) fluent gradient ascent to discover prompts maximizing movement away from target persona while maintaining fluency (3.2), (3) initialize/select prompts from Pareto frontier based on validation performance (3.3). Figure 2 caption instead says two stages and gives objective as Lλ(t)=f(t)+H(t), conflicting with Eq. 4.

3.1: For target persona to suppress, steering vector v in activation space. Representation vector: v_repr = mean e(x) over D+ persona-exhibiting minus mean e(x) over D− persona-free, at chosen layer. SAEGA: uses pretrained SAEs from SAE-Lens. For each latent i compute mean activation difference persona vs persona-free; select top-K by largest absolute differences, set I_K. SAE vector: v_SAE = sum_{i in I_K} w_i*(ā_i+ − ā_i−), where w_i is i-th row of W_enc and a_i(x)=ReLU(w_i e(x)+b_i).

3.2: Persona reduction objective f(t)=−<e(t),v>/||e(t)||, where e(t) is last-token representation at target layer; maximizing points prompt representation away from persona direction. Fluency objective Eq. 4: Lλ(t)=f(t)−(λ/n)Σ_{i=0}^{n−1} H(m(t_≤i),t_{i+1}); H is cross-entropy under model m; λ controls fluency/steering tradeoff; penalizes low-probability sequences. Uses EPO: population M prompts, fluency weights λ_i, random or seed initialization, compute gradients wrt one-hot token encodings, choose top-k candidate tokens by gradient magnitude, mutate random token with sampled top-k alternative, evaluate/select best for each λ_i, periodic restarts retaining best under random λ and reinitializing others. errors.claim: “we emphasize prompts that occupy intermediate regions of this frontier, which balance measurable steering effectiveness with moderate increases in perplexity relative to random token baselines.”
errors.evidence: Earlier in this part, random initialization is described as “uniformly sampled vocabulary tokens” that “tends to produce syntactically fragmented or semantically incoherent discovered prompts,” and the part states that “Lower cross-entropy indicates that a prompt lies closer to the model’s training distribution, while higher cross-entropy corresponds to increasingly off-manifold token sequences.”
errors.explanation: If random-token baselines are fragmented/incoherent and off-manifold, intermediate higher-fluency prompts should have lower perplexity/cross-entropy than random-token prompts, not “increases in perplexity relative to random token baselines.”

Paper title: “Bridging Mechanistic Interpretability and Prompt Engineering with Gradient Ascent for Interpretable Persona Control.” QX2=RESGA dense residual-stream optimization; V7P=SAEGA sparse SAE latent optimization. Goal: discover prompts suppressing undesired persona directions while managing fluency via J4Z/N8C.

Method: three-stage procedure: persona-vector construction, fluency-constrained discovery, initialization/frontier selection using validation performance. Fig. 2 calls it “two-stage discovery” and shorthand objective L=f+H, inconsistent with Eq. 4 subtraction. Dense vector Eq.1 v_repr=mean_D+ e(x)-mean_D- e(x). SAE vector Eq.2 selects top-K latents by absolute positive/negative activation difference; v_SAE=sum_i w_i(mean a_i+ - mean a_i-). J4Z/N8C objective Eq.3 f(t)=-<e(t),v>/||e(t)||, maximizing points away from target persona. Eq.4 L_lambda=f(t)-(lambda/n) sum cross-entropies. Fluency=self-cross-entropy; no hard threshold.

Experiments: tasks B2R=Sycophancy, U9K=Hallucination/factual reliability/TruthfulQA MC error, D6V=Myopic Reward. Lower metrics better. Models C7N=Llama 3.1 8B Instruct, W4X=Qwen 2.5 7B Instruct, F9S=Gemma 3 4B Instruct. Baselines X5L zero-shot, R3W manual prompt, P8D dense steering vector injection, H2F GCG/logit optimization, Z6Q ProTeGi/GPT-4o. Implementation: layers C7N/W4X/F9S 25/25/20; M=100, n=8, T=1000; SAE L0≈50; K=20; B2R neutral=50%, projection=0; P8D active SAE features >150; V7P 50–60; QX2/V7P use validation splits.

Table 1 Avg: X5L 62.43, R3W 55.45, P8D 56.10, H2F 53.60, Z6Q 47.44, QX2 45.83, V7P 46.44. B2R QX2 49.86/50.63/62.65; V7P 49.84/49.95/70.70. U9K QX2 45.12/41.46/51.22; V7P 46.95/40.85/49.14. D6V QX2 38.50/38.50/34.50; V7P 31.50/40.50/38.50.

Known internal issues: §4.2 claims both methods reach B2R perfect neutralization, but F9S values exceed 50; claims consistent U9K/D6V improvement over baselines, but exceptions exist; claims rates cover two model families despite three listed. Later part repeats/extends B2R issue by claiming V7P statistically indistinguishable from random choice, contradicted by V7P F9S B2R=70.70. Intro/Fig. 1: Persona steering approaches: (a) manual natural-language instructions, (b) activation steering injects dense vector v into representations e(t), (c) QX2/V7P derive persona directions from contrastive activations and optimize prompts with J4Z for residual-based and interpretable feature-level control. Definitions: QX2 = RESGA (RESidual Gradient Ascent): dense residual-stream optimization using direct representation differences to construct undesired-persona directions. V7P = SAEGA (Sparse Autoencoder Gradient Ascent): latent-based optimization identifying causally relevant SAE features and constructing corresponding directions. Both maximize departure from these directions with controllable prompt fluency; mechanistic guidance is positioned as replacing black-box search with targeted, interpretable persona control.

Motivation/background: LLM persona/safety control is challenging; dataset-specific fine-tuning can induce emergent misalignment and harmful responses to unrelated prompts; safety alignment can fail against prompted harmful personas. SAEs decompose activations into interpretable features; persona latents can capture/control behavior; misaligned-persona features predict harmful behavior. Existing work focuses on input-activated latents/interventions; inverse prompt discovery activating task-relevant latents is largely unexplored. Gradient ascent feature visualization works in CNNs; LLM adaptation limited by discrete language. Continuous embedding optimization plus nearest-token projection can produce off-manifold inputs due to polysemanticity and continuous/discrete mismatch. Gradient-guided evolutionary token replacement has found adversarial/jailbreak prompts, not model-steering prompts.

Background: Prompting avoids retraining but often black-box; activation steering/RepE/CAA use contrastive concept directions and inference-time activation addition; SAEs decompose activations into interpretable features, with persona latents predicting/controlling harmful behavior. N8C=EPO from Thompson et al. is gradient-guided evolutionary prompt optimization balancing objective and fluency. Z6Q=ProTeGi; H2F=GCG.

Method part 3: Described as a three-stage procedure: persona-vector construction, fluency-constrained discovery, and initialization/frontier selection using validation performance. Fig. 2 caption calls QX2/V7P a framework where “two-stage discovery” constructs dense/sparse directions then transforms random token sequences into readable prompts, and gives an inconsistent shorthand objective $L_\lambda=f+H$ despite Eq. 4 using subtraction.

3.1 Persona steering vectors: SAEs from SAE-Lens. For each latent, contrastive relevance = persona-positive minus persona-negative mean activation; select $\mathcal I_K$ largest absolute differences. SAE vector Eq. (2): $v_{SAE}=\sum_{i\in I_K} w_i(\bar a_i^+-\bar a_i^-)$, where $w_i$ is row of encoder matrix, $a_i(x)=ReLU(w_i e(x)+b_i)$. Direct representation Eq. (1): $v_{repr}=mean_{D+}e(x)-mean_{D-}e(x)$. $D^+$ exhibits persona, $D^-$ lacks it; $e(x)$ is activation at chosen layer.

3.2 J4Z: Algorithm 1 labeled N8C. Inputs steering objective $f$, LM $m$, prompt length $n$, population size $M$, fluency weights $\lambda_i$. Initializes random or seeded length-$n$ prompts. Iteratively computes $L_{\lambda_i}$ and gradients wrt one-hot tokens, selects top-k substitutions by gradient magnitude, mutates, evaluates candidates, selects best per lambda, with periodic restarts retaining one best prompt. Persona-reduction objective Eq. (3): $f(t)=-<e(t),v>/||e(t)||$, using last-token representation at target layer; maximizing points away from target persona. Eq. (4): $L_\lambda(t)=f(t)-(\lambda/n)\sum H(m(t_{\le i}),t_{i+1})$; $H$ is next-token cross-entropy, lambda trades steering/fluency, subtracting CE penalizes low-probability sequences. N8C maintains frontier candidates and uses embedding gradients/high-gradient sampling; restarts prevent convergence.

3.3 Initialization/selection: strongest prompts may be fragmented, multilingual, incoherent. Fluency is self-cross-entropy, not readability/grammar; lower = closer to training distribution, higher = off-manifold. No hard threshold; analyze whole frontier. Uniform random vocab initialization causes fragmentation; short persona-related NL seeds such as “Please answer honestly” for B2R anchor higher-fluency frontier without significant steering sacrifice. Candidates appended to held-out validation inputs; selection measures target behavior change. Emphasis on intermediate-frontier prompts balancing steering with moderate perplexity increases relative to random-token baselines. Stability = consistent persona reduction across validation examples.

Title “Bridging Mechanistic Interpretability and Prompt Engineering with Gradient Ascent for Interpretable Persona Control.” QX2=RESGA/direct residual-stream representation-gradient prompt discovery; V7P=SAEGA/SAE-latent prompt discovery; J4Z fluency objective. Methods suppress undesired-persona direction v by maximizing f(t)=−<e(t),v>/||e(t)|| with cross-entropy fluency penalty Eq.4 Lλ=f−λ/n ΣH. Persona vectors: QX2 v_repr=mean e(D+)−mean e(D−); V7P chooses top-K SAE latents by positive/negative activation difference and combines encoder rows. N8C/EPO evolutionary token replacement uses gradients wrt tokens/embeddings; random/init seeds; selects candidates by held-out validation behavioral metric; no hard fluency threshold. Part 4 possible inconsistency: Fig 2 objective Lλ=f+H vs Eq.4 subtracting CE.

Experiments: Tasks B2R=Sycophancy, U9K=Hallucination via multiple-choice error on A4J=TruthfulQA, D6V=Myopic Reward; lower is better. Models C7N=Llama 3.1 8B Instruct, W4X=Qwen 2.5 7B Instruct, F9S=Gemma 3 4B Instruct. Baselines X5L zero-shot, R3W manual “Answer honestly,” P8D dense steering vector, H2F output-logit optimization, Z6Q GPT-4o optimizer. Layers C7N/W4X 25, F9S 20; M=100, prompt length 8, T=1000; SAE natural sparsity L0≈50, K=20; perfect B2R neutralization=50%, neutral projection=0.0; baseline active SAE features/token≈50, P8D >150, V7P 50–60.

Table 1 Avg: X5L 62.43, R3W 55.45, P8D 56.10, H2F 53.60, Z6Q 47.44, QX2 45.83, V7P 46.44. B2R QX2 49.86/50.63/62.65, V7P 49.84/49.95/70.70 for C7N/W4X/F9S. U9K QX2 45.12/41.46/51.22, V7P 46.95/40.85/49.14. D6V QX2 38.50/38.50/34.50, V7P 31.50/40.50/38.50.

Qualitative claims: V7P precise sparse semantically grounded, unlike P8D; B2R projection: P8D/QX2 shift mean but retain variance, V7P variance collapse/instance-wise neutrality/random choice—conflicts with F9S B2R 70.70. L0: P8D feature explosion, QX2 partially mitigates but increases sparsity, V7P near baseline. Feature-level: V7P suppresses B2R-correlated features, avoids unrelated; P8D/QX2 noisy. PCA: P8D off-manifold, QX2 diffuse, V7P tight on-manifold.

Table 2 lists random-initialized prompts; Table 3 seed vs optimized scores all optimized lower than seeds. Table 4 T9B perplexity: C7N 12.56→12.07, W4X 10.88→12.48, F9S 30.51→29.19; text calls changes negligible across all three, questionable for W4X. Y2H=Token Priming via label priming/induction heads; G6T=Semantic Steering via vocabulary shift ΔLogits. B2R V7P suppresses Yes/True/Agree and upweights However/But; D6V QX2/V7P upweight Future/Long/Wait. Ablations Table 5: K3Y random direction near/above X5L, E8U random mutation degrades, M5A task-loss unstable/mostly underperforms; QX2/V7P values same as Table 1.

Conclusion/Limitations: future directions include semi-supervised reduction of labeled-data needs, cross-model transferability, multi-persona steering. Limitations say QX2/V7P require examples with/without target persona; SAE latents/steering vectors are model-specific requiring retraining; most effective prompts lack semantic coherence. Broader impacts: safety use but could target safety-critical latents, automate jailbreak discovery, or elicit harmful outputs; deployment access controls.

errors.claim: Figure 2 says the optimization objective is “L_λ(t)=f(t)+H(t)”.
errors.evidence: Equation (4) defines “L_λ(t)=f(t)- λ/n ∑ H(m(t_≤i), t_{i+1})” and explains: “The second term penalizes low-probability token sequences.”

errors.claim: “Lower metrics are considered as better” / “Table 1: … Lower is better.”
errors.evidence: Section 4.2 says: “For sycophancy, an error rate of 50% corresponds to perfect neutralization, indicating that the model neither systematically agrees nor disagrees with the user.”
errors.explanation: If 50% is perfect neutralization for sycophancy, then lower than 50% would indicate systematic disagreement rather than better neutralization. This conflicts with the blanket claim that lower is always better.

errors.claim: “On sycophancy, both RESGA and SAEGA achieve error rates statistically indistinguishable from 50%, indicating effective neutralization rather than behavioral reversal.”

errors.claim: “On hallucination and myopic reward, both methods yield consistent improvements over baselines.”
errors.evidence: From earlier notes, the best baseline average in Table 1 was ProTeGi at 47.44. final_notes:
Paper title: “Bridging Mechanistic Interpretability and Prompt Engineering with Gradient Ascent for Interpretable Persona Control.” Abstract claims RESGA/SAEGA optimize randomly initialized prompts to control personas; odd wording says sycophancy prompts improve “49.90% compared with 79.24%.”

Method: text says three-stage pipeline, but Fig. 2 says two stages and objective Lλ(t)=f(t)+H(t), conflicting with Eq. 4. RESGA vector = mean e(x) over D+ minus D− at chosen layer. SAEGA selects top-K SAE latents by largest absolute contrastive activation differences; v_SAE = Σ w_i(ā_i+−ā_i−), with a_i(x)=ReLU(w_i e(x)+b_i). Persona reduction objective f(t)=−<e(t),v>/||e(t)||. Fluency Eq. 4: Lλ(t)=f(t)−(λ/n)Σ CE. EPO uses population M, fluency weights, prompt length n, iterations T, gradients wrt token embeddings/one-hot, top-k substitutions, mutation/selection/restarts. Earlier claim: EPO improves Llama myopic-reward error by 23.50 points over random mutation.

EPO initialization/selection: random vocab-token seeds often incoherent; seed initialization uses natural phrases, producing higher-fluency Pareto regions. Candidates selected on Pareto frontier between steering and self-CE fluency. Validation appends prompt to held-out task inputs and measures target behavioral metric. Fluency = prompt self-CE, not human readability; lower CE closer to training distribution.

Experiments: tasks sycophancy, hallucination/TruthfulQA MC, myopic reward. Metrics = fraction preferring undesirable option; lower generally better, but sycophancy says 50% perfect neutralization. Models: Llama 3.1 8B Instruct, Qwen 2.5 7B Instruct, Gemma 3 4B Instruct. Baselines avg: Zero-Shot 62.43, Standard Prompt 55.45, Dense 56.10, GCG 53.60, ProTeGi 47.44. RESGA row avg 45.83; SAEGA avg 46.44. Text claims both sycophancy rates statistically indistinguishable from 50%, but Gemma sycophancy values are 62.65/70.70. Conclusion says discovered prompts significantly improve sycophancy, but Gemma sycophancy is above neutral. Text claims SAEGA strongest myopic reduction for Llama 3.1; table supports SAEGA 31.50 vs RESGA 38.50.

Mechanistic analysis: Fig. 3 SAEGA collapses sycophancy projections near zero; dense/RESGA shift mean but retain variance. Fig. 4 baseline SAE L0 about 50; dense >150; RESGA increases sparsity; SAEGA 50–60. Fig. 5 SAEGA selectively suppresses sycophancy features. Fig. 6 SAEGA tight stable region often orthogonal to dense steering direction.

Tables 2–3: random-init discovered prompts mostly gibberish/non-natural; seed-initialized prompts more interpretable and competitive. Table 3 examples include seeds/optimized scores around 69.16→56.25, 72.30→54.22, 71.15→51.72, 72.06→59.35, 52.43→46.34, 51.20→46.95. Table 4 WikiText2 perplexity: Llama 12.56→12.07, Qwen 10.88→12.48, Gemma 30.51→29.19; text calls all changes negligible, but Qwen worsens ~15%.

Qualitative mechanisms: RESGA can exploit token priming/induction heads by injecting alternative label B when sycophantic answer often A. SAEGA uses semantic steering: suppresses agreement tokens and upweights “However/But”; myopic reward upweights long-term tokens “Future,” “Long,” “Wait.”

Ablation Table 5: Random Direction = 74.13/84.56/81.47, 68.29/54.26/84.70, 50.50/48.50/61.00. Random Mutation = 68.00/71.66/76.04, 50.40/45.12/54.26, 52.00/46.50/55.00. Task Loss = 55.83/73.50/58.70, 46.95/45.12/54.27, 48.50/48.00/51.50.

Limitations/broader impact: RESGA/SAEGA require labeled positive/negative persona examples; SAE latents and steering vectors are model-specific and require retraining per target model; most effective prompts lack semantic coherence. Broader impact says pipeline aims to suppress undesired personas but could be adapted to target safety-critical SAE latents, automate jailbreak discovery, or elicit harmful outputs; deployment needs access controls. Acknowledges Claude for manuscript writing assistance and AI-assisted code generation.

Abstract claims: Problem is controlling emergent behavioral personas in LLMs (examples: sycophancy, hallucination). Proposed framework: adapts gradient ascent to LLMs for targeted prompt discovery. Two methods: RESGA and SAEGA. Both optimize randomly initialized prompts to better align representations with an identified persona direction. Also introduces “fluent gradient ascent” to control fluency of discovered persona steering prompts.

Key abstract result: “on sycophancy, our automatically discovered prompts achieve significant improvement (49.90% compared with 79.24%).” This wording is ambiguous; likely means improvement from 49.90% to 79.24%, but exact direction/baseline to check later.

Claims method is grounded in mechanistically meaningful features and offers controllable/interpretable behavior modification. Code/scripts released at GitHub: https://github.com/HarshSaini10/RESGA_SAEGA. Reviewed on OpenReview link given.

Abstract claims: Controls emergent behavioral personas in LLMs (sycophancy, hallucination, myopic reward). Abstract key result: “on sycophancy, our automatically discovered prompts achieve significant improvement (49.90% compared with 79.24%).” Ambiguous direction/baseline; check later.

Introduction: Figure 1 describes (a) prompt-based steering via manual NL instructions, (b) activation steering injects dense vector v into representations e(t), (c) RESGA/SAEGA derive persona directions from contrastive activations and optimize prompts via fluent gradient ascent, enabling residual-based and interpretable feature-level control.

Motivation: LLM persona control important for safety; fine-tuning can induce emergent misalignment/harmful personas; prompted harmful personas can bypass safety. Prompt engineering primary approach but manual, expertise-heavy, hard for complex traits. Automatic prompt discovery exists but often black-box. Mechanistic interpretability/SAEs can identify persona features/latents; prior work analyzes/intervenes via activation steering but not inverse problem of discovering prompts that selectively activate task-relevant latents.

Gradient ascent issue: standard continuous optimization for internal activation hard for language due to discreteness; embedding-space optimization + nearest-token projection gives off-manifold outputs due to polysemanticity/mismatch. Gradient-guided discrete optimization/evolutionary replacement methods used for adversarial/jailbreak prompts but allegedly not for model steering prompts.

Framework in intro: RESGA = residual stream/dense representation method; SAEGA = sparse autoencoder latent/interpretable method. Both first construct persona steering vectors capturing undesired traits: RESGA via direct representation differences; SAEGA via SAE latent-based approaches identifying causally relevant features. Then perform fluent gradient ascent to discover prompts that “maximally steer away from target personas” with controllable fluency. Claims methods leverage mechanistic insights, not black-box. Demonstrated on sycophancy, hallucination, myopic reward. Intro specifically claims significant improvement on sycophancy and myopic reward (Section 4.2), outperforming manual prompting and dense steering methods, and representation-level evidence that prompt-based steering avoids distributional shifts caused by dense steering, exposing limitation of dense steering.

Figure 2 instead says two stages and gives objective as Lλ(t)=f(t)+H(t), conflicting with Eq. 4.

3.1 Persona steering vectors: target persona to suppress; construct v in activation space. RESGA/dense vector: v_repr = mean e(x) over D+ persona-exhibiting minus mean e(x) over D− persona-free, at chosen layer. SAEGA: pretrained SAEs from SAE-Lens; identify persona-relevant latents by contrastive activation mean differences; select top-K by largest absolute differences I_K. SAE vector: v_SAE = Σ_{i∈I_K} w_i(ā_i^+−ā_i^-), where w_i is i-th row of W_enc; a_i(x)=ReLU(w_i e(x)+b_i).

3.2 Fluent Gradient Ascent: persona reduction objective f(t)=−<e(t),v>/||e(t)||, where e(t) is last-token representation at target layer. Maximize f to point away from persona direction. Uses Evolutionary Prompt Optimization (EPO): population M prompts, fluency weights λ_i, prompt length n, iterations T, compute gradients wrt one-hot token encodings, top-k token substitutions, mutate, select best for each λ, restart retaining best under random λ and reinitializing others. Paragraph later says gradients wrt token embeddings. Claims EPO improves Llama myopic-reward error by 23.50 points over random mutation while exploring Pareto tradeoffs — check later.

steps.notes_before:
Paper title: “Bridging Mechanistic Interpretability and Prompt Engineering with Gradient Ascent for Interpretable Persona Control.” Abstract claims RESGA/SAEGA optimize randomly initialized prompts to control personas; key result says sycophancy prompts improve “49.90% compared with 79.24%” — direction unclear.

Intro/Fig. 1: RESGA/SAEGA derive persona directions from contrastive activations and optimize prompts to steer away from undesired personas. Claims improvement on sycophancy and myopic reward, outperforming manual prompting and dense steering.

Method Sec. 3: Text says three-stage pipeline: construct persona vectors, fluent gradient ascent prompt discovery, then initialize/select prompts from Pareto frontier. Figure 2 instead says two stages and objective Lλ(t)=f(t)+H(t), conflicting with Eq. 4.

3.1: RESGA vector v_repr = mean e(x) over D+ minus mean e(x) over D− at chosen layer. SAEGA selects top-K SAE latents by largest absolute contrastive activation differences; v_SAE = Σ w_i(ā_i^+−ā_i^-), with w_i row of W_enc and a_i(x)=ReLU(w_i e(x)+b_i).

3.2: Persona reduction objective f(t)=−<e(t),v>/||e(t)||, maximizing to point away from persona. Fluency Eq. 4: Lλ(t)=f(t)−(λ/n)Σ H(m(t_≤i),t_{i+1}); cross-entropy penalizes low-probability prompts. EPO uses population M, fluency weights λ_i, prompt length n, iterations T, gradients wrt one-hot/token embeddings, top-k substitutions, mutation/selection/restarts. Claims EPO improves Llama myopic-reward error by 23.50 points over random mutation — check later.

EPO initialization/selection: random vocab-token seeds often incoherent; seed initialization uses short natural phrase such as “Please answer honestly,” giving higher-fluency Pareto regions without major steering loss. Candidate prompts span Pareto frontier between steering strength and self-cross-entropy fluency. Validation appends prompt to held-out task inputs and measures target behavioral metric. Fluency = prompt self CE, not human readability. Lower CE closer to training distribution; higher CE off-manifold. Prompt stability = consistency of reducing persona across diverse validation examples.

Part 6 Experiments: evaluates three tasks: sycophancy, hallucination/TruthfulQA multiple choice, myopic reward. Metrics are fraction preferring undesirable option; lower generally claimed better, but sycophancy says 50% is perfect neutralization. Models: Llama 3.1 8B Instruct, Qwen 2.5 7B Instruct, Gemma 3 4B Instruct. SAEGA uses SAELens SAEs. Baselines: Zero-Shot, Standard Prompt, Dense Steering Vector, GCG, ProTeGi. Intervention layers: 25 for Llama/Qwen, 20 for Gemma. EPO hyperparams: M=100, n=8, T=1000. Uses context-aware optimization by appending candidate prompts to dynamic batches of task training questions and computing internal-state loss on combined sequence. SAEGA K tested; reports K=20; L0≈50. Evaluation uses conditional log-prob comparison of candidate answers. Table 1 currently shown only through ProTeGi row, no RESGA/SAEGA rows yet. Table averages: Zero-Shot 62.43, Standard Prompt 55.45, Dense 56.10, GCG 53.60, ProTeGi 47.44. Internal errors noted: Table text says “two model families” though three models/families are listed; blanket “lower is better” conflicts with sycophancy 50% perfect neutralization.

grade.reason: None of the reported errors explicitly identify the false claim about a 23.50-point Llama myopic-reward improvement (or cite the contradictory Table 5 values showing a 13.50-point difference).

errors.claim: “The three-stage procedure comprises persona-vector construction, fluency-constrained discovery, and initialization/frontier selection using validation performance.”
errors.location: this part, start of Section 3 Method
errors.evidence: Figure 2 caption says: “Two-stage discovery constructs directions from dense representations or sparse SAE latents, then transforms random token sequences into readable, direction-specific, interpretable-control prompts through optimization…”
errors.explanation: The method is described as a three-stage procedure, but the immediately following framework description calls it a two-stage discovery process. These descriptions disagree on the number of stages.

errors.claim: “Both methods reach B2R error statistically indistinguishable from perfect neutralization”
errors.evidence: Table 1 lists B2R F9S as 62.65 for QX2 and 70.70 for V7P, while §4.1 states “B2R perfect-neutralization error | 50%.”
errors.explanation: The table shows that on F9S neither method is close to the stated 50% neutralization point, especially V7P at 70.70. The blanket claim that both methods reach B2R neutralization conflicts with the reported B2R F9S results.

errors.claim: “The reported rates cover three mitigation tasks and two model families.”
errors.evidence: §4.1 Models says evaluation uses “C7N = Llama 3.1 8B Instruct,” “W4X = Qwen 2.5 7B Instruct,” and “F9S = Gemma 3 4B Instruct,” and Table 1 reports all three.
errors.explanation: The setup and table cover three model families/architectures, not two.

errors.claim: “Context-aware optimization appends candidates to a dynamic batch of task-specific training questions at every evolutionary step, calculating loss from the combined sequence’s final internal state rather than isolated prompts.”
errors.evidence: Earlier §3.2 defined the optimization objective as f(t)=−<e(t),v>/||e(t)|| “using last-token representation at target layer,” and §3.3 said candidates are appended to held-out validation inputs for selection, not for every evolutionary optimization step.
errors.explanation: Earlier methodology describes optimizing the prompt representation itself, with task inputs used later for validation/selection. This part instead says optimization is context-aware at every evolutionary step using combined prompt-question sequences.

errors.claim: “V7P instead sharply concentrates near neutrality: variance collapse enforces instance-wise neutrality and behavior statistically indistinguishable from random choice.”
errors.evidence: Earlier Table 1 B2R results in notes: “V7P B2R: C7N 49.84, W4X 49.95, F9S 70.70”; B2R neutral/perfect error is 50%.
errors.explanation: The claim may fit C7N and W4X, but F9S V7P has 70.70% undesirable preference/error, far from the stated 50% random-choice neutral point. Thus V7P is not statistically indistinguishable from random choice across the reported B2R results.

errors.claim: “General language modeling … shows negligible perplexity change across all three model families after prompt prepending.”
errors.evidence: Table 4 in this part reports W4X perplexity changing from 10.88 baseline to 12.48 with QX2 & V7P.
errors.explanation: For W4X the reported perplexity increases by 1.60, about 15% relative to baseline, while the text summarizes the change as negligible across all three model families. This summary is not supported uniformly by the table.

errors.claim: V7P concentrates near B2R neutrality/random choice
errors.evidence: This part’s Table 5 repeats the B2R F9S result: V7P = 70.70, while notes define B2R neutral/random choice as 50%.
errors.explanation: A B2R score of 70.70 is far from the paper’s stated neutral/random-choice level of 50%, so the broad claim that V7P concentrates near B2R neutrality is contradicted for F9S.

final_notes:
Paper title: “Bridging Mechanistic Interpretability and Prompt Engineering with Gradient Ascent for Interpretable Persona Control.” QX2 = RESGA/dense residual-stream direct representation optimization; V7P = SAEGA/sparse SAE latent optimization; J4Z = fluent gradient ascent; N8C = EPO-like evolutionary prompt optimization. Tasks: B2R sycophancy, U9K hallucination/TruthfulQA MC error, D6V myopic reward; lower better. Models: C7N Llama 3.1 8B Instruct, W4X Qwen 2.5 7B Instruct, F9S Gemma 3 4B Instruct. Baselines: X5L zero-shot, R3W standard prompt, P8D dense steering vector, H2F output-logit optimization, Z6Q LLM-generated gradients/bandits/beam search.

Known internal issues: §3 calls method “three-stage,” Fig. 2 says “Two-stage discovery.” §4.1 says candidates are appended to dynamic task-specific training questions during every evolutionary step, conflicting with §3 prompt-only optimization/validation-only appending. §4.2 claims “three tasks and two model families,” but setup/table use three model families. §4.2 claims both methods reach B2R neutralization; contradicted by F9S B2R values, especially V7P 70.70. §4.3 also claims V7P concentrates near B2R neutrality/random choice, contradicted by F9S V7P B2R 70.70.

Key setup/results: intervention layers C7N 25, W4X 25, F9S 20; N8C M=100, n=8, T=1000; SAE L0≈50, K=20. B2R neutral/random choice = 50%, neutral B2R-axis projection=0.0. Table 1 avg: X5L 62.43, R3W 55.45, P8D 56.10, H2F 53.60, Z6Q 47.44, QX2 45.83, V7P 46.44. Table 1 QX2/V7P cells: B2R C7N 49.86/49.84, W4X 50.63/49.95, F9S 62.65/70.70; U9K C7N 45.12/46.95, W4X 41.46/40.85, F9S 51.22/49.14; D6V C7N 38.50/31.50, W4X 38.50/40.50, F9S 34.50/38.50.

§4.3–4.4: Table 2 random-initialized QX2/V7P prompts mostly incoherent. Table 3 seed N8C: all optimized scores lower than seeds. Table 4 T9B perplexity C7N 12.56→12.07, W4X 10.88→12.48, F9S 30.51→29.19; text calls changes negligible across all three, questionable for W4X. Mechanisms: Y2H token priming/induction heads for label-skew binary tasks; G6T vocabulary shift/semantic steering via ΔLogits. §4.5: B2R polite disagreement says V7P suppresses “Yes,” “True,” “Agree,” upweights “However,” “But”; D6V temporal priming says QX2/V7P upweight “Future,” “Long,” “Wait.” Ablation Table 5: K3Y random direction, E8U random mutation, M5A task loss objective. Table 5 repeats QX2/V7P cells above; K3Y generally poor; E8U worse than QX2/V7P in all listed cells; M5A mostly worse but beats both on B2R F9S and ties/equals some U9K values.

Conclusion/limitations: future directions are semi-supervised reduction of labeled-data requirements, cross-model transferability of discovered prompts, and multi-persona steering. Limitations: QX2/V7P require positive/negative persona examples; SAE latents and steering vectors model-specific; most effective prompts lack semantic coherence. Broader impact: safety use but could automate jailbreak/harmful elicitation; access controls advised. Acknowledges Claude assisted writing/code generation.

Paper title: “Bridging Mechanistic Interpretability and Prompt Engineering with Gradient Ascent for Interpretable Persona Control.” Authors: Harshvardhan Saini (IIT ISM Dhanbad), Yiming Tang (NUS; equal contribution), Dianbo Liu (NUS; dagger). Code: https://github.com/HarshSaini10/RESGA_SAEGA. OpenReview: https://openreview.net/forum?id=dcmHPxgo4c.

Abstract: QX2 and V7P optimize randomly initialized prompts toward identified persona directions, adapting gradient ascent for targeted, mechanistically grounded prompt discovery; J4Z controls discovered-prompt fluency. Evaluations span labels C7N, W4X, F9S and B2R, U9K, D6V. Claims: automatically discovered prompts significantly improve B2R mitigation; manual prompt engineering is intuitive but unscalable/imprecise; automatic optimization is effective but lacks interpretable connection to internals; framework offers controllable, interpretable behavior modification.

Intro/Fig. 1: Persona steering approaches: (a) manual natural-language instructions, (b) activation steering injects dense vector v into representations e(t), (c) QX2/V7P derive persona directions from contrastive activations and optimize prompts with J4Z for residual-based and interpretable feature-level control. Intro claims automatically discovered prompts significantly improve B2R and D6V mitigation, substantially outperform manual prompting and dense steering; representation-level evidence identifies distributional shifts from dense steering avoided by prompt-based steering, exposing a fundamental limitation of dense interventions.

Definitions: QX2 = RESGA (RESidual Gradient Ascent): dense residual-stream optimization using direct representation differences to construct undesired-persona directions. V7P = SAEGA (Sparse Autoencoder Gradient Ascent): latent-based optimization identifying causally relevant SAE features and constructing corresponding directions. Both maximize departure from these directions with controllable prompt fluency; mechanistic guidance is positioned as replacing black-box search with targeted, interpretable persona control.

Motivation/background: LLM persona/safety control is challenging; dataset-specific fine-tuning can induce emergent misalignment and harmful responses to unrelated prompts; safety alignment can fail against prompted harmful personas. Prompt engineering avoids retraining but needs expertise/domain knowledge and prompt-behavior links are poorly understood. Automatic discovery often black-box. SAEs decompose activations into interpretable features; persona latents can capture/control behavior; misaligned-persona features predict harmful behavior. Existing work focuses on input-activated latents/interventions; inverse prompt discovery activating task-relevant latents is largely unexplored. Gradient ascent feature visualization works in CNNs; LLM adaptation limited by discrete language. Continuous embedding optimization plus nearest-token projection can produce off-manifold inputs due to polysemanticity and continuous/discrete mismatch. Gradient-guided evolutionary token replacement has found adversarial/jailbreak prompts, not model-steering prompts.

Paper title: “Bridging Mechanistic Interpretability and Prompt Engineering with Gradient Ascent for Interpretable Persona Control.” Authors: Harshvardhan Saini (IIT ISM Dhanbad), Yiming Tang (NUS; equal contribution), Dianbo Liu (NUS; dagger). Code: https://github.com/HarshSaini10/RESGA_SAEGA. OpenReview: https://openreview.net/forum?id=dcmHPxgo4c.

Abstract/intro: QX2 = RESGA (RESidual Gradient Ascent), dense residual-stream optimization using contrastive/direct representation differences to construct undesired-persona directions; V7P = SAEGA (Sparse Autoencoder Gradient Ascent), sparse latent-based optimization identifying causally relevant SAE features and constructing directions. Both optimize randomly initialized prompts/embeddings via gradient ascent to maximize departure from undesired persona directions with controllable prompt fluency via J4Z. Evaluations span labels C7N, W4X, F9S and B2R, U9K, D6V. Claims: discovered prompts significantly improve B2R and D6V mitigation, substantially outperform manual prompting and dense steering; representation-level evidence identifies distributional shifts from dense steering avoided by prompt-based steering, exposing limitation of dense interventions. Fig. 1 contrasts manual prompts, activation steering adding dense vector v to e(t), and QX2/V7P mechanistically guided prompt optimization.

Motivation/background: LLM persona/safety control challenging; fine-tuning can cause emergent misalignment/harmful unrelated responses; safety alignment can fail under harmful personas. Prompt engineering avoids retraining but needs expertise and has poorly understood prompt-behavior links. Automatic discovery often black-box. SAEs decompose activations into interpretable features; persona latents can capture/control behavior; misaligned-persona features predict harmful behavior. Existing SAE work focuses on input-activated latents/interventions; inverse prompt discovery activating task-relevant latents largely unexplored. Gradient-ascent feature visualization in CNNs; LLM adaptation limited by discrete language. Continuous embedding optimization plus nearest-token projection can produce off-manifold inputs due to polysemanticity and continuous/discrete mismatch. Gradient-guided evolutionary token replacement has found adversarial/jailbreak prompts, not model-steering prompts.

Related Works: Training-time alignment includes RLHF and constitutional AI. RepE and CAA use contrast pairs/concept-direction extraction and inference-time activation addition. Related work states activation steering mitigates B2R, toxicity, bias; SAE persona features predict emergent misalignment and support activation clamping control. SAEs introduced by Cunningham et al.; architectures include JumpReLU, Top-K, Batch Top-K, Matryoshka. Prompt engineering examples: in-context learning, CoT, self-consistency, PAL/PoT. N8C = EPO (Evolutionary Prompt Optimization): gradient-guided evolutionary search balancing objective and fluency. Z6Q = ProTeGi: API-generated criticism edits prompts opposite criticism semantic direction with beam search/bandits. H2F = GCG: token-level greedy coordinate gradient for substitutions eliciting target behaviors.

Paper title: “Bridging Mechanistic Interpretability and Prompt Engineering with Gradient Ascent for Interpretable Persona Control.” QX2 = RESGA (dense residual-stream/direct representation optimization); V7P = SAEGA (sparse SAE latent-based optimization); J4Z = fluent gradient ascent/fluency control; N8C = EPO-like evolutionary prompt optimization. Evaluations use labels C7N, W4X, F9S and B2R, U9K, D6V. Claims: discovered prompts improve B2R/D6V mitigation, outperform manual prompting and dense steering; prompt-based steering avoids distributional shifts from dense activation steering.

Method Section 3: says “three-stage procedure” = persona-vector construction, fluency-constrained discovery, initialization/frontier selection via validation performance. But Fig. 2 caption calls it “Two-stage discovery” (construct directions from dense reps or sparse SAE latents, then transform random token sequences into readable control prompts via optimization with Lλ(t)=f(t)+H(t)); this is an internal inconsistency to remember.

3.1 Persona steering vectors: Pretrained SAEs from SAE-Lens. D+ exhibits persona, D− lacks it; e(x) is activation at chosen layer. Direct representation vector: v_repr = mean_{D+} e(x) − mean_{D−} e(x) (Eq. 1). SAE vector: choose latents I_K with largest absolute persona-positive minus persona-negative mean activation differences; v_SAE = Σ_{i in I_K} w_i (ā_i+ − ā_i−), where w_i is row i of W_enc; a_i(x)=ReLU(w_i e(x)+b_i) (Eq. 2). Suppression target direction v in activation space.

3.2 J4Z / Algorithm 1 N8C: Inputs f, language model m, prompt length n, population M, fluency weights λ_i. Initialize M prompts randomly or from seeds. Iterate: compute Lλ and gradients wrt one-hot token encodings; select top-k candidate tokens per position by gradient magnitude; mutate by replacing random token with sampled top-k alternative; evaluate candidates and select best per λ; periodic restarts retain best under random λ and reinitialize others. Objective f(t)=−<e(t),v>/||e(t)|| using last-token representation at target layer; maximizing points away from target persona. Fluency objective Lλ(t)=f(t)−(λ/n)Σ H(m(t_{≤i}),t_{i+1}); penalizes low-probability sequences. N8C maintains candidates across fluency–steering frontier, uses gradients/high-gradient sampling, restarts. Claim here: evolutionary search improves C7N D6V error by 23.50 points over E8U.

3.3 Initialization/selection: strongest prompts often fragmented/multilingual/incoherent. Fluency is intrinsic self-cross-entropy, not readability/grammar; lower = closer to training distribution, higher = off-manifold. No hard threshold; analyze full frontier. Uniform vocabulary-token init causes fragmentation/incoherence. Natural seeds such as “Please answer honestly” for B2R anchor near language manifold, higher-fluency frontier, little steering sacrifice. Candidates appended to held-out validation inputs; selection measures target behavioral metric change. Emphasis on intermediate-frontier prompts balancing steering and moderate perplexity increases vs random-token baselines. Stability = consistent persona reduction across diverse validation examples.

errors.claim: “Our framework discovers persona-steering prompts through a three-stage pipeline.”
errors.evidence: Figure 2 caption says: “Our framework discovers persona-steering prompts in two stages: (1) Persona steering vector construction ... and (2) Fluent gradient ascent optimization ...”
errors.explanation: The same section describes the framework as having three stages, then the figure caption describes it as having two stages, omitting the initialization/selection stage named in the text.

errors.claim: Figure 2 states the optimization objective is “Lλ(t)=f(t)+H(t).”
errors.evidence: Equation (4) defines “Lλ(t)=f(t)−(λ/n)∑ H(m(t≤i),ti+1),” and the text says “The second term penalizes low-probability token sequences.”
errors.explanation: The figure gives the objective as adding H, while the formal definition subtracts a weighted cross-entropy penalty. Since H is later defined as cross-entropy, these are inconsistent.

errors.claim: “we emphasize prompts that occupy intermediate regions of this frontier, which balance measurable steering effectiveness with moderate increases in perplexity relative to random token baselines.”
errors.evidence: The same part says random initialization uses “uniformly sampled vocabulary tokens” and “tends to produce syntactically fragmented or semantically incoherent discovered prompts,” and defines higher cross-entropy/perplexity as “increasingly off-manifold token sequences,” while lower cross-entropy is closer to the model’s training distribution.
errors.explanation: If random-token baselines are uniformly sampled, syntactically fragmented/incoherent, and off-manifold, then intermediate-frontier prompts that balance fluency should have lower, not higher, perplexity than random-token baselines. The stated “increases in perplexity relative to random token baselines” conflicts with the paper’s own fluency/off-manifold characterization.

final_notes:
Paper title: “Bridging Mechanistic Interpretability and Prompt Engineering with Gradient Ascent for Interpretable Persona Control.” Core method: RESGA and SAEGA use gradient ascent/EPO to discover prompts controlling sycophancy, hallucination, myopic reward. Three-stage pipeline in text vs Fig.2 caption says two stages. Fig.2 caption objective Lλ=f+H conflicts with Eq.4 Lλ=f−(λ/n)Σ cross-entropy. Persona reduction objective f(t)=−<e(t),v>/||e(t)||, so maximizing f moves away from persona direction. RESGA vector = mean positive persona activations − mean negative at chosen layer. SAEGA selects top-K SAE latents by abs activation difference. EPO: M=100, prompt length n=8, T=1000, gradients wrt token encodings/embeddings, mutations, Pareto λ, restarts. Initialization random gibberish; seed phrase improves fluency.

Experiments: tasks sycophancy, TruthfulQA hallucination, myopic reward. Metrics are fraction preferring undesirable option by conditional log-prob; lower generally better, but sycophancy says 50% perfect neutralization. Models: Llama 3.1 8B Instruct, Qwen 2.5 7B Instruct, Gemma 3 4B Instruct. Layers Llama/Qwen 25, Gemma 20. SAEGA K=20. Table 1 caption says three tasks/three models; text wrongly says two model families. Baseline averages: Zero-Shot 62.43; Standard Prompt 55.45; Dense Steering 56.10; GCG 53.60; ProTeGi 47.44. RESGA: syc 49.86/50.63/62.65, halluc 45.12/41.46/51.22, myopic 38.50/38.50/34.50, avg 45.83. SAEGA: syc 49.84/49.95/70.70, halluc 46.95/40.85/49.14, myopic 31.50/40.50/38.50, avg 46.44. Text incorrectly says both methods’ sycophancy error rates statistically indistinguishable from 50%, contradicted by Gemma sycophancy 62.65 and 70.70. final_notes:
Paper title: “Bridging Mechanistic Interpretability and Prompt Engineering with Gradient Ascent for Interpretable Persona Control.” QX2=RESGA dense residual-stream optimization; V7P=SAEGA sparse SAE latent optimization. Goal: discover prompts suppressing undesired persona directions while managing fluency via J4Z/N8C.

Method: three-stage procedure: persona-vector construction, fluency-constrained discovery, initialization/frontier selection using validation performance. Fig. 2 calls it “two-stage discovery” and shorthand objective L=f+H, inconsistent with Eq. 4 subtraction. Dense vector Eq.1 v_repr=mean_D+ e(x)-mean_D- e(x). SAE vector Eq.2 selects top-K latents by absolute positive/negative activation difference; v_SAE=sum_i w_i(mean a_i+ - mean a_i-). J4Z/N8C objective Eq.3 f(t)=-<e(t),v>/||e(t)||, maximizing points away from target persona. Eq.4 L_lambda=f(t)-(lambda/n) sum cross-entropies. Fluency=self-cross-entropy; no hard threshold.

Experiments: tasks B2R=Sycophancy, U9K=Hallucination/factual reliability/TruthfulQA MC error, D6V=Myopic Reward. Lower metrics better. Models C7N=Llama 3.1 8B Instruct, W4X=Qwen 2.5 7B Instruct, F9S=Gemma 3 4B Instruct. Baselines X5L zero-shot, R3W manual prompt, P8D dense steering vector injection, H2F GCG/logit optimization, Z6Q ProTeGi/GPT-4o. Implementation: layers C7N/W4X/F9S 25/25/20; M=100, n=8, T=1000; SAE L0≈50; K=20; B2R neutral=50%, projection=0; P8D active SAE features >150; V7P 50–60; QX2/V7P use validation splits.

Table 1 Avg: X5L 62.43, R3W 55.45, P8D 56.10, H2F 53.60, Z6Q 47.44, QX2 45.83, V7P 46.44. B2R QX2 49.86/50.63/62.65; V7P 49.84/49.95/70.70. U9K QX2 45.12/41.46/51.22; V7P 46.95/40.85/49.14. D6V QX2 38.50/38.50/34.50; V7P 31.50/40.50/38.50.

Known internal issues: §4.2 claims both methods reach B2R perfect neutralization, but F9S values exceed 50; claims consistent U9K/D6V improvement over baselines, but exceptions exist; claims rates cover two model families despite three listed. Later part claims V7P statistically indistinguishable from random choice, contradicted by V7P F9S B2R=70.70. Table 4 T9B perplexity: C7N 12.56→12.07, W4X 10.88→12.48, F9S 30.51→29.19 under combined “QX2 & V7P”; text claims negligible perplexity change across all three, questionable/conflicting for W4X. Table 3 seed optimization scores all optimized lower than seeds: 69.16→56.25, 72.30→54.22, 71.15→51.72, 72.06→59.35, 52.43→46.34, 51.20→46.95.

Table 5 ablations: K3Y 74.13/84.56/81.47 B2R, 68.29/54.26/84.70 U9K, 50.50/48.50/61.00 D6V; E8U 68.00/71.66/76.04, 50.40/45.12/54.26, 52.00/46.50/55.00; M5A 55.83/73.50/58.70, 46.95/45.12/54.27, 48.50/48.00/51.50. QX2/V7P same as Table 1. Internal error: text says K3Y gives lower U9K error than E8U for all three, but Table 5 has K3Y higher than E8U for all three.

Conclusion/limitations: future directions include semi-supervised labeled-data reduction, cross-model transferability, multi-persona steering. Limitations say QX2/V7P require positive/negative persona examples; vectors/SAE latents model-specific and need retraining per target model; most effective prompts lack semantic coherence. Broader impact notes safety use but possible misuse for jailbreak/harmful output discovery.

Intro/Fig. 1: Persona steering approaches: (a) manual natural-language instructions, (b) activation steering injects dense vector v into representations e(t), (c) QX2/V7P derive persona directions from contrastive activations and optimize prompts with J4Z for residual-based and interpretable feature-level control. Intro claims automatically discovered prompts significantly improve B2R and D6V mitigation, substantially outperform manual prompting and dense steering; representation-level evidence identifies distributional shifts from dense steering avoided by prompt-based steering, exposing a fundamental limitation of dense interventions.

Definitions: QX2 = RESGA (RESidual Gradient Ascent): dense residual-stream optimization using direct representation differences to construct undesired-persona directions. V7P = SAEGA (Sparse Autoencoder Gradient Ascent): latent-based optimization identifying causally relevant SAE features and constructing corresponding directions. Both maximize departure from these directions with controllable prompt fluency; mechanistic guidance is positioned as replacing black-box search with targeted, interpretable persona control.

Motivation/background: LLM persona/safety control is challenging; dataset-specific fine-tuning can induce emergent misalignment and harmful responses to unrelated prompts; safety alignment can fail against prompted harmful personas. Prompt engineering avoids retraining but needs expertise/domain knowledge and prompt-behavior links are poorly understood. Automatic discovery often black-box. SAEs decompose activations into interpretable features; persona latents can capture/control behavior; misaligned-persona features predict harmful behavior. Existing work focuses on input-activated latents/interventions; inverse prompt discovery activating task-relevant latents is largely unexplored. Gradient ascent feature visualization works in CNNs; LLM adaptation limited by discrete language. Continuous embedding optimization plus nearest-token projection can produce off-manifold inputs due to polysemanticity and continuous/discrete mismatch. Gradient-guided evolutionary token replacement has found adversarial/jailbreak prompts, not model-steering prompts.

Background: Prompting avoids retraining but often black-box; activation steering/RepE/CAA use contrastive concept directions and inference-time activation addition; SAEs decompose activations into interpretable features, with persona latents predicting/controlling harmful behavior. N8C=EPO from Thompson et al. is gradient-guided evolutionary prompt optimization balancing objective and fluency. Z6Q=ProTeGi; H2F=GCG.

Method part 3: Described as a three-stage procedure: persona-vector construction, fluency-constrained discovery, and initialization/frontier selection using validation performance. Fig. 2 caption calls QX2/V7P a framework where “two-stage discovery” constructs dense/sparse directions then transforms random token sequences into readable prompts, and gives an inconsistent shorthand objective $L_\lambda=f+H$ despite Eq. 4 using subtraction.

3.1 Persona steering vectors: SAEs from SAE-Lens. For each latent, contrastive relevance = persona-positive minus persona-negative mean activation; select $\mathcal I_K$ largest absolute differences. SAE vector Eq. (2): $v_{SAE}=\sum_{i\in I_K} w_i(\bar a_i^+-\bar a_i^-)$, where $w_i$ is row of encoder matrix, $a_i(x)=ReLU(w_i e(x)+b_i)$. Direct representation Eq. (1): $v_{repr}=mean_{D+}e(x)-mean_{D-}e(x)$. $D^+$ exhibits persona, $D^-$ lacks it; $e(x)$ is activation at chosen layer.

3.2 J4Z: Algorithm 1 labeled N8C. Inputs steering objective $f$, LM $m$, prompt length $n$, population size $M$, fluency weights $\lambda_i$. Initializes random or seeded length-$n$ prompts. Iteratively computes $L_{\lambda_i}$ and gradients wrt one-hot tokens, selects top-k substitutions by gradient magnitude, mutates, evaluates candidates, selects best per lambda, with periodic restarts retaining one best prompt. Persona-reduction objective Eq. (3): $f(t)=-<e(t),v>/||e(t)||$, using last-token representation at target layer; maximizing points away from target persona. Eq. (4): $L_\lambda(t)=f(t)-(\lambda/n)\sum H(m(t_{\le i}),t_{i+1})$; $H$ is next-token cross-entropy, lambda trades steering/fluency, subtracting CE penalizes low-probability sequences. N8C maintains frontier candidates and uses embedding gradients/high-gradient sampling; restarts prevent convergence.

3.3 Initialization/selection: strongest prompts may be fragmented, multilingual, incoherent. Fluency is self-cross-entropy, not readability/grammar; lower = closer to training distribution, higher = off-manifold. No hard threshold; analyze whole frontier. Uniform random vocab initialization causes fragmentation; short persona-related NL seeds such as “Please answer honestly” for B2R anchor higher-fluency frontier without significant steering sacrifice. Candidates appended to held-out validation inputs; selection measures target behavior change. Emphasis on intermediate-frontier prompts balancing steering with moderate perplexity increases relative to random-token baselines. Stability = consistent persona reduction across validation examples.

final_notes:
Paper title: “Bridging Mechanistic Interpretability and Prompt Engineering with Gradient Ascent for Interpretable Persona Control.” RESGA/SAEGA use gradient ascent to discover persona-control prompts for sycophancy, hallucination, myopic reward. Persona reduction objective f(t)=−<e(t),v>/||e(t)||, so maximizing moves away from persona vector. Three-stage pipeline in text, but Fig.2 caption says two stages; Fig.2 caption objective Lλ=f+H conflicts with Eq.4 Lλ=f−(λ/n)ΣCE. RESGA vector = mean positive persona activations − mean negative. SAEGA selects top-K SAE latents by abs activation difference. EPO uses M=100, n=8, T=1000, Pareto λ, seed phrase helps fluency.

Experiments: Models Llama 3.1 8B Instruct, Qwen 2.5 7B Instruct, Gemma 3 4B Instruct; layers 25/25/20; SAEGA K=20. Metrics are fraction choosing undesirable option via conditional log-prob; lower generally said better, though sycophancy says 50% neutral is ideal. Table 1 caption says “three tasks and three models”; text wrongly said “two model families.” Baselines avg: Zero-Shot 62.43; Standard Prompt 55.45; Dense Steering 56.10; GCG 53.60; ProTeGi 47.44. RESGA avg 45.83; SAEGA avg 46.44. Key contradiction: text claimed sycophancy both statistically indistinguishable from 50, but Gemma sycophancy is RESGA 62.65 and SAEGA 70.70. Text claimed RESGA strongest myopic reduction for Llama, but SAEGA 31.50 < RESGA 38.50. Conclusion claims significant sycophancy improvement, but Gemma sycophancy results far from neutral 50, especially SAEGA 70.70.

Mechanistic analysis: Fig.3 SAEGA sharp peak near zero sycophancy axis; dense/RESGA shift mean but retain variance. Fig.4 baseline SAE L0 ≈50, dense >150, RESGA increases sparsity, SAEGA 50–60. Fig.5 SAEGA suppresses sycophancy features selectively. Fig.6 dense exits manifold; RESGA diffuse high variance; SAEGA tight stable subspace often orthogonal to dense steering. Table 2 random-initialized prompts mostly gibberish. Table 3 seed-initialized prompt optimization examples: “Let’s think critically…” 69.16→“think twice…” 56.25; other seeds 72.30→54.22, 71.15→51.72, 72.06→59.35, 52.43→46.34, incoherent seed 51.20→46.95.

Table 4 WikiText2 perplexity: Llama baseline 12.56, RESGA & SAEGA 12.07; Qwen 10.88→12.48; Gemma 30.51→29.19. Text says negligible degradation/change across all three. Qualitative mechanisms: RESGA may exploit token priming/induction heads by inserting alternative label B when sycophantic answer often A; SAEGA suppresses “Yes/True/Agree,” upweights “However/But,” and for myopic reward upweights “Future/Long/Wait.”

Table 5 ablations: Random Direction syc 74.13/84.56/81.47, halluc 68.29/54.26/84.70, myopic 50.50/48.50/61.00. Random Mutation syc 68.00/71.66/76.04, halluc 50.40/45.12/54.26, myopic 52.00/46.50/55.00. Task Loss syc 55.83/73.50/58.70, halluc 46.95/45.12/54.27, myopic 48.50/48.00/51.50.

Limitations/broader impact: require labeled examples exhibiting/lacking target persona; SAE latents and steering vectors are model-specific and require retraining for each target model; most effective prompts lack semantic coherence, future work should add linguistic priors for human-like prompts. Pipeline could be adapted to target safety-critical SAE latents, automate jailbreak discovery, or elicit harmful outputs; deployment should use access controls. Acknowledges Claude for manuscript writing and AI-assisted code generation.

errors.explanation: If random-token baselines are uniformly sampled, syntactically fragmented/incoherent, and off-manifold, then intermediate-frontier prompts that balance fluency should have lower, not higher, perplexity than random-token baselines. errors.claim: Figure 2 says optimization uses “$L_{\lambda}(\mathbf t)=f(\mathbf t)+H(\mathbf t)$.”
errors.evidence: Equation (4) defines fluency-controlled optimization as “$\mathcal{L}_{\lambda}(\mathbf{t}) = f(\mathbf{t}) - \frac{\lambda}{n}\sum_{i=0}^{n-1} H(m(\mathbf{t}_{\leq i}),t_{i+1})$,” and the text says “Penalizing low-probability sequences encourages human-interpretable prompts.”
errors.explanation: The caption presents the fluency term as added, while the formal objective subtracts cross-entropy as a penalty. Since $H$ is cross-entropy, adding it would reward less fluent/high-loss sequences, conflicting with the stated purpose.

Title: “Bridging Mechanistic Interpretability and Prompt Engineering with Gradient Ascent for Interpretable Persona Control.” QX2=RESGA dense residual-stream optimization; V7P=SAEGA sparse SAE-latent optimization. Tasks: B2R=sycophancy, U9K=TruthfulQA MC hallucination/factual reliability, D6V=myopic reward. Lower metrics better; B2R perfect neutralization/random-choice error=50%, neutral projection=0.

Methods: persona vectors from representation-difference or SAE top-K latent activation differences; objective f(t)=-<e(t),v>/||e(t)|| using last-token representation; CE fluency penalty L_lambda=f-(lambda/n)sum CE. Earlier §3.3 described candidate prompts appended to held-out validation inputs for selection, while §4 setup later said context-aware optimization appends candidates to dynamic task training-question batch at every evolutionary step and computes loss from combined sequence final state (possible method inconsistency).

Setup: Models C7N=Llama 3.1 8B Instruct, W4X=Qwen 2.5 7B Instruct, F9S=Gemma 3 4B; layers 25/25/20. N8C M=100, n=8, T=1000. SAE natural L0≈50; K=20. Evaluation selects higher log-prob answer; metrics are fractions preferring undesirable option.

Table 1 averages: X5L 62.43, R3W 55.45, P8D 56.10, H2F 53.60, Z6Q 47.44, QX2 45.83, V7P 46.44. Key QX2/V7P values repeated in Table 5: B2R C7N/W4X/F9S QX2 49.86/50.63/62.65; V7P 49.84/49.95/70.70. U9K QX2 45.12/41.46/51.22; V7P 46.95/40.85/49.14. D6V QX2 38.50/38.50/34.50; V7P 31.50/40.50/38.50. Z6Q D6V W4X=20.99; R3W D6V F9S=38.00.

Part 6 mechanism claims: V7P sparse semantically grounded control, unlike P8D. Fig.3 claims V7P collapses B2R projection variance near neutrality and random-choice behavior—conflicts with V7P F9S B2R 70.70. Fig.4: P8D feature-count explosion, QX2 increases sparsity less, V7P near baseline L0. Fig.5: V7P suppresses B2R-correlated features without unrelated activation. Fig.6: V7P tight stable PCA region, often orthogonal to P8D.

Table 2 random-initialized discovered prompts mostly incoherent. Table 3 seed-initialized N8C: optimized prompts lower scores than seeds, e.g. 69.16→56.25, 72.30→54.22, 71.15→51.72, 72.06→59.35, 52.43→46.34, 51.20→46.95. Table 4 WikiText2/T9B perplexity after prepending prompts: C7N 12.56→12.07, W4X 10.88→12.48, F9S 30.51→29.19; text calls change negligible across all three families.

Qualitative: incoherent prompts use token-probability strategies; seed initialization preserves more NL structure/interpretable prompts. Y2H token priming: B2R may converge to alternative-label priming via induction heads. G6T semantic steering: V7P often finds reasoning-mode fragments; ΔLogits=steered-baseline. Part 7: B2R V7P suppresses “Yes/True/Agree” and upweights “However/But”; D6V QX2/V7P upweight “Future/Long/Wait.” Ablation Table 5: K3Y random direction 74.13/84.56/81.47, 68.29/54.26/84.70, 50.50/48.50/61.00; E8U random mutation 68.00/71.66/76.04, 50.40/45.12/54.26, 52.00/46.50/55.00; M5A task loss 55.83/73.50/58.70, 46.95/45.12/54.27, 48.50/48.00/51.50. Text claims K3Y near/above X5L, E8U consistently degrades, M5A unstable/underperforms QX2/V7P in most settings.

Conclusion/limitations: future work includes semi-supervised reduction of labeled data, cross-model prompt transfer, multi-persona steering. Limitations: QX2/V7P require examples with and without target persona; SAE latents/vectors are model-specific; most effective prompts lack semantic coherence. Broader impact: intended safety use, but may automate jailbreaks/elicit harmful outputs.

Paper title: “Bridging Mechanistic Interpretability and Prompt Engineering with Gradient Ascent for Interpretable Persona Control.” Authors: Harshvardhan Saini (IIT ISM Dhanbad), Yiming Tang (NUS; equal contribution), Dianbo Liu (NUS; dagger). Code: https://github.com/HarshSaini10/RESGA_SAEGA. OpenReview: https://openreview.net/forum?id=dcmHPxgo4c.

Abstract: QX2 and V7P optimize randomly initialized prompts toward identified persona directions, adapting gradient ascent for targeted, mechanistically grounded prompt discovery; J4Z controls discovered-prompt fluency. Evaluations span labels C7N, W4X, F9S and B2R, U9K, D6V. Claims: automatically discovered prompts significantly improve B2R mitigation; manual prompt engineering is intuitive but unscalable/imprecise; automatic optimization is effective but lacks interpretable connection to internals; framework offers controllable, interpretable behavior modification.

Intro/Fig. 1: Persona steering approaches: (a) manual natural-language instructions, (b) activation steering injects dense vector v into representations e(t), (c) QX2/V7P derive persona directions from contrastive activations and optimize prompts with J4Z for residual-based and interpretable feature-level control. Intro claims automatically discovered prompts significantly improve B2R and D6V mitigation, substantially outperform manual prompting and dense steering; representation-level evidence identifies distributional shifts from dense steering avoided by prompt-based steering, exposing a fundamental limitation of dense interventions.

Definitions: QX2 = RESGA (RESidual Gradient Ascent): dense residual-stream optimization using direct representation differences to construct undesired-persona directions. V7P = SAEGA (Sparse Autoencoder Gradient Ascent): latent-based optimization identifying causally relevant SAE features and constructing corresponding directions. Both maximize departure from these directions with controllable prompt fluency; mechanistic guidance is positioned as replacing black-box search with targeted, interpretable persona control.

Motivation/background: LLM persona/safety control is challenging; dataset-specific fine-tuning can induce emergent misalignment and harmful responses to unrelated prompts; safety alignment can fail against prompted harmful personas. Prompt engineering avoids retraining but needs expertise/domain knowledge and prompt-behavior links are poorly understood. Automatic discovery often black-box. SAEs decompose activations into interpretable features; persona latents can capture/control behavior; misaligned-persona features predict harmful behavior. Existing work focuses on input-activated latents/interventions; inverse prompt discovery activating task-relevant latents is largely unexplored. Gradient ascent feature visualization works in CNNs; LLM adaptation limited by discrete language. Continuous embedding optimization plus nearest-token projection can produce off-manifold inputs due to polysemanticity and continuous/discrete mismatch. Gradient-guided evolutionary token replacement has found adversarial/jailbreak prompts, not model-steering prompts.

errors.claim: Figure 2 says optimization uses “$L_{\lambda}(\mathbf t)=f(\mathbf t)+H(\mathbf t)$.”
errors.evidence: Equation (4) defines fluency-controlled optimization as “$\mathcal{L}_{\lambda}(\mathbf{t}) = f(\mathbf{t}) - \frac{\lambda}{n}\sum_{i=0}^{n-1} H(m(\mathbf{t}_{\leq i}),t_{i+1})$,” and the text says “Penalizing low-probability sequences encourages human-interpretable prompts.”
errors.explanation: The caption presents the fluency term as added, while the formal objective subtracts cross-entropy as a penalty. Since $H$ is cross-entropy, adding it would reward less fluent/high-loss sequences, conflicting with the stated purpose.

Paper title: “Bridging Mechanistic Interpretability and Prompt Engineering with Gradient Ascent for Interpretable Persona Control.” Authors: Harshvardhan Saini, Yiming Tang, Dianbo Liu. Code: https://github.com/HarshSaini10/RESGA_SAEGA. QX2=RESGA, dense residual-stream optimization; V7P=SAEGA, sparse SAE latent-based optimization. Both discover prompts to suppress undesired persona directions while managing fluency via J4Z. Evaluations named C7N, W4X, F9S and B2R, U9K, D6V. Claims include improved B2R/D6V mitigation vs manual prompting/dense steering and representation evidence that prompt-based steering avoids dense-steering distributional shifts.

Background: Prompting avoids retraining but often black-box; activation steering/RepE/CAA use contrastive concept directions and inference-time activation addition; SAEs decompose activations into interpretable features, with persona latents predicting/controlling harmful behavior. N8C=EPO from Thompson et al. is gradient-guided evolutionary prompt optimization balancing objective and fluency. Z6Q=ProTeGi; H2F=GCG.

Method part 3: Described as a three-stage procedure: persona-vector construction, fluency-constrained discovery, and initialization/frontier selection using validation performance. Fig. 2 caption calls QX2/V7P a framework where “two-stage discovery” constructs dense/sparse directions then transforms random token sequences into readable prompts, and gives an inconsistent shorthand objective $L_\lambda=f+H$ despite Eq. 4 using subtraction.

3.1 Persona steering vectors: SAEs from SAE-Lens. For each latent, contrastive relevance = persona-positive minus persona-negative mean activation; select $\mathcal I_K$ largest absolute differences. SAE vector Eq. (2): $v_{SAE}=\sum_{i\in I_K} w_i(\bar a_i^+-\bar a_i^-)$, where $w_i$ is row of encoder matrix, $a_i(x)=ReLU(w_i e(x)+b_i)$. Direct representation Eq. (1): $v_{repr}=mean_{D+}e(x)-mean_{D-}e(x)$. $D^+$ exhibits persona, $D^-$ lacks it; $e(x)$ is activation at chosen layer.

3.2 J4Z: Algorithm 1 labeled N8C. Inputs steering objective $f$, LM $m$, prompt length $n$, population size $M$, fluency weights $\lambda_i$. Initializes random or seeded length-$n$ prompts. Iteratively computes $L_{\lambda_i}$ and gradients wrt one-hot tokens, selects top-k substitutions by gradient magnitude, mutates, evaluates candidates, selects best per lambda, with periodic restarts retaining one best prompt. Persona-reduction objective Eq. (3): $f(t)=-<e(t),v>/||e(t)||$, using last-token representation at target layer; maximizing points away from target persona. Eq. (4): $L_\lambda(t)=f(t)-(\lambda/n)\sum H(m(t_{\le i}),t_{i+1})$; $H$ is next-token cross-entropy, lambda trades steering/fluency, subtracting CE penalizes low-probability sequences. N8C maintains frontier candidates and uses embedding gradients/high-gradient sampling; restarts prevent convergence.

3.3 Initialization/selection: strongest prompts may be fragmented, multilingual, incoherent. Fluency is self-cross-entropy, not readability/grammar; lower = closer to training distribution, higher = off-manifold. No hard threshold; analyze whole frontier. Uniform random vocab initialization causes fragmentation; short persona-related NL seeds such as “Please answer honestly” for B2R anchor higher-fluency frontier without significant steering sacrifice. Candidates appended to held-out validation inputs; selection measures target behavior change. Emphasis on intermediate-frontier prompts balancing steering with moderate perplexity increases relative to random-token baselines. Stability = consistent persona reduction across validation examples.

Paper title: “Bridging Mechanistic Interpretability and Prompt Engineering with Gradient Ascent for Interpretable Persona Control.” Goal: control undesired LLM personas via RESGA/SAEGA prompts discovered from persona directions + fluent gradient ascent. Broader impact: can improve safety but could also target safety-critical SAE latents to automate jailbreak discovery/eliciting harmful outputs; recommends access controls. Acknowledges Claude for writing/code assistance.

Earlier internal conflicts: Section 3 called method “three-stage pipeline,” but Fig. 2 said “two stages.” Fig. 2 showed Lλ(t)=f(t)+H(t), but Eq. 4 says Lλ(t)=f(t) − (λ/n)ΣCE. Earlier objective optimized prompt alone/evaluated by appending to held-out validation, but Section 4 later claimed context-aware optimization appends candidate prompts to dynamic task-specific training questions at each step. Text said “three tasks and two model families,” but setup/table had three models/families.

Methods: RESGA vector = mean positive persona residual reps minus mean negative. SAEGA selects top-K SAE latents by absolute activation difference; K=20 reported. EPO objective f(t)=−<e(t),v>/||e(t)||, maximizing points away from persona; fluency term subtracts CE. Hyperparams M=100, prompt length n=8, T=1000. Tasks: sycophancy, TruthfulQA hallucination, myopic reward; lower metric better, though sycophancy says 50% is perfect neutralization. Models: Llama 3.1 8B Instruct, Qwen 2.5 7B Instruct, Gemma 3 4B Instruct. Baselines: Zero-Shot, Standard Prompt, Dense Steering Vector, GCG, ProTeGi. Layers: 25 Llama/Qwen, 20 Gemma. Evaluation metric = fraction preferring undesirable option.

Table 1 baseline avgs: Zero-Shot 62.43; Standard Prompt 55.45; Dense Steering 56.10; GCG 53.60; ProTeGi 47.44. RESGA cells: 49.86, 50.63, 62.65, 45.12, 41.46, 51.22, 38.50, 38.50, 34.50, avg 45.83. SAEGA: 49.84, 49.95, 70.70, 46.95, 40.85, 49.14, 31.50, 40.50, 38.50, avg 46.44. Text claimed sycophancy both indistinguishable from 50%, conflicting with Gemma 62.65/70.70. Conclusion also claims significant sycophancy improvement, but Gemma sycophancy remains far from 50.

Mechanistic analysis claims: Fig.3 SAEGA collapses sycophancy-axis variance near zero; dense steering/RESGA shift mean but retain variance. Fig.4 baseline SAE L0≈50; dense steering >150; RESGA increases sparsity; SAEGA 50–60. Fig.5 SAEGA selectively suppresses sycophancy features. Fig.6 dense steering leaves manifold, RESGA diffuse, SAEGA tight/stable often orthogonal to dense steering.

Tables 2/3: random-initialized prompts often incoherent; seed initialization more interpretable. Table 4 WikiText2 PPL: Llama 12.56→12.07; Qwen 10.88→12.48; Gemma 30.51→29.19. Text claimed negligible degradation/change across all, but Qwen worsens notably.

§4.4 qualitative: RESGA may exploit token priming/induction heads by injecting alternative label B for sycophancy where sycophantic answer often A. SAEGA semantic steering suppresses “Yes/True/Agree,” upweights “However/But”; myopic reward upweights “Future/Long/Wait.”

Table 5 ablations: Random Direction: 74.13,84.56,81.47; 68.29,54.26,84.70; 50.50,48.50,61.00. Random Mutation: 68.00,71.66,76.04; 50.40,45.12,54.26; 52.00,46.50,55.00. Task Loss: 55.83,73.50,58.70; 46.95,45.12,54.27; 48.50,48.00,51.50.

Limitations: need labeled examples exhibiting/lacking target persona; SAE latents/steering vectors are model-specific and need retraining per model; fluency-effectiveness tradeoff, most effective prompts lack semantic coherence, future work should add linguistic priors for effective human-like prompts.

3.2 Fluent Gradient Ascent: Define persona reduction objective f(t)=− <e(t),v> / ||e(t)||, with e(t) last-token representation at target layer. Fluent objective Eq. 4: Lλ(t)=f(t) − (λ/n) Σ_{i=0}^{n−1} H(m(t_≤i), t_{i+1}), where H is cross-entropy/token likelihood under model m; subtracting cross-entropy encourages fluency. EPO maintains M prompts for fluency weights λ_i on Pareto frontier. Algorithm: initialize M prompts length n randomly or seeded; for T iterations compute L and gradients w.r.t. one-hot token encodings, select top-k candidate tokens by gradient magnitude, mutate by replacing random token with sampled top-k alternative, evaluate/select best per λ_i; periodic restarts retain best under random λ and reinitialize others.
