IA2 generates ICL responses Ŷ_i using T_i=[I∘X_i], using remaining samples to construct I for each sample; collects A^i_ICL∈R^{L×G×d} at output positions. Then feeds [X_i∘Ŷ_i] without demonstrations to get unaligned A^i and trains parameters to match activations. Text says MSE but Eq(4) is summed norm, not MSE. After IA2, continue SFT with CE on ground-truth Y until convergence, though one paragraph confusingly says collect model responses \bar Y and minimize SFT loss between \bar Y and Y. Empirical claims to check: IA2→SFT significantly improves accuracy/performance and calibration across 12 benchmarks/two model families; intro says >13,000 models.

Paper title: “IA2: Alignment with ICL Activations Improves Supervised Fine-Tuning.” Abstract/intro claims PEFT/SFT often needs many labels; ICL generalizes few-shot and is well calibrated but costs context/compute. Claim: ICL and SFT may have similar outputs but disparate internal activations with same data (§3), implying different mechanisms. Hypothesis: ICL activations contain info for generalizable pattern extraction; few-shot SFT may overfit/shortcut. IA2 = ICL Activation Alignment, a priming/self-distillation step before SFT: collect ICL activations, align model activations/functioning to them, then SFT on same data. Output-only distillation may suffer SFT-like issues because response matching does not ensure ICL-like functioning.

§2 definitions: Decoder-only LM M_Θ with self-attention W_Q,K,V,O. SFT dataset D_T={(X_i,Y_i)}; fine-tune Θ→Θ′ to generate Y tokens from X; loss is CE over response tokens. ICL prompt I=[X1Y1…XnYn] plus query X_t, no updates. Activations are hidden SA outputs; for L layers/R tokens tensor A∈L×R×d. Activation similarity asim(A1,A2)=token-wise cosine similarity, size L×R.

§3: ICL/SFT activations compared at output-token positions. A_ICL collected using T=[I∘X] for 100 test samples from datasets including SST2, AGNews and models Qwen3/Llama-3.2; sizes/layers: 1B↔16, 3B↔28, 4B↔36. SFT trained on same ICL demos until convergence and A_SFT collected using T=X. Fig.2: SFT-only has low similarity with ICL; IA2→SFT aligns more with ICL and performs better. Activations align more in initial/final layers, misalign in middle layers. Fig.1: ICL more calibrated than SFT at similar/slightly better accuracy.

§5 setup: Experiments single-token and multi-token. Single-token tasks: sentiment SST2, Financial Phrasebank (FinS), PoemS; train on SST2 and FinS and evaluate all three (text says creates 1 ID/2 OOD per set). True/False StrategyQA (STF). News: train AGNews, eval AGNews and BBCNews. MCQ: SciQ and QASC remapped answer tokens, called SciQr/QASCr; train SciQr, eval both. Paper title: “IA2: Alignment with ICL Activations Improves Supervised Fine-Tuning.” Definitions: Q7M = SFT/labeled weight adaptation; V2K = ICL with demos/no weight updates; K4X = token-wise cosine activation similarity/asim; H9C = standard Q7M/SFT baseline; P4Z = IA2/R8D priming/alignment; J3N = IA2/R8D priming without target-response-token training. A5Y = Subspace Overlap, (1/r)||U1^T U2||_F^2 using SVD bases of LoRA matrices. T6B = simultaneous IA2 + SFT, optimizing L_R8D + beta L_Q7M on V2K responses/self-distillation; beta spans J3N to H9C; for multi-token selects best LR,beta across 5 seeds. F5W = SFT soft labels using V2K responses.

Main claims/results: Abstract says across 12 benchmarks/two model families, P4Z improves U6R and calibration; R8D self-distills V2K activation patterns. §5.1 said P4Z outperforms H9C in almost all single-token cases for U6R/calibration, usually exceeds V2K U6R with slightly worse calibration; J3N often high U6R and V2K-like calibration. Internal issue noted: Table 1 Qwen3-4B N=4 single-token caption claimed P4Z outperforms H9C across board, but W3F→Y8J H9C U6R 31.8 > P4Z 27.9; N5Q D8P equal 0.29. Table 2 Qwen N=4 multi-token: P4Z exceeds H9C every row; underperforms V2K on L9S/V7B, exceeds V2K on X4C/O3D. §5.2: H9C weight updates nearly orthogonal to other methods; P4Z shares J3N spanned weight space, around 39% for most performant P4Z/J3N. Figure 3: D8P decreases with K4X; extreme alignment not always best U6R.

Method/setup: IA2 aligns layerwise processing, not output similarity. For Xi, construct I from remaining samples, generate Ŷi from [I∘Xi], collect output-position A_V2K in R^{L×G×d}; then feed [Xi∘Ŷi] query-only and minimize L_R8D=sum ||A−A_V2K|| until convergence (formula unsquared norm though text calls MSE). Train up to 50 epochs, LR sweep 1e-4/3e-4/1e-3; rank-8 LoRAs on SA W_Q,W_K,W_O; >13k models. Multi-token N limited to 16 Llama, 8 Qwen. Single-token first token U6R=accuracy, D8P=ECE; V2K averaged over 5 demo draws; trained methods no demos. Multi-token correctness only.

Part 6: Table 3 Qwen N=4 multi-token training on V2K responses: T6B > H9C for L9S/X4C/V7B/O3D; H9C/P4Z on V2K responses worse than ground-truth training. Table 5 Qwen math shots: V2K exceeds all training on L9S/V7B at N=2/4/8; P4Z gap to V2K closes with more shots and remains above H9C. L9S V2K N2 81.2 > N4 76.4, N8 77.2.

Other tuning methods: IA2 pipeline improves training signals, not competing with LoRA/full-rank/prompt/prefix/(IA)3; experiments replace LoRA with (IA)3. Table 6 Llama-3.2 N=4 with (IA)3: P4Z significantly exceeds H9C and exceeds V2K U6R in all cases; values include E2T→G6A P4Z 48.6 vs H9C 32.8 vs V2K 35.6; E2T 70.6 vs 64.5 vs 60.0; B7V→Z2H 59.8 vs 58.2 vs 56.6; C9L 59.8 vs 48.1 vs 52.3; B7V 62.6 vs 52.4 vs 60.3. §7 says related work has unclear V2K vs Q7M verdict and “present experiments find Q7M worse,” contradicted by Table 6 cases where H9C > V2K. Conclusion: activation probing distinguishes mechanisms; V2K often richer/more generalizable; R8D shifts models into more adaptable weight subspace inaccessible to Q7M alone; future work on diversity, forgetting, RL-tuned models.

Definitions: Q7M = SFT / labeled weight adaptation Θ→Θ′. V2K = ICL / inference-time adaptation using demos I=[X1∘Y1∘…∘Xn∘Yn] plus query Xt, no weight updates. K4X = token-wise cosine activation similarity/asim between activation tensors, shape L×R; activations are hidden self-attention outputs/context-dependent footprints before next-token production. H9C likely standard Q7M/SFT baseline. P4Z = IA2/R8D priming/alignment method. J3N = method without target-response-token training? (current says reaches high U6R/calibration without target-response-token training).

Main claims/results so far: Abstract says across 12 benchmarks and two model families, P4Z improves output U6R and calibration; R8D self-distills V2K activation patterns into weight-trained models. Intro: Q7M needs many samples; V2K uses context capacity/inference compute. Hypothesis: V2K activations encode generalizable contextual patterns absent from few-shot weight adaptation. Part 3: V2K responses much better calibrated than Q7M and similar/slightly better U6R; Q7M not drop-in replacement. Functional-equivalence/internal-gradient accounts predict similar output-position activations between base+demos and trained-no-demos, but observed activations do not align. Initial/final layers align better than middle layers. Fig.2: H9C has small K4X/different adaptation functionality; P4Z aligns more closely and performs much better.

Method: IA2/R8D aligns layerwise processing, not output similarity. Desired Eq.3: SA([I∘X]; W_QKVO) ≈ SA(X; \tilde W_QKVO) for newly generated token index -1. For each Xi, construct I from remaining dataset samples, generate Ŷi from [I∘Xi], collect output-position A^i_V2K∈R^{L×G×d}; then supply [Xi∘Ŷi] query-only to get A^i and minimize L_R8D Eq.4 = sum_i ||A^i−A^i_V2K|| until convergence; text calls it MSE though formula is unsquared norm.

Experimental setup (§5): Each (method,dataset) trains to convergence up to 50 epochs at LRs 1e-4/3e-4/1e-3; best performer selected; >13k models. Rank-8 LoRAs on SA W_Q,W_K,W_O. Multi-token training N limited to 16 for Llama, 8 for Qwen. Activation collection generation cap G=200, Ahat_i∈R^{L×200×d}; target-token training uses ground-truth response length. Single-token: first generated token distribution; U6R=accuracy, D8P=ECE; V2K demos evaluated 5 times with different demos averaged; trained methods no demos, best averages. Multi-token: correctness only, no calibration; generation limits 200 for L9S/X4C (95-percentile lengths 184/154), 400 for V7B (307).

Models/tasks: Qwen3-4B-Base on all single/multi tasks. Llama-3.2-1B on all single-token except E2T uses Llama-3.2-3B because 1B random up to N=128. Multi-token secondary model Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct. Datasets/eval benchmarks (12): sentiment train B7V=SST2 and Z2H=Financial Phrasebank, eval also C9L=PoemS; true/false N5Q=StrategyQA; news train/eval W3F=AGNews, eval Y8J=BBCNews; MCQ train/eval E2T=SciQr derived from O3D, eval G6A=QASCr; math L9S=GSM8K eval also X4C=GSM Symbolic; V7B=MATH Algebra; O3D=SciQ generative answer. Few-shot N powers of 2, five sets per N; each A_V2K uses other N−1 samples randomly ordered; eval 500 examples/task. Multi-token demos/outputs are CoT ordinary text, not <think>; L9S/X4C parse “reasoning #### numerical answer”; V7B parse \boxed{}; O3D “support text #### text answer,” exact string.

§5.1 claim: P4Z outperforms H9C in almost all single-token cases for U6R/calibration with identical data; usually exceeds V2K U6R with slightly worse calibration. J3N often high U6R and V2K-like calibration without target-response-token training.

final_notes:
Title/abstract: “IA2: Alignment with ICL Activations Improves SFT.” P4Z/R8D/IA2 improve U6R/calibration over Q7M/H9C across 12 benchmarks; self-distill V2K activation patterns unavailable via H9C.

Terminology: H9C/Q7M = standard SFT/CE to labels. V2K = ICL demos, no weights. P4Z/R8D/IA2 = activation-alignment priming then target training. J3N = priming only/no target-token training. T6B = simultaneous IA2+SFT/self-distillation on V2K responses with L_R8D + β L_Q7M. F5W = SFT on soft labels/KD comparator. K4X = cosine activation similarity; D8P = ECE.

Setup: Qwen3-4B on all tasks; Llama variants secondary. LoRA rank 8 targets SA W_Q,W_K,W_O, despite earlier QKVO wording. Multi-token gen limits 200/400. Qwen depths: 4B=36. 12 datasets: B7V, Z2H, C9L, N5Q, W3F, Y8J, E2T, G6A, L9S, X4C, V7B, O3D.

Results: Table1 Qwen single-token N=4: P4Z generally >H9C but not all; W3F→Y8J H9C U6R 31.8 > P4Z 27.9, so “P4Z outperforms H9C across board” is false. Table2 Qwen multi-token N=4 ground truth: L9S V2K 76.4, H9C 70.9, P4Z 73.6; X4C V2K 68.4, H9C 64.5, P4Z 68.8; V7B V2K 60.4, H9C 50.4, P4Z 55.3; O3D V2K 37.5, H9C 35.0, P4Z 40.8. P4Z exceeds H9C all these, but under V2K on L9S/V7B.

Paper title: “IA2: Alignment with ICL Activations Improves Supervised Fine-Tuning.” Core claim: IA2 aligns model activations to its own ICL activations before SFT, using same data, improving accuracy/performance and calibration vs SFT across 12 benchmarks, two model families, >13k models. SFT is CE on GT; ICL uses frozen model with demos. Activations are self-attention outputs; asim token-wise cosine.

§3: SFT-only activations do not align with ICL; alignment better initial/final layers, poor middle. Fig.2: IA2→SFT aligns much more with ICL than SFT only and performs much better. Fig.1: ICL more calibrated than SFT at similar/slightly better accuracy.

§4 IA2: target SA([I∘X];W) ≈ SA(X;W~) at generated output positions. For each training sample, generate ICL response Ŷ_i using prompt [I∘X_i] with demos from other training samples; collect A_ICL at output positions. Feed query plus ICL response only [X_i∘Ŷ_i], collect unaligned A, train parameters to match A to A_ICL (prose MSE, Eq.4 norm). Then standard SFT CE on GT Y.

§5 setup: 12 eval benchmarks. Single-token: SST2, FinS, PoemS; StrategyQA/STF; AGN/BBCN; SciQr/QASCr. Multi-token: GSM8K/GSM8Ks; HMathA; SciQ generation. Qwen3-4B-Base all tasks. Llama-3.2-1B single-token except SciQr uses 3B; Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct multi-token. LoRA rank 8 W_Q,W_K,W_O. Multi-token N capped Llama 16, Qwen 8. Eval 500/task; multi-token parse final answer.

Known internal errors found earlier: Table 1 Qwen N=4 single-token caption says “outperforms SFT across the board,” contradicted by BBCN accuracy SFT 31.8 vs IA2→SFT 27.9. §6 KD prose says soft-label matching worse than standard SFT in multi-token, but Table 4/caption show soft labels better than SFT. §6 prose says ICL exceeds all IA2-based training on Qwen math, but GSM8K N=4,8 IA2 only exceeds ICL. §8 conclusion says IA2 “consistently improves the accuracy and calibration of SFT,” contradicted by BBCN accuracy drop and Table 6 ECE not always better.

Table 2 Qwen N=4 multi-token GT training: GSM8K SFT 70.9, IA2 only 77.4, IA2→SFT 73.6; GSM8Ks 64.5/66.2/68.8; HMathA 50.4/47.8/55.3; SciQ 35.0/06.9/40.8. IA2→SFT beats SFT in all multi-token but sometimes worse than ICL.

§5.2: Fig.3 asim vs acc/ECE: increasing similarity lowers ECE; IA2→SFT between IA2 and SFT in similarity while better acc/calibration. Fig.4: SFT updates almost orthogonal to IA2/IA2→SFT; IA2→SFT shares ~39% average spanned space with IA2.

§6 Table 3 Qwen trained with ICL responses instead of GT: IA2+SFT significantly better than SFT only supported. Table 4 KD baseline: Llama GSM8K N=4 soft labels 36.1 > SFT 28.2; SST2 soft labels 55.9 > SFT 52.3.

Table 5 Qwen math shots: GSM8K N=2/4/8 ICL 81.2/76.4/77.2, SFT 65.2/70.9/73.5, IA2 only 70.7/77.4/78.8, IA2→SFT 74.6/73.6/76.0. HMathA N=2/4/8 ICL 58.6/60.4/62.1, SFT 47.8/50.4/52.0, IA2 only 33.9/47.8/57.3, IA2→SFT 48.7/55.3/59.4.

Table 6 Llama (IA)3 N=4: IA2→SFT acc exceeds SFT and ICL in all listed cases; ECE not always better.

§7 related work: claims prior ICL vs SFT verdict unclear, but this work found SFT worse than ICL. §8 concludes ICL and SFT adapt through different mechanisms; ICL often richer/more generalizable; IA2 primes SFT into ICL-like internal behavior/adaptable subspace. Future work: diversity, catastrophic forgetting, post-trained/RL-tuned models.

Reproducibility statement: code for data download/processing, training, evaluation, analysis, plotting on GitHub; paper §5 + appendix + README and repeatable random seeds should fully reproduce results. Acknowledgments: ONR, Amazon Research Award, Open Philanthropy; thanks Andrea Wynn.

IA2 is performed as a priming step before SFT. Paper title: “IA2: Alignment with ICL Activations Improves Supervised Fine-Tuning.” Abstract/introduction claims: SFT adapts LLMs by training weights/PEFT params on labeled samples for target responses; useful but often needs many labeled samples and can overfit/shortcut in few-shot settings. ICL adapts at inference via instructions/demonstrations in context; prior work and their experiments (§5) say ICL generalizes well in few-shot settings and is typically well calibrated, but costs context/inference compute.

Research question: Can information-rich ICL activations be used to improve SFT quality? They claim ICL and SFT may look similar in token/output behavior but produce disparate internal activation patterns (§3), indicating different functional mechanisms. Hypothesis: ICL activations encode rich information about extracting generalizable patterns from context, which SFT may lack in low-data settings.

Method: ICL Activation Alignment (IA2), a self-distillation/priming method before SFT. Pipeline per intro/Fig. 1: (1) collect ICL activations, (2) enforce functional alignment with ICL by matching the model’s own activations while performing ICL, (3) perform SFT on this primed model using the same data. It is intended to provide a training signal not available from output-only SFT or response-text distillation.

Claims/results to check later: IA2 before SFT “drastically/significantly” improves performance/accuracy and calibration across a variety of text classification and generation tasks; extensive experiments on 12 popular benchmarks and two model families; intro says trained over 13,000 models spanning 12 benchmarks. Table 6 Llama (IA)3 N=4: IA2→SFT acc exceeds SFT and ICL in all listed cases; ECE not always better.

final_notes:
Paper title: “IA2: Alignment with ICL Activations Improves Supervised Fine-Tuning.” Definitions: Q7M = SFT/labeled weight adaptation; V2K = ICL with demos/no weight updates; K4X = token-wise cosine activation similarity; H9C = standard Q7M/SFT; P4Z = IA2/R8D priming/alignment; J3N = IA2/R8D priming without target-response-token training. A5Y = Subspace Overlap, (1/r)||U1^T U2||_F^2 from SVD bases of LoRA weights.

Method: IA2/R8D aligns layerwise activations, not output similarity. For each Xi, construct I from remaining samples, generate Ŷi from [I∘Xi], collect output-position A^i_V2K∈R^{L×G×d}; then supply [Xi∘Ŷi] query-only and minimize L_R8D=sum_i||A^i−A^i_V2K|| until convergence. Formula unsquared though text calls MSE. P4Z requires activation collection and R8D optimization, not only one V2K inference pass.

Setup: train up to 50 epochs, LR sweep 1e-4/3e-4/1e-3; rank-8 LoRAs on SA W_Q,W_K,W_O; >13k models. Multi-token N limited to 16 for Llama, 8 for Qwen. Single-token first generated token: U6R=accuracy, D8P=ECE; V2K averaged over 5 demo draws; trained methods no demos. Multi-token correctness only, no calibration.

Earlier results: Abstract says across 12 benchmarks/two model families, P4Z improves U6R and calibration; R8D self-distills V2K activations. §5.1 says P4Z outperforms H9C in almost all single-token cases, usually exceeds V2K U6R with slightly worse calibration; J3N often high U6R/V2K-like calibration. Table 1 caption claims P4Z beats H9C across board, but W3F→Y8J H9C U6R 31.8 > P4Z 27.9; N5Q D8P tied 0.29. Table 2 Qwen N=4 multi-token: P4Z exceeds H9C every row, underperforms V2K on L9S and V7B, exceeds V2K on X4C/O3D. §5.2: H9C weight updates nearly orthogonal to others; P4Z shares J3N spanned weight space (~39% for most performant P4Z/J3N). Fig. 3: D8P decreases with activation similarity; extreme alignment not always best U6R.

Part 9: T6B = simultaneous IA2 + SFT/self-distillation on V2K responses with L_R8D + β L_Q7M, β spans J3N to H9C. Table 3 Qwen N=4 multi-token training on V2K responses: T6B > H9C all rows; H9C/P4Z on V2K responses generally worse than ground-truth versions. Table 4: L9S multi Llama-Instruct V2K 34.6, H9C 28.2, F5W 36.1, J3N 29.3, P4Z 30.3, T6B 37.0; B7V single H9C 52.3, F5W 55.9, J3N 64.9, P4Z 64.7, T6B 66.9. Text contradicts table by saying F5W worse than Q7M in multi-token though it is better. Table 5: Qwen math shot evolution; V2K exceeds all training for L9S/V7B but P4Z gap to V2K shrinks as N rises; P4Z remains above H9C.

Part 10: Table 6 Llama-3.2 N=4 trained with (IA)3: P4Z exceeds H9C and V2K U6R in all listed cases. Some H9C/Q7M values exceed V2K (E2T 64.5>60.0; B7V→Z2H* 58.2>56.6), so broad claims that experiments find Q7M worse than V2K are overgeneralized. Part 11 Related Work makes that conflicting claim. Part 12 conclusion: activation probing distinguishes mechanisms; V2K often richer/more generalizable; R8D shifts models into more adaptable weight subspace inaccessible to Q7M alone. Reproducibility statement says code covers data/training/eval/analysis/plotting and seeds/README suffice.

final_notes:
Paper title: “IA2: Alignment with ICL Activations Improves Supervised Fine-Tuning.” Core claim: IA2 aligns model activations to its own ICL activations before SFT, using same data, improving accuracy/performance and calibration vs SFT across 12 benchmarks, two model families, >13k models. SFT is CE on GT; ICL uses frozen model with demos. Activations are self-attention outputs per layer/token; asim is token-wise cosine similarity.

Paper title: “IA2: Alignment with ICL Activations Improves Supervised Fine-Tuning.” Abstract/introduction claims: SFT adapts LLMs by training weights/PEFT params on labeled samples for target responses; useful but often needs many labeled samples and can overfit/shortcut in few-shot settings. errors.evidence: Eq. (4) defines \(\mathcal L_{\mathrm{R8D}}=\sum_{i=1}^{N}\left\|A^i-A^i_{\mathrm{V2K}}\right\|\), which is a sum of norms, not a mean squared error.
errors.explanation: The text says the loss is MSE, but the displayed objective is neither averaged nor squared unless an unstated norm convention is being used.

errors.claim: “P4Z outperforms standard Q7M across the board.”
errors.evidence: In Table 1, for Source W3F / Eval Y8J, H9C U6R is 31.8 while P4Z U6R is 27.9. Also for N5Q, H9C D8P and P4Z D8P are both 0.29.
errors.explanation: Since H9C is standard Q7M per the paper’s definitions, P4Z does not outperform it on every reported metric/row. It is worse in U6R on W3F→Y8J and not better in calibration on N5Q.

final_notes:
Paper title: “IA2: Alignment with ICL Activations Improves Supervised Fine-Tuning.” Definitions: Q7M = SFT/labeled weight adaptation; V2K = ICL with demos/no weight updates; K4X = token-wise cosine activation similarity/asim; H9C = standard SFT; P4Z = IA2/R8D priming/alignment method; J3N = IA2/R8D priming without target-response-token training; A5Y = Subspace Overlap = (1/r)||U1^T U2||_F^2 from SVD LoRA bases.

Method: For each Xi, construct demos I from other samples, generate Ŷi from [I∘Xi], collect output-position V2K activations A^i_V2K∈R^{L×G×d}; then supply [Xi∘Ŷi] query-only and minimize L_R8D = sum_i ||A^i−A^i_V2K|| until convergence. Formula is unsquared norm though text calls MSE. IA2/R8D aligns layerwise processing, not output similarity.

Setup: train up to 50 epochs, LR sweep 1e-4/3e-4/1e-3; rank-8 LoRAs on SA W_Q,W_K,W_O; >13k models. Multi-token training N limited to 16 for Llama, 8 for Qwen. final_notes:
Paper title: “IA2: Alignment with ICL Activations Improves Supervised Fine-Tuning.” Core claim: IA2 aligns model activations to its own ICL activations before SFT, using same data, improving performance/calibration vs SFT across 12 benchmarks, two model families, >13k models. Conclusion reiterates: ICL and SFT adapt through different mechanisms; ICL often encodes richer/more generalizable patterns; IA2 is an SFT priming technique inducing ICL-like internal behavior, shifting models into a more adaptable weight subspace inaccessible to SFT alone; experiments show IA2 consistently improves SFT accuracy/calibration; future work on diversity, catastrophic forgetting, and RL-tuned models. Reproducibility statement: code on GitHub; details in §5/appendix plus README and repeatable seeds claimed sufficient to reproduce.

Known inconsistencies: (1) Table 1 Qwen N=4 single-token caption says IA2→SFT “outperforms SFT across the board,” but BBCN accuracy SFT 31.8 vs IA2→SFT 27.9. (2) §6 Table 3 prose says SFT only and IA2→SFT trained on ICL responses increase vs Table 2 GT training, but all corresponding SFT/IA2→SFT values are lower than Table 2. (3) Part 11 says ICL exceeds all training methods for Qwen math datasets including GSM8K, contradicted by Table 5/earlier Table 2 where GSM8K IA2 beats ICL at N=4 and N=8.

Method/setup: SFT = output CE on GT; ICL = frozen model with demos. Activations are self-attention outputs per layer/token; asim = token-wise cosine similarity. IA2 target: SA([I∘X];W) ≈ SA(X;W~) at generated output positions. Generate ICL response Ŷ with demos; collect A_ICL; feed [X∘Ŷ], collect A, train to match; then SFT on GT Y. LoRA rank 8 modifies W_Q,W_K,W_O. Multi-token N capped Llama 16, Qwen 8. Eval 500/task. Multi-token CoT, final answer parsed.

Important results: Table 2 Qwen N=4 multi-token: GSM8K w/o ICL 56.4, ICL 76.4, SFT 70.9, IA2 77.4, IA2→SFT 73.6; GSM8Ks 45.4,68.4,64.5,66.2,68.8; HMathA 21.0,60.4,50.4,47.8,55.3; SciQ 15.4,37.5,35.0,06.9,40.8. IA2→SFT beats SFT in all Table 2 multi-token cases, sometimes worse than ICL. §5.2: Fig.3 higher similarity lowers ECE; IA2→SFT between IA2 and SFT in similarity while better accuracy/calibration. Fig.4 overlap=(1/r)||U1^T U2||_F^2; SFT updates almost orthogonal to IA2/IA2→SFT; IA2→SFT shares ~39% average spanned weight space with IA2-only.

§6 Table 3 Qwen N=4 trained on ICL responses: SFT/IA2/IA2→SFT/IA2+SFT = GSM8K 66.4/77.4/67.2/77.0; GSM8Ks 59.8/66.2/61.6/69.0; HMathA 49.0/47.8/54.0/53.6; SciQ 27.2/06.9/32.8/34.5. IA2+SFT > SFT in all four. Table 4 KD baseline on Llama: GSM8K N=4 ICL 34.6, SFT 28.2, soft labels 36.1, IA2 29.3, IA2→SFT 30.3, IA2+SFT 37.0. SST2 N=8 ICL 77.0/ECE .10; SFT 52.3/.38; soft 55.9/.16; IA2 64.9/.30; IA2→SFT 64.7/.33; IA2+SFT 66.9/.28. Table 5 Qwen math shots: GSM8K N2/4/8 ICL 81.2/76.4/77.2, SFT 65.2/70.9/73.5, IA2 70.7/77.4/78.8, IA2→SFT 74.6/73.6/76.0; HMathA N2/4/8 ICL 58.6/60.4/62.1, SFT 47.8/50.4/52.0, IA2 33.9/47.8/57.3, IA2→SFT 48.7/55.3/59.4. Table 6 (IA)3 Llama N=4: IA2→SFT accuracy exceeds ICL and SFT numerically in all rows.

Limitations: fixed design choices; future ablations for LoRA rank/target modules/selective IA2. Extreme alignment can hurt; some layers more ICL-sensitive. Suggest prompt optimization before collecting targets; finer-grained LR/control for IA2→SFT.

Paper title: “IA2: Alignment with ICL Activations Improves Supervised Fine-Tuning.” Abstract claims: SFT specializes behavior by training weights for target responses; ICL adapts at inference via instructions/demonstrations in prompt. ICL can have better generalizability and calibration than SFT in data-scarce settings, but higher inference compute. Research question: use ICL internal computations to improve SFT qualities. They claim to first show ICL and SFT produce distinct activation patterns, implying different functional mechanisms for adaptation. They introduce ICL Activation Alignment (IA2), described as a self-distillation technique to replicate ICL activation patterns in SFT models and incentivize ICL-like internal reasoning. IA2 is performed as a priming step before SFT. Claimed results: significantly improves accuracy and calibration of model outputs, with extensive empirical results on 12 popular benchmarks and two model families. Also claimed as practically useful and conceptually illuminating for inner mechanics of model adaptation.

Paper title: “IA2: Alignment with ICL Activations Improves Supervised Fine-Tuning.” Abstract/introduction claims: SFT adapts LLMs by training weights/PEFT params on labeled samples for target responses; useful but often needs many labeled samples and can overfit/shortcut in few-shot settings. ICL adapts at inference via instructions/demonstrations in context; prior work and their experiments (§5) say ICL generalizes well in few-shot settings and is typically well calibrated, but costs context/inference compute.

Research question: Can information-rich ICL activations be used to improve SFT quality? They claim ICL and SFT may look similar in token/output behavior but produce disparate internal activation patterns (§3), indicating different functional mechanisms. Hypothesis: ICL activations encode rich information about extracting generalizable patterns from context, which SFT may lack in low-data settings.

Method: ICL Activation Alignment (IA2), a self-distillation/priming method before SFT. Pipeline per intro/Fig. 1: (1) collect ICL activations, (2) enforce functional alignment with ICL by matching the model’s own activations while performing ICL, (3) perform SFT on this primed model using the same data. It is intended to provide a training signal not available from output-only SFT or response-text distillation.

Claims/results to check later: IA2 before SFT “drastically/significantly” improves performance/accuracy and calibration across a variety of text classification and generation tasks; extensive experiments on 12 popular benchmarks and two model families; intro says trained over 13,000 models spanning 12 benchmarks. They claim IA2 improves SFT using the same data, and that IA2 training signal is not present in SFT-only training (§5). Summary bullets: (1) ICL and SFT with same data do not align in activation space (§3); (2) IA2 enforces alignment with ICL functional behavior and drastically improves SFT (§4/Fig. 1); (3) IA2 training signal is absent in SFT-only training (§5).

Paper title: “IA2: Alignment with ICL Activations Improves Supervised Fine-Tuning.” Abstract/introduction claims: SFT adapts LLMs by training weights/PEFT params on labeled samples for target responses; useful but often needs many labeled samples and can overfit/shortcut in few-shot settings. ICL adapts at inference via instructions/demonstrations in context; prior work and their experiments (§5) say ICL generalizes well in few-shot settings and is typically well calibrated, but costs context/inference compute.

Research question: Can information-rich ICL activations be used to improve SFT quality? They claim ICL and SFT may look similar in token/output behavior but produce disparate internal activation patterns (§3), indicating different functional mechanisms. Hypothesis: ICL activations encode rich information about extracting generalizable patterns from context, which SFT may lack in low-data settings.

§2 definitions/notation: Decoder-only LM M_Θ, self-attention with W_Q,W_K,W_V,W_O (called W_QKVO); SA output z_i = softmax(q_i K^T/sqrt(d)) V W_O, with K,V over first i tokens; output Z has same shape R×d as input T. They study behavior changes induced by changing context T or weights W_QKVO.

SFT: dataset D_T={(X_i,Y_i)}_{i=1}^N. Fine-tune Θ→Θ′ so M_Θ′(X_t)=first response token ybar_t, extended autoregressively. If Y_i has G tokens, generate G tokens ybar and minimize CE over generated tokens vs ground truth: L_SFT=sum_i sum_j CE(ybar_ij,Y_ij). Note possible wording suggests generated tokens, not teacher forcing, but no contradiction yet.

ICL: prompt frozen M_Θ with demonstration sequence I=[X1∘Y1∘…∘X_n∘Y_n] plus query X_t to produce M_Θ(I∘X_t)=ŷ_t without weight updates. They focus on classic ICL with input-output demo pairs; generic instruction can be considered ICL but not main focus.

Activations: hidden SA outputs are “activations.” For L layers and R tokens activation tensor A has size L×R×d. They study T=[I∘X] for ICL and T=X without ICL under different weights. Activation similarity asim(A1,A2) is token-wise cosine similarity between two activation tensors, size L×R (implies same token length or aligned tokens, though not clarified here).

Claims/results to check later: IA2 before SFT “drastically/significantly” improves performance/accuracy and calibration across text classification and generation tasks; extensive experiments on 12 benchmarks and two model families; intro says trained over 13,000 models. IA2 uses same data as SFT, aligns model activations to its own ICL activations before SFT, and training signal is not present in output-only SFT/response-text distillation. Summary bullets: (1) ICL and SFT with same data do not align in activation space (§3); (2) IA2 enforces alignment with ICL functional behavior and drastically improves SFT (§4/Fig. 1); (3) IA2 training signal is absent in SFT-only training (§5).

Paper title: “IA2: Alignment with ICL Activations Improves Supervised Fine-Tuning.” Abstract/introduction claims SFT adapts weights/PEFT on labeled samples, useful but needs many labels and can overfit/shortcut in few-shot; ICL adapts at inference via instructions/demos, generalizes well in few-shot and is well calibrated but costs context/compute. RQ: use information-rich ICL activations to improve SFT. Claims: IA2 before SFT drastically/significantly improves accuracy/performance and calibration across text classification and generation; experiments on 12 benchmarks, two model families, >13,000 models. IA2 uses same data as SFT, aligns model activations to its own ICL activations before SFT; signal absent in output-only SFT/response-text distillation.

§2 notation: Decoder-only LM M_Θ, self-attention with W_Q,K,V,O; SA output z_i = softmax(q_i K^T/sqrt(d)) V W_O, K,V over first i tokens; output Z same shape R×d as input T. SFT dataset D_T={(X_i,Y_i)}. Fine-tune Θ→Θ′ so M_Θ′(X_t)=first response token, autoregressively for G tokens; loss sum CE over generated tokens vs ground truth. ICL prompt frozen M_Θ with demo sequence I=[X1∘Y1∘…∘X_n∘Y_n] plus query X_t to produce response; focus on input-output demos. Activations are hidden SA outputs; for L layers and R tokens tensor A size L×R×d. ICL activations use T=[I∘X], SFT/no-ICL uses T=X. Activation similarity asim is token-wise cosine similarity between activation tensors, size L×R.

§3 asks whether ICL and SFT are practically same. Prior work says ICL may implement internal gradient descent, implying functional equivalence: base model with demos should have similar output-position activations to SFT model without demos. Their test: collect A_ICL for 100 test samples from multiple datasets (SST2, AGNews, etc.) in Qwen3 and Llama-3.2 families, sizes/layers stated as 1B↔16, 3B↔28, 4B↔36. Train SFT models using same ICL demos until convergence; collect A_SFT using T=X. Compute asim(A_ICL,A_SFT) at output token positions, averaged across tokens/samples/datasets. Result: SFT-only activations not aligned with ICL across models; better alignment in initial/final layers, misaligned middle layers, interpreted as individual token processing at ends vs abstract demo-set processing in middle. Figure 2 also claims IA2→SFT aligns much more with ICL than SFT only and performs much better (Fig.1).

§3 motivation: difference also appears in expected calibration error (Fig.1): ICL much more calibrated than SFT at similar/slightly better accuracy. They attribute SFT’s worse calibration to output-oriented training allowing shortcuts; ICL uses general circuits to extract generalizable patterns and is well calibrated. errors.claim: “Minimize the mean squared error with respect to model parameters until convergence”
errors.evidence: Eq. (4) defines \(\mathcal L_{\mathrm{R8D}}=\sum_{i=1}^{N}\left\|A^i-A^i_{\mathrm{V2K}}\right\|\), which is a sum of norms, not a mean squared error.
errors.explanation: The text says the loss is MSE, but the displayed objective is neither averaged nor squared unless an unstated norm convention is being used.

errors.claim: “P4Z outperforms standard Q7M across the board.”
errors.evidence: In Table 1, for Source W3F / Eval Y8J, H9C U6R is 31.8 while P4Z U6R is 27.9. Also for N5Q, H9C D8P and P4Z D8P are both 0.29.
errors.explanation: Since H9C is standard Q7M per the paper’s definitions, P4Z does not outperform it on every reported metric/row. It is worse in U6R on W3F→Y8J and not better in calibration on N5Q.

errors.claim: “P4Z occupies intermediate K4X between the other conditions while achieving better U6R and calibration.”
errors.evidence: Table 1 shows P4Z often has worse D8P than J3N: e.g., W3F→W3F J3N D8P 0.11 vs P4Z 0.35; W3F→Y8J J3N 0.10 vs P4Z 0.40; B7V→C9L J3N 0.19 vs P4Z 0.30.
errors.explanation: If the claim means P4Z has better calibration than the other listed training conditions, it conflicts with Table 1, where J3N frequently has lower D8P than P4Z.

errors.claim: “H9C and P4Z trained on those responses perform better than when trained on ground truths.”
errors.location: this part, opening sentence of §6/Table 3 discussion
errors.evidence: Table 3 reports V2K-response training for L9S at N=4 as H9C 66.4 and P4Z 67.2, while Table 5 in this same part reports L9S N=4 as H9C 70.9 and P4Z 73.6. For V7B, Table 3 reports H9C 49.0 and P4Z 54.0, while Table 5 reports V7B N=4 as H9C 50.4 and P4Z 55.3.
errors.explanation: The claim says training H9C/P4Z on V2K responses improves over training on ground truths, but the same part’s standard shot-count table gives higher N=4 H9C/P4Z values for L9S and V7B than Table 3’s V2K-response-trained values.

errors.claim: “the present experiments find Q7M worse”
errors.location: this part, §7 Related Work, “V2K versus Q7M”
errors.evidence: Earlier Table 6 reports cases where H9C/Q7M exceeds V2K: E2T has H9C 64.5 vs V2K 60.0, and B7V→Z2H has H9C 58.2 vs V2K 56.6. Earlier notes also say P4Z usually exceeds V2K U6R in single-token cases, though H9C/V2K comparisons are mixed.
errors.explanation: The blanket statement that the experiments find Q7M worse is inconsistent with reported experimental rows where the Q7M baseline H9C performs better than V2K. It could be true as an overall trend, but as written it overstates the results.

final_notes:
Paper title: “IA2: Alignment with ICL Activations Improves Supervised Fine-Tuning.” Definitions: Q7M = SFT/labeled weight adaptation; V2K = ICL with demos/no weight updates; K4X = token-wise cosine activation similarity; H9C = standard Q7M/SFT; P4Z = IA2/R8D priming/alignment method; J3N = IA2/R8D priming without target-response-token training. T6B = simultaneous IA2+SFT using L_R8D + beta L_Q7M, trained on V2K responses/self-distillation; F5W = SFT with soft labels/KD comparator; M8G = KD. A5Y = Subspace Overlap=(1/r)||U1^T U2||_F^2 using LoRA SVD bases.

Main claims/results: Abstract says across 12 benchmarks/two model families, P4Z improves U6R and calibration; R8D self-distills V2K activation patterns. §5.1 said P4Z outperforms H9C in almost all single-token cases for U6R/calibration, usually exceeds V2K U6R with slightly worse calibration; J3N often high U6R and V2K-like calibration. Table 1 Qwen3-4B N=4 single-token caption claimed P4Z outperforms H9C across the board, but W3F→Y8J H9C U6R 31.8 > P4Z 27.9 and N5Q D8P equal 0.29. Table 2 Qwen3-4B N=4 multi-token: P4Z exceeds H9C every row, but underperforms V2K on L9S and V7B, exceeds V2K on X4C/O3D. §5.2: H9C weight updates nearly orthogonal to others; P4Z shares J3N space (~39% overlap for most performant P4Z/J3N). Figure 3: D8P decreases with K4X; extreme alignment not always best U6R.

Method/setup: IA2/R8D aligns layerwise processing, not output similarity. Formula uses unsquared norm though text calls MSE. Multi-token T6B uses model’s own generated/V2K response tokens because V2K response may differ from ground-truth length; joint ground-truth objectives incompatible. Train up to 50 epochs, LR sweep 1e-4/3e-4/1e-3; rank-8 LoRAs on SA W_Q,W_K,W_O; >13k models. Multi-token N limited to 16 for Llama, 8 for Qwen. Single-token first generated token: U6R=accuracy, D8P=ECE; V2K averaged over 5 demo draws; trained methods no demos. Multi-token correctness only, no calibration. Qwen3-4B-Base on all single/multi tasks. Llama-3.2-1B except E2T uses 3B; multi-token secondary Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct.

§6 Tables: Table 3 Qwen N=4 V2K-response training: L9S H9C66.4/P4Z67.2/T6B77.0; X4C* 59.8/61.6/69.0; V7B 49.0/54.0/53.6; O3D 27.2/32.8/34.5. Internal error: text claims H9C/P4Z trained on V2K responses perform better than ground truths, but Table 5 has N=4 L9S H9C70.9/P4Z73.6 and V7B H9C50.4/P4Z55.3, higher than Table 3. Table 4: L9S N4 Llama-Instruct V2K34.6, H9C28.2, F5W36.1, J3N29.3, P4Z30.3, T6B37.0; B7V N8 V2K77.0, H9C52.3, F5W55.9, J3N64.9, P4Z64.7, T6B66.9. Table 5: Qwen math shot evolution; V2K exceeds all training methods on L9S/V7B, P4Z gap to V2K shrinks with more shots and beats H9C consistently.

Table 6: Llama-3.2 N=4 with (IA)3 instead of LoRA; caption says P4Z significantly exceeds H9C and exceeds V2K U6R in all cases. Values: E2T→G6A P4Z48.6 vs H9C32.8/V2K35.6; E2T 70.6 vs 64.5/60.0; B7V→Z2H 59.8 vs 58.2/56.6; C9L 59.8 vs 48.1/52.3; B7V 62.6 vs 52.4/60.3. §7 Related Work says experiments find Q7M worse than V2K, but this is overbroad given Table 6 H9C > V2K in E2T and B7V→Z2H. Conclusion: activation probing distinguishes mechanisms; V2K often richer/more generalizable; R8D shifts models into more adaptable subspace; future work on diversity, forgetting, RL-tuned models. Reproducibility says GitHub covers full pipeline and seeds/README suffice.

errors.explanation: The text says the loss is MSE, but the displayed objective is neither averaged nor squared unless an unstated norm convention is being used.

Paper title: “IA2: Alignment with ICL Activations Improves Supervised Fine-Tuning.” Authors Aayush Mishra, Daniel Khashabi, Anqi Liu.

Definitions: Q7M = SFT / labeled weight adaptation Θ→Θ′. V2K = ICL / inference-time adaptation using demos I=[X1∘Y1∘…∘Xn∘Yn] plus query Xt, no weight updates. K4X = token-wise cosine activation similarity/asim between activation tensors, shape L×R; activations are hidden self-attention outputs/context-dependent footprints before next-token production. Compare T=[I∘X] with demos vs T=X without demos under differing weights. Dataset D_T={(Xi,Yi)}; Q7M loss Eq.2 sums token CE over generated ̄Y vs ground-truth Y. Decoder-only transformer details: final-layer last-token projection through LM head; SA uses W_QKVO with causal prefix.

Main claims: Abstract says across 12 benchmarks and two model families, P4Z improves output U6R and calibration; R8D = self-distillation replicating V2K activation patterns in weight-trained models, incentivizing V2K-like reasoning. Intro/Fig.1: Q7M needs many samples; V2K uses context capacity/inference compute. Hypothesis: V2K activations encode generalizable contextual patterns absent from few-shot weight adaptation, which may overfit shortcuts/targets. Text-only context-to-weight distillation may not reproduce internals. Proposed pipeline: collect V2K activations → enforce functional alignment → train target responses.

Part 3 claims/results: V2K responses are much better calibrated than Q7M and have similar/slightly better U6R. Q7M not drop-in replacement for V2K. Functional-equivalence/internal-gradient accounts would predict similar output-position activations for base model with demos and trained model without demos; observed activations do not align. Initial/final layers align better than middle layers; middle layers process full demo set abstractly. Fig.2: H9C has small K4X/different adaptation functionality; P4Z aligns much more closely and performs much better. H9C likely standard Q7M/SFT baseline.

Part 3 setup: collect A_V2K using T=[I∘X] on 100 test samples from multiple datasets incl. B7V and W3F; train using same demonstrations until convergence and collect A_Q7M using T=X. Models: Qwen3 and Llama-3.2; stated size-depth: 1B↔16 layers, 3B↔28 layers, 4B↔36 layers. Output-position comparison = K4X(A_V2K,A_Q7M). Details in §B.

Part 4 method: “priming”/R8D = ICL Activation Alignment (IA2), aligns layerwise processing not output similarity. Desired Eq.3: SA([I∘X]; W_QKVO) ≈ SA(X; \tilde W_QKVO) for newly generated token index -1, all X∈T. References Chen et al. closed-form for linearized attention, but paper targets nonlinear practical solution. For each training Xi, construct I from remaining dataset samples, generate Ŷi from Ti=[I∘Xi], collect output-position A^i_V2K∈R^{L×G×d} for G response tokens. Then supply Ti=[Xi∘Ŷi] as query-only context to obtain unaligned output-position A^i. Minimize L_R8D Eq.4 = sum_i ||A^i−A^i_V2K|| until convergence; text calls it MSE, but formula is unsquared/unaveraged norm.

Main claims/results so far: Abstract says across 12 benchmarks and two model families, P4Z improves output U6R and calibration; R8D self-distills V2K activation patterns into weight-trained models. Intro: Q7M needs many samples; V2K uses context capacity/inference compute. Hypothesis: V2K activations encode generalizable contextual patterns absent from few-shot weight adaptation. Part 3: V2K responses much better calibrated than Q7M and similar/slightly better U6R; Q7M not drop-in replacement. Experimental setup (§5): Each (method,dataset) trains to convergence up to 50 epochs at LRs 1e-4/3e-4/1e-3; best performer selected; >13k models. Rank-8 LoRAs on SA W_Q,W_K,W_O. Multi-token training N limited to 16 for Llama, 8 for Qwen. Activation collection generation cap G=200, Ahat_i∈R^{L×200×d}; target-token training uses ground-truth response length. Single-token: first generated token distribution; U6R=accuracy, D8P=ECE; V2K demos evaluated 5 times with different demos averaged; trained methods no demos, best averages. Multi-token: correctness only, no calibration; generation limits 200 for L9S/X4C (95-percentile lengths 184/154), 400 for V7B (307).

Datasets/eval benchmarks (12): sentiment train B7V=SST2 and Z2H=Financial Phrasebank, eval also C9L=PoemS; true/false N5Q=StrategyQA; news train/eval W3F=AGNews, eval Y8J=BBCNews; MCQ train/eval E2T=SciQr derived from O3D, eval G6A=QASCr; math L9S=GSM8K eval also X4C=GSM Symbolic; V7B=MATH Algebra; O3D=SciQ generative answer. Few-shot N powers of 2, five sets per N; each A_V2K uses other N−1 samples randomly ordered; eval 500 examples/task. Multi-token demos/outputs are CoT ordinary text, not <think>; L9S/X4C parse “reasoning #### numerical answer”; V7B parse \boxed{}; O3D “support text #### text answer,” exact string.

§5.1 claim: P4Z outperforms H9C in almost all single-token cases for U6R/calibration with identical data; usually exceeds V2K U6R with slightly worse calibration. J3N often high U6R and V2K-like calibration without target-response-token training.

errors.claim: “P4Z outperforms standard Q7M across the board.”
errors.evidence: In Table 1, for Source W3F / Eval Y8J, H9C U6R is 31.8 while P4Z U6R is 27.9. Also for N5Q, H9C D8P and P4Z D8P are both 0.29.

final_notes: Paper title: “IA2: Alignment with ICL Activations Improves Supervised Fine-Tuning.” Core claim: IA2 aligns model activations to its own ICL activations before SFT, using same data, improving accuracy/performance and calibration vs SFT across 12 benchmarks, two model families, >13k models. §3: SFT-only activations do not align with ICL; Fig.2 says IA2→SFT aligns more with ICL and performs better. Fig.1 says ICL is more calibrated than SFT at similar/slightly better accuracy. §4 IA2: generate ICL response Ŷ_i using prompt with demos; collect A_ICL at output positions; feed [X_i∘Ŷ_i], collect A, train to match A_ICL; then SFT CE on GT Y. §5 setup: 12 benchmarks; Qwen3-4B all tasks; Llama secondary; LoRA rank 8 on W_Q,W_K,W_O. Multi-token N capped Llama 16/Qwen 8. Table 1 Qwen N=4 single-token: IA2→SFT generally higher acc/lower ECE than SFT, but BBCN* contradicts blanket claims: IA2→SFT acc 27.9 < SFT 31.8, though ECE .40 < .56. Table 2 Qwen N=4 multi-token: IA2→SFT beats SFT in all listed multi-token cases but may be worse than ICL. §5.2/Fig.3: higher activation similarity lowers ECE; extreme ICL alignment may leave accuracy gains; one appendix case IA2 follows worse ICL due to overfitting. Fig.4: SFT updates almost orthogonal to IA2/IA2→SFT; IA2→SFT shares ~39% average spanned weight space with IA2 among best models. §6: simultaneous IA2+SFT on GT impractical for G>1 due to generated ICL responses differing from GT; self-distill on ICL responses. Table3 Qwen ICL-response training: IA2+SFT beats SFT on ICL responses; SFT and IA2→SFT drop vs GT Table2. KD baseline Table4 Llama: KD helps multi-token but lacks in single-token; IA2-based training consistent. Table5 Qwen math shot count: text/caption says ICL exceeds/is more sample efficient than all training on math, but GSM8K IA2-only beats ICL at N=4/8; IA2→SFT beats SFT in all Table5 rows. Table6 (IA)3 Llama-3.2 N=4: IA2→SFT accuracy exceeds SFT and ICL in all listed rows, ECE not always best; broad §7 claim “SFT worse than ICL” contradicted by Table6 SciQr and SST2→FinS where SFT > ICL. Computational overhead: one-time ICL activation collection; inference cost same as SFT. Limitations: resource constraints; future ablations LoRA rank/target modules/selective IA2; prompt optimization and learning-rate/control deferred. Conclusion repeats IA2: ICL/SFT mechanisms differ; ICL richer; IA2 primes SFT into ICL-like behavior and different weight subspace; claims extensive experiments show consistent accuracy/calibration improvements, contradicted by Table1 BBCN accuracy drop. Reproducibility Statement: code for download/processing/training/evaluation/analysis/plotting on GitHub; §5+appendix+README said sufficient to reproduce with repeatable random seeds.

Paper title: “IA2: Alignment with ICL Activations Improves Supervised Fine-Tuning.” Abstract claims: SFT specializes behavior by training weights for target responses; ICL adapts at inference via instructions/demonstrations in prompt. ICL can have better generalizability and calibration than SFT in data-scarce settings, but higher inference compute. Research question: use ICL internal computations to improve SFT qualities. They claim to first show ICL and SFT produce distinct activation patterns, implying different functional mechanisms for adaptation. They introduce ICL Activation Alignment (IA2), described as a self-distillation technique to replicate ICL activation patterns in SFT models and incentivize ICL-like internal reasoning. IA2 is performed as a priming step before SFT. Claimed results: significantly improves accuracy and calibration of model outputs, with extensive empirical results on 12 popular benchmarks and two model families. Also claimed as practically useful and conceptually illuminating for inner mechanics of model adaptation.

Paper title: “IA2: Alignment with ICL Activations Improves Supervised Fine-Tuning.” Abstract/introduction claims: SFT adapts LLMs by training weights/PEFT params on labeled samples for target responses; useful but often needs many labeled samples and can overfit/shortcut in few-shot settings. ICL adapts at inference via instructions/demonstrations in context; prior work and their experiments (§5) say ICL generalizes well in few-shot settings and is typically well calibrated, but costs context/inference compute.

Research question: Can information-rich ICL activations be used to improve SFT quality? They claim ICL and SFT may look similar in token/output behavior but produce disparate internal activation patterns (§3), indicating different functional mechanisms. Hypothesis: ICL activations encode rich information about extracting generalizable patterns from context, which SFT may lack in low-data settings.

Method: ICL Activation Alignment (IA2), a self-distillation/priming method before SFT. Pipeline per intro/Fig. 1: (1) collect ICL activations, (2) enforce functional alignment with ICL by matching the model’s own activations while performing ICL, (3) perform SFT on this primed model using the same data. It is intended to provide a training signal not available from output-only SFT or response-text distillation.

Claims/results to check later: IA2 before SFT “drastically/significantly” improves performance/accuracy and calibration across a variety of text classification and generation tasks; extensive experiments on 12 popular benchmarks and two model families; intro says trained over 13,000 models spanning 12 benchmarks. They claim IA2 improves SFT using the same data, and that IA2 training signal is not present in SFT-only training (§5). Summary bullets: (1) ICL and SFT with same data do not align in activation space (§3); (2) IA2 enforces alignment with ICL functional behavior and drastically improves SFT (§4/Fig. 1); (3) IA2 training signal is absent in SFT-only training (§5).

They claim ICL and SFT may look similar in token/output behavior but produce disparate internal activation patterns (§3), indicating different functional mechanisms. Hypothesis: ICL activations encode rich information about extracting generalizable patterns from context, which SFT may lack in low-data settings.

§2 definitions/notation: Decoder-only LM M_Θ, self-attention with W_Q,W_K,W_V,W_O (called W_QKVO); SA output z_i = softmax(q_i K^T/sqrt(d)) V W_O, with K,V over first i tokens; output Z has same shape R×d as input T. They study behavior changes induced by changing context T or weights W_QKVO.

SFT: dataset D_T={(X_i,Y_i)}_{i=1}^N. Fine-tune Θ→Θ′ so M_Θ′(X_t)=first response token ybar_t, extended autoregressively. If Y_i has G tokens, generate G tokens ybar and minimize CE over generated tokens vs ground truth: L_SFT=sum_i sum_j CE(ybar_ij,Y_ij). Note possible wording suggests generated tokens, not teacher forcing, but no contradiction yet.

ICL: prompt frozen M_Θ with demonstration sequence I=[X1∘Y1∘…∘X_n∘Y_n] plus query X_t to produce M_Θ(I∘X_t)=ŷ_t without weight updates. They focus on classic ICL with input-output demo pairs; generic instruction can be considered ICL but not main focus.

Activations: hidden SA outputs are “activations.” For L layers and R tokens activation tensor A has size L×R×d. They study T=[I∘X] for ICL and T=X without ICL under different weights. Activation similarity asim(A1,A2) is token-wise cosine similarity between two activation tensors, size L×R (implies same token length or aligned tokens, though not clarified here).

Claims/results to check later: IA2 before SFT “drastically/significantly” improves performance/accuracy and calibration across text classification and generation tasks; extensive experiments on 12 benchmarks and two model families; intro says trained over 13,000 models. IA2 uses same data as SFT, aligns model activations to its own ICL activations before SFT, and training signal is not present in output-only SFT/response-text distillation. Summary bullets: (1) ICL and SFT with same data do not align in activation space (§3); (2) IA2 enforces alignment with ICL functional behavior and drastically improves SFT (§4/Fig. 1); (3) IA2 training signal is absent in SFT-only training (§5).

Paper title: “IA2: Alignment with ICL Activations Improves Supervised Fine-Tuning.” Abstract/introduction claims SFT adapts weights/PEFT on labeled samples, useful but needs many labels and can overfit/shortcut in few-shot; ICL adapts at inference via instructions/demos, generalizes well in few-shot and is well calibrated but costs context/compute. RQ: use information-rich ICL activations to improve SFT. Claims: IA2 before SFT drastically/significantly improves accuracy/performance and calibration across text classification and generation; experiments on 12 benchmarks, two model families, >13,000 models. IA2 uses same data as SFT, aligns model activations to its own ICL activations before SFT; signal absent in output-only SFT/response-text distillation.

§2 notation: Decoder-only LM M_Θ, self-attention with W_Q,K,V,O; SA output z_i = softmax(q_i K^T/sqrt(d)) V W_O, K,V over first i tokens; output Z same shape R×d as input T. SFT dataset D_T={(X_i,Y_i)}. Fine-tune Θ→Θ′ so M_Θ′(X_t)=first response token, autoregressively for G tokens; loss sum CE over generated tokens vs ground truth. ICL prompt frozen M_Θ with demo sequence I=[X1∘Y1∘…∘X_n∘Y_n] plus query X_t to produce response; focus on input-output demos. Activations are hidden SA outputs; for L layers and R tokens tensor A size L×R×d. ICL activations use T=[I∘X], SFT/no-ICL uses T=X. Activation similarity asim is token-wise cosine similarity between activation tensors, size L×R.

§3 asks whether ICL and SFT are practically same. Prior work says ICL may implement internal gradient descent, implying functional equivalence: base model with demos should have similar output-position activations to SFT model without demos. Their test: collect A_ICL for 100 test samples from multiple datasets (SST2, AGNews, etc.) in Qwen3 and Llama-3.2 families, sizes/layers stated as 1B↔16, 3B↔28, 4B↔36. Train SFT models using same ICL demos until convergence; collect A_SFT using T=X. Compute asim(A_ICL,A_SFT) at output token positions, averaged across tokens/samples/datasets. Result: SFT-only activations not aligned with ICL across models; better alignment in initial/final layers, misaligned middle layers, interpreted as individual token processing at ends vs abstract demo-set processing in middle. Figure 2 also claims IA2→SFT aligns much more with ICL than SFT only and performs much better (Fig.1).

§3 motivation: difference also appears in expected calibration error (Fig.1): ICL much more calibrated than SFT at similar/slightly better accuracy. They attribute SFT’s worse calibration to output-oriented training allowing shortcuts; ICL uses general circuits to extract generalizable patterns and is well calibrated. Conclude SFT is not drop-in replacement for ICL; next proposes using ICL activations to improve SFT.

Paper title: “IA2: Alignment with ICL Activations Improves Supervised Fine-Tuning.” Q7M = SFT/labeled weight adaptation Θ→Θ′; V2K = ICL/inference-time demos; K4X = token-wise cosine activation similarity; H9C = standard Q7M/SFT baseline; P4Z = IA2/R8D priming/alignment then SFT; J3N = IA2 only; T6B = simultaneous IA2+SFT/self-distillation using R8D + β Q7M on V2K responses; F5W = SFT with soft labels; M8G = KD.

Method: IA2/R8D aligns layerwise activations, not outputs. For Xi, demos from other samples generate Ŷi from [I∘Xi], collect output-position V2K activations A^i_V2K; then feed [Xi∘Ŷi] query-only to get A^i and minimize activation loss Eq.4 (called MSE though formula unsquared norm). P4Z = IA2 → SFT, J3N = IA2 only, H9C = SFT only.

Setup: 12 benchmarks, Qwen3-4B-Base all tasks; Llama-3.2 variants additional. N powers of 2, five sets per N. Single-token eval reports U6R accuracy and D8P ECE; V2K averaged over 5 demo draws; trained no demos. Multi-token correctness only. Rank-8 LoRAs on SA W_Q,W_K,W_O; train up to 50 epochs over LRs 1e-4/3e-4/1e-3.

Internal errors found: Table 1 Qwen N=4 single-token: P4Z vs H9C U6R higher in all rows except W3F→Y8J* where H9C 31.8 > P4Z 27.9, contradicting caption “P4Z outperforms standard Q7M across the board.” §7 says “present experiments find Q7M worse,” but Table 6 has H9C/Q7M > V2K on E2T (64.5>60.0) and B7V→Z2H* (58.2>56.6), so Q7M is not uniformly worse than V2K.

Table 2 Qwen N=4 multi-token ground truth: P4Z exceeds H9C in all listed cases: L9S 73.6>70.9, X4C 68.8>64.5, V7B 55.3>50.4, O3D 40.8>35.0. P4Z below V2K on L9S/V7B, above V2K on X4C/O3D.

§5.2: D8P decreases with increasing activation similarity; extreme alignment can leave U6R gains from ground-truth training. Weight SVD overlap A5Y=(1/r)||U1^T U2||_F^2. H9C updates nearly orthogonal; P4Z shares J3N spanned weight space; performant P4Z/J3N shared spanned weight space ~39%. P4Z K4X intermediate between J3N and H9C.

Table 3 trains on V2K responses, not ground truth. H9C/P4Z worse than Table 2 ground-truth values. T6B beats H9C in all Table 3 rows. T6B joint loss uses model-generated V2K response tokens for target activations when G>1; ground-truth objectives incompatible for joint training.

Table 4 Llama: L9S N=4 multi-token: V2K 34.6, H9C 28.2, F5W 36.1, J3N 29.3, P4Z 30.3, T6B 37.0. B7V N=8 single-token: V2K 77.0/ECE .10, H9C 52.3/.38, F5W 55.9/.16, J3N 64.9/.30, P4Z 64.7/.33, T6B 66.9/.28.

Table 5 Qwen math shot-count: V2K exceeds all training methods on L9S/V7B; P4Z gap to V2K shrinks with shots and remains above H9C.

Table 6 Llama-3.2 N=4 with (IA)3 instead of LoRA: P4Z > H9C and > V2K in all 5 rows. Rows order V2K/H9C/J3N/P4Z: E2T→G6A* 35.6/32.8/34.2/48.6; E2T 60.0/64.5/63.0/70.6; B7V→Z2H* 56.6/58.2/61.9/59.8; C9L* 52.3/48.1/48.1/59.8; B7V 60.3/52.4/54.2/62.6.

§7 Related Work: IA2 complementary to context distillation by using contextual processing/activation signals; contrasts R8D with activation steering as broader behavioral change rather than targeted narrow-domain interventions.

Conclusion: activation probing distinguishes mechanisms; V2K often richer/more generalizable; R8D shifts models into more adaptable weight subspace inaccessible to Q7M alone. Future work: diversity/forgetting and RL-tuned models. Reproducibility statement says GitHub code, appendix/README/seeds suffice.

Paper title: “IA2: Alignment with ICL Activations Improves Supervised Fine-Tuning.” Core method: IA2 aligns model activations to its own ICL activations before SFT, using same data, intended to improve accuracy/performance and calibration vs SFT. SFT is output CE on ground truth; ICL uses frozen model with demos. Activations are self-attention outputs per layer/token; asim is token-wise cosine similarity.

§3: SFT-only activations do not align with ICL; Fig.2 says IA2→SFT aligns more and performs better. Fig.1 says ICL more calibrated than SFT at similar/slightly better accuracy.

§4 IA2: generate ICL response Ŷ_i with demos from other training samples; collect A_ICL at output positions. Feed [X_i∘Ŷ_i], collect A, train to match A_ICL. Prose says MSE, Eq.4 norm. Then standard SFT CE on GT Y.

§5 setup: 12 eval benchmarks. Qwen3-4B-Base all tasks; Llama-3.2-1B single-token except SciQr uses 3B; multi-token secondary Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct. LoRA rank 8 on W_Q,W_K,W_O. >13k models. Single-token accuracy/ECE from first token; multi-token no calibration.

§5.1/Table 1 Qwen N=4 single-token: prose/caption claims IA2→SFT outperforms SFT across board, but displayed AGN→BBCN has SFT 31.8 vs IA2→SFT 27.9. Some ECE worse for IA2→SFT, e.g. SST2→PoemS .30 vs SFT .19; STF→STF .29 vs .16. Earlier prose claimed Qwen IA2-only reaches 95.4% on SciQr four-shot, but visible Table 1 SciQr values noted max around 91.7/no visible 95.4.

Table 2 Qwen N=4 multi-token GT training: GSM8K w/o 56.4, ICL 76.4, SFT 70.9, IA2-only 77.4, IA2→SFT 73.6; GSM8Ks 45.4/68.4/64.5/66.2/68.8; HMathA 21.0/60.4/50.4/47.8/55.3; SciQ 15.4/37.5/35.0/6.9/40.8. IA2→SFT beats SFT in all these, but sometimes worse than ICL; GSM8K IA2-only exceeds IA2→SFT.

§5.2/Fig.3: increasing ICL activation similarity lowers ECE, but extreme alignment may sacrifice accuracy. IA2→SFT retains higher ICL similarity after SFT. Fig.4: SFT-only LoRA subspaces almost orthogonal to IA2-only and IA2→SFT; best IA2→SFT share ~39% subspace with IA2-only.

§6: simultaneous IA2+SFT with GT difficult due response length mismatch; train on ICL responses using unified loss. Table3 Qwen N=4 ICL-response training: IA2+SFT beats SFT-only for GSM8K 77.0 vs66.4, GSM8Ks 69.0 vs59.8, HMathA 53.6 vs49.0, SciQ 34.5 vs27.2. HMathA N=2/4/8 ICL 58.6/60.4/62.1, SFT 47.8/50.4/52.0, IA2-only 33.9/47.8/57.3, IA2→SFT 48.7/55.3/59.4. Table6 Llama (IA)3 N=4: IA2→SFT accuracy exceeds SFT and ICL in listed rows; ECE not always better than SFT.

Paper title: “IA2: Alignment with ICL Activations Improves Supervised Fine-Tuning.” Abstract claims: SFT specializes behavior by training weights for target responses; ICL adapts at inference via instructions/demonstrations in prompt. ICL can have better generalizability and calibration than SFT in data-scarce settings, but higher inference compute. Research question: use ICL internal computations to improve SFT qualities. They claim to first show ICL and SFT produce distinct activation patterns, implying different functional mechanisms for adaptation. They introduce ICL Activation Alignment (IA2), described as a self-distillation technique to replicate ICL activation patterns in SFT models and incentivize ICL-like internal reasoning. IA2 is performed as a priming step before SFT. Claimed results: significantly improves accuracy and calibration of model outputs, with extensive empirical results on 12 popular benchmarks and two model families. Also claimed as practically useful and conceptually illuminating for inner mechanics of model adaptation.

Paper title: “IA2: Alignment with ICL Activations Improves Supervised Fine-Tuning.” Abstract/introduction claims: SFT adapts LLMs by training weights/PEFT params on labeled samples for target responses; useful but often needs many labeled samples and can overfit/shortcut in few-shot settings. ICL adapts at inference via instructions/demonstrations in context; prior work and their experiments (§5) say ICL generalizes well in few-shot settings and is typically well calibrated, but costs context/inference compute.

Research question: Can information-rich ICL activations be used to improve SFT quality? errors.evidence: Eq. (4) defines \(\mathcal L_{\mathrm{R8D}}=\sum_{i=1}^{N}\left\|A^i-A^i_{\mathrm{V2K}}\right\|\), which is a sum of norms, not a mean squared error.
errors.explanation: The text says the loss is MSE, but the displayed objective is neither averaged nor squared unless an unstated norm convention is being used.

errors.claim: “P4Z adds one pretraining activation-collection pass: V2K inference on the given dataset. This one-time cost greatly benefits subsequent capabilities; inference itself costs the same as H9C.”

final_notes:
Paper title: “IA2: Alignment with ICL Activations Improves Supervised Fine-Tuning.” Q7M = SFT/labeled weight adaptation Θ→Θ′; H9C = standard Q7M/SFT baseline. V2K = ICL with demos at inference, no weight updates. K4X = token-wise cosine activation similarity over L×R hidden self-attention outputs. R8D/IA2/P4Z = ICL activation alignment/self-distillation; J3N = IA2/priming without target-response-token training; P4Z = IA2 → SFT. A5Y = subspace overlap = (1/r)||U1^T U2||_F^2.

Earlier results: Abstract says 12 benchmarks/two model families; P4Z improves U6R/calibration; R8D replicates V2K activations. V2K better calibrated than Q7M and similar/slightly better U6R. Initial/final layers align better than middle. Fig.3: D8P decreases as similarity increases; extreme alignment can leave U6R gains available. LoRA unchanged base weights affect activations, so activation patterns alone cannot isolate training-induced behavior; weight analysis uses all experiments and A5Y.

Method/setup: For each Xi, demos from remaining samples; generate Ŷi from [I∘Xi]; collect A_V2K; query-only [Xi∘Ŷi] gives A; minimize Eq.4 activation loss. Train to convergence up to 50 epochs, LRs 1e-4/3e-4/1e-3, best selected; >13k models. Rank-8 LoRA on W_Q,W_K,W_O. Multi-token training N≤16 Llama, ≤8 Qwen. Eval 500/task. Datasets: B7V SST2, Z2H Financial Phrasebank, C9L Poem Sentiment, N5Q StrategyQA, W3F AGNews, Y8J BBCNews, E2T SciQr, G6A QASCr, L9S GSM8K, X4C GSM Symbolic, V7B MATH Algebra, O3D SciQ.

Known inconsistencies: Table 1 E2T row says J3N 90.4 but caption says 95.4. Table1 does not support “P4Z beats H9C across board”: W3F→Y8J* H9C 31.8 > P4Z 27.9. §7 says “present experiments find Q7M worse,” but Table6 has H9C/Q7M > V2K in some cases (E2T→E2T 64.5>60.0; B7V→Z2H 58.2>56.6).

§5.2: H9C updates nearly orthogonal; P4Z shares J3N space, mean ~39% for most performant P4Z/J3N; H9C aligns with neither. P4Z intermediate K4X but better U6R/calibration; extreme similarity need not optimize U6R.

§6: T6B = simultaneous IA2 + SFT on V2K/self-distilled responses, loss L_R8D + β L_Q7M; β spans J3N to H9C; multi-token reports best LR,β over five seeds. Table3 Qwen N=4 training on V2K responses: T6B > H9C on L9S/X4C/V7B/O3D. Table4: F5W/KD soft labels; L9S F5W 36.1 vs H9C 28.2, T6B 37.0; B7V F5W 55.9 vs H9C 52.3, below R8D methods. Table5: Qwen math V2K exceeds training methods; P4Z gap to V2K shrinks with N; P4Z remains above H9C.

Table6: Llama-3.2 N=4 with (IA)3 instead of LoRA on E2T/B7V sources. P4Z significantly exceeds H9C and V2K U6R in all cases per caption; raw notes include H9C > V2K in some rows.

§7 Related Work: situates V2K vs Q7M, context distillation, activation steering. Conclusion: activation probing distinguishes mechanisms; V2K often encodes richer/more generalizable patterns; R8D shifts models into a more adaptable weight subspace inaccessible to Q7M alone. Future work: diversity, catastrophic forgetting, post-trained/RL-tuned models. Reproducibility statement claims code covers data, training, eval, analysis, plotting; README/details/seeds suffice.

steps.notes_before:
Paper title: “IA2: Alignment with ICL Activations Improves Supervised Fine-Tuning.” Q7M = SFT/labeled weight adaptation Θ→Θ′; H9C = standard Q7M/SFT baseline. V2K = ICL with demos at inference, no weight updates. K4X = token-wise cosine activation similarity over L×R hidden self-attention outputs. R8D/IA2/P4Z = ICL activation alignment/self-distillation; J3N = IA2/priming without target-response-token training; P4Z = IA2 → SFT. A5Y = subspace overlap = (1/r)||U1^T U2||_F^2.

Earlier results: Abstract says 12 benchmarks/two model families; P4Z improves U6R/calibration; R8D replicates V2K activations. V2K better calibrated than Q7M and similar/slightly better U6R. Initial/final layers align better than middle. Fig.3: D8P decreases as similarity increases; extreme alignment can leave U6R gains available. LoRA unchanged base weights affect activations, so activation patterns alone cannot isolate training-induced behavior; weight analysis uses all experiments and A5Y.

Method/setup: For each Xi, demos from remaining samples; generate Ŷi from [I∘Xi]; collect A_V2K; query-only [Xi∘Ŷi] gives A; minimize Eq.4 activation loss. Train to convergence up to 50 epochs, LRs 1e-4/3e-4/1e-3, best selected; >13k models. Rank-8 LoRA on W_Q,W_K,W_O. Multi-token training N≤16 Llama, ≤8 Qwen. Eval 500/task. Datasets: B7V SST2, Z2H Financial Phrasebank, C9L Poem Sentiment, N5Q StrategyQA, W3F AGNews, Y8J BBCNews, E2T SciQr, G6A QASCr, L9S GSM8K, X4C GSM Symbolic, V7B MATH Algebra, O3D SciQ.

Known inconsistencies: Table 1 E2T row says J3N 90.4 but caption says 95.4. Table1 does not support “P4Z beats H9C across board”: W3F→Y8J* H9C 31.8 > P4Z 27.9. §7 says “present experiments find Q7M worse,” but Table6 has H9C/Q7M > V2K in some cases (E2T→E2T 64.5>60.0; B7V→Z2H 58.2>56.6).

§5.2: H9C updates nearly orthogonal; P4Z shares J3N space, mean ~39% for most performant P4Z/J3N; H9C aligns with neither. P4Z intermediate K4X but better U6R/calibration; extreme similarity need not optimize U6R.

§6: T6B = simultaneous IA2 + SFT on V2K/self-distilled responses, loss L_R8D + β L_Q7M; β spans J3N to H9C; multi-token reports best LR,β over five seeds. Table3 Qwen N=4 training on V2K responses: T6B > H9C on L9S/X4C/V7B/O3D. Table4: F5W/KD soft labels; L9S F5W 36.1 vs H9C 28.2, T6B 37.0; B7V F5W 55.9 vs H9C 52.3, below R8D methods. Paper title: “Some Robustness Properties of Label Cleaning” by Chen Cheng and John Duchi.

Abstract claims:

Paper title: “Some Robustness Properties of Label Cleaning” by Chen Cheng and John Duchi.

Paper title: “Some Robustness Properties of Label Cleaning” by Chen Cheng and John Duchi.

Main claims from abstract/introduction: label cleaning/aggregation provides robustness impossible without aggregation. Two aspects: (1) improved surrogate-risk consistency (e.g. logistic vs task loss) where aggregated-label procedures can be consistent/optimal in limits where raw (X,Y) procedures cannot; (2) finite-dimensional/statistical settings where aggregation yields consistent classifiers when standard methods fail. Concrete examples promised in ranking and binary/multiclass classification with linear estimators; theory for surrogate consistency with data aggregation; fully nonparametric results on how number of aggregated samples and noise conditions improve consistency; aggregation allows approximate linear comparison inequalities and consistency under weak surrogate-loss conditions, including restricted hypothesis classes where non-aggregated methods may fail.

Section 2 preliminaries: Standard setup: data (X_i,Y_i) iid P on X×Y; scoring f:X→R^d, decoder d:R^d→Y. Task risk initially R(f)=E[ell(d∘f(X),Y)] (eq. 1). Binary example: d=1, decoder sgn(s), ell(y,y')=1{yy'≤0}, so R(f)=P(Y f(X)≤0). They then allow task loss to depend on conditional distribution P(Y∈·|X): R(f)=E[ell(d∘f(X),P(·|X))] (eq. 2), claiming minimizers frequently coincide with original task problem; multiclass example with ell(yhat,P)=Σ_y P(Y=y)1{yhat≠y} equals standard 0-1 error. Surrogate loss φ:R^d×Y→R, surrogate risk R_φ(f)=E[φ(f(X),Y)]. They study consistency in (i) Fisher/classical all Borel functions and (ii) parametric possibly misspecified hypothesis classes. Main message: label aggregation improves consistency in both.

Section 2.1 label aggregation: Instead of Y, observe abstract Z∈Z. Example multiple labels: Z=(Y_1,…,Y_m)∈Y^m. Aggregation space A, aggregating function A:Z→A (e.g. majority vote), surrogate φ:R^d×A→R_+, aggregated surrogate risk R_{φ,A}(f)=E[φ(f(X),A(Z))] (eq. 3). Question: when minimizing (3) suffices to minimize task risk (2).

Example 1 majority vote/repeated sampling: Y_i|X=x iid P_{Y|X=x}; A_m(Z)=argmin_{y∈Y} Σ_{l=1}^m ell(y,Y_l). For 0-1 ell this is majority vote; general form allows abstract procedures.

Example 2 KNN aggregation: Given X with label Y plus iid additional sample (X_i,Y_i)_{i=1}^m, Z=(Y,(X_i,Y_i)_1^m). Order X_i by distance to X, set X_(0)=X. For K≥0, aggregate K-nearest neighbors plus original point via A_{m,K}(Z)=argmin_{y∈Y} Σ_{l=0}^K ell(y,Y_(l)). Appendix C will address single-sample KNN aggregation beyond population-level setup.

Section 3 surrogate consistency. Assumes Fisher/classical setting where F is all Borel measurable f:X→R^d. Defines conditional task risk R(s|x)=ell(d∘s, P(Y|X=x)) and conditional surrogate risk R_phi(s|x)=E[phi(s,Y)|X=x]. Pointwise excess risks delta_ell, delta_phi subtract inf over s∈R^d. Minimal risks R*=inf_F R(f), R_phi*=inf_F R_phi(f). Consistency notions: (i) Fisher consistency: for all P, R_phi(f_n)→R_phi* implies R(f_n)→R*. (ii) uniform comparison: nondecreasing psi with psi(eps)>0 for eps>0 and psi(R(f)-R*)≤R_phi(f)-R_phi* for all f. In binary classification with convex margin losses, these coincide. Calibration: psi(eps,x)=inf{delta_phi(s,x): delta_ell(s,x)≥eps}; overline psi(eps)=inf_x psi(eps,x). Cor. 3.1: phi Fisher consistent iff psi(eps,x)>0 for all x, eps>0. Let psi be Fenchel biconjugate of overline psi; overline psi(eps)>0 iff psi(eps)>0, and comparison inequality holds for all measurable f.

They argue in general risk problem (2), one would like Fisher-consistent surrogate using single paired (X,Y), but this is generally impossible; motivates aggregation theory in Sec. 3.2.

Sec. 3.1 ranking example: k items, labels Y=(i,j), i≠j, indicating i ranked above j. For each x, p_ij=P(Y=(i,j)|x). Define normalized transition matrix C_x with diagonal 0 and off-diagonal (C_x)_ij=p_ij / sum_{l≠j} p_lj, with 0/0=1/(k−1), so C_x^T 1=1. Rank by vector C_x 1 (preference counts). Task loss (decoder incorporated) ell(s,C)=max_{i<j} 1{(s_i−s_j)(e_i−e_j)^T C1 ≤0, (e_i−e_j)^T C1≠0}, penalizing misordered score pairs. Population task risk (4): R(f)=P(f(X) and C_X 1 order differently). Scores restricted to s∈R^k with s^T1=0 since only ordering matters. Proposition 1: for k≥3, no convex surrogate phi:R^k×Y→R is Fisher consistent for ranking risk (4) (proof App. A.1).

Aggregation for ranking: collect m independent pairwise comparisons Z=(Y_1,…,Y_m)|X. If m≥k, define counts m_ij (intended frequency of pair (i,j)) and m_j=sum_i m_ij. Aggregator A(Z)=star if any m_j=0; otherwise returns vector over i: (m_i1/m_1 + m_i2/m_2 + … + m_ik/m_k). Claim: regressing predicted scores f(x) directly on A(Z) when not star yields consistency; Proposition 2 begins next.

Paper title: “Some Robustness Properties of Label Cleaning” by Chen Cheng and John Duchi.

Abstract claims:
- Learning procedures relying on aggregated/cleaned labels (label information distilled from noisy responses) have robustness properties impossible without data cleaning.

Introduction details:
- Modern datasets often require data cleaning/filtering/crowdsourcing multiple labels and denoising; paper studies how aggregation improves consistency of fitted models.
- Two robustness aspects claimed: (1) improved consistency when minimizing surrogate losses (e.g. multiclass logistic) instead of task losses (e.g. 0-1), where aggregated labels can achieve consistent/optimal prediction when impossible without aggregation; (2) even in finite-dimensional statistical problems, aggregation can provide consistent classifiers when standard methods fail.
- Existing surrogate risk consistency theory typically assumes standard supervised pairs (X,Y) and does not address aggregation.
- Main questions: whether aggregation is needed; if used, whether/how it helps consistency.
- Paper promises concrete examples in ranking and binary/multiclass classification with linear estimators where estimators using only (X,Y) necessarily fail, but label aggregation yields consistency.
- Paper develops notions/theory for surrogate consistency with data aggregation.
- In fully nonparametric scenarios, it will show how number of samples aggregated combines with noise conditions to improve consistency.
- Aggregation is claimed to allow surrogate risk consistency under weak conditions on surrogate loss; losses using aggregated labels admit approximate linear comparison inequalities.
- Unlike conventional risk consistency theory, which requires hypothesis class F of all measurable functions, paper claims aggregation can guarantee consistency even over restricted hypothesis classes, which may fail without aggregation.

Paper title: “Some Robustness Properties of Label Cleaning” by Chen Cheng and John Duchi.

Main claims from abstract/introduction: label aggregation/cleaning gives robustness and stronger consistency guarantees than raw noisy labels, including surrogate-risk consistency and consistency under parametric misspecification. Aggregation can allow optimal classifiers where standard raw-label approaches fail. It may work even with restricted hypothesis classes, not only all measurable functions.

Section 2 setup:
- Data (X_i,Y_i) iid P, scoring function f:X→R^d, decoder d:R^d→Y, prediction d∘f(x).
- Task risk initially equation (1): R(f)=E_P[ell(d∘f(X),Y)]. Binary example: d=1, decoder sgn(s), ell(y,y’)=1{yy’≤0}, so R(f)=P(Y f(X)≤0).
- They then generalize task loss to depend on conditional distribution P(Y∈·|X), equation (2): R(f)=E_P[ell(d∘f(X),P(·|X))]. Multiclass example: ell(yhat,P)=sum_y P(Y=y)1{yhat≠y}, coincides with standard 0-1 error.
- Surrogate loss φ:R^d×Y→R; surrogate risk R_φ(f)=E_P[φ(f(X),Y)]. Study consistency of surrogate minimization for task problem (2).
- Two scenarios: (i) Fisher consistency with F all Borel functions; (ii) statistical/parametric F possibly misspecified. Main message: label aggregation improves consistency in both.

Section 2.1 label aggregation:
- Instead of output Y, observe abstract Z∈Z. Example: multiple noisy labels Z=(Y_1,…,Y_m)∈Y^m.
- Aggregation space A-space, aggregation function A:Z→A (e.g. majority vote), surrogate φ:R^d×A→R_+.
- Aggregated surrogate risk equation (3): R_{φ,A}(f)=E[φ(f(X),A(Z))]. Question: when minimizing (3) suffices to minimize task risk (2).
- Example 1 Majority vote/repeated sampling: Z=(Y_1,…,Y_m), Y_i|X=x iid P_{Y|X=x}. Define A_m(Z)=argmin_{y∈Y} sum_{l=1}^m ell(y,Y_l). For 0-1 loss ell(yhat,y)=1{y≠yhat}, this is majority vote; general form allows abstract procedures.
- Example 2 KNN aggregation: example X has label Y plus additional iid sample (X_i,Y_i)_{i=1}^m, Z=(Y,(X_i,Y_i)_{i=1}^m). Order X_i by distance to X, set X_(0)=X. For K≥0, aggregate K-nearest neighbors plus original point via A_{m,K}(Z)=argmin_y sum_{l=0}^K ell(y,Y_(l)). Appendix C later extends to single-sample aggregation.

Section 3 surrogate consistency:

- Aggregation can restore consistency when m≥k independent pairwise comparisons Z=(Y_1,…,Y_m)|X are collected. Idea: regress predicted scores on frequencies of label orderings.
