final_notes:
Title: “Some Robustness Properties of Label Cleaning” by Chen Cheng and John Duchi. Thesis: aggregation/label cleaning improves robustness and task-risk consistency vs raw-label surrogate learning under misspecification/finite-dimensional restrictions.

Sec. 2: Data (X,Y), scores f:X→R^d, decoder d. Task risk R(f)=E ell(d∘f(X),Y) or distribution-dependent. Aggregated surrogate risk R_{φ,A}=Eφ(f(X),A(Z)) evaluated against original task risk. Repeated labels Z=(Y_1,...,Y_m) iid conditional on X; majority/generalized empirical task-loss minimizer A_m/T4K.

Sec. 3: Prop. 1: for k≥3 pairwise ranking, every convex single-label surrogate fails Q7D. Prop. 2: expanded response q∈R^k plus star/square loss with comparison-count aggregation gives Q7D if m≥k. Cor. 3.2 finite label + instantaneous loss + m(n)→∞ + W3C ⇒ aggregated surrogate excess→0 implies task excess→0. W3C identifying surrogate constants C_{φ,1}, C_{φ,2}; binary hinge W3C (1,2). Theorem 1 gives linear excess-risk bound above threshold ξ. Potential internal errors: formulas undefined at α=1 though text discusses α=1/ξ=0; corollary text claims finite m at α=1. Sec. 3.3 examples: matching W3C C1=1/N,C2=2; structured hinge/A3J W3C with C1=min loss, C2=max τ+1. General structured bound factor 8/min ell conflicts with Theorem 1’s 16/C1 unless sharper unannounced result.

Sec. 4: Restricted/parametric classes. Binary setting: Y={±1}, 0-1 risk P(Y f(X)≤0), margin surrogate φ(s,y)=φ(sy), linear f_θ(x)=<θ,x>. K7M/optimal predictability: sgn(<θ*,x>)=sgn(P(Y=1|x)-1/2), so f_{θ*} minimizes task risk over all measurable functions. Prop. 4: for any ε>0 and nonzero θ*, some P satisfies K7M along θ*, yet every unaggregated surrogate minimizer has worse task risk than θ* and is nearly orthogonal, for any nonnegative loss φ. Cor. 4.1 claims from Theorem 2 that aggregated approximate minimizers have R(f_{θ_m})→R(f_{θ*}) and cos angle→1; angle part not supported by Theorem 2 as stated. Theorem 2: If cone F satisfies K7M, P(Δ(X)>0)=1, ε_m→0, then every ε_m-argmin of aggregated surrogate over F has R(f_m)→R*.

Sec. 4.3 multiclass: Prop. 5 for k≥3 Gaussian X, logistic link; tiny misspecification set T_ε causes Θ_1 direction ≠ Θ*. Theorem 3: if Θ*=U*T*, aggregated estimators Θ_m=U*T_m with ||T_m||→∞ and T_m/||T_m||→T*/||T*||. Corruption link σ^ε definition/prose reversed inside/outside. General message: aggregation robust under ordering-consistent misspecification; unaggregated multiclass generally inconsistent.

Sec. 5 numerics: D4X/squared hinge φ(δ)=max{1−δ,0}^2, unaggregated ψ(ε)=ε^2; aggregated ψ_m=(1/16)(ε−sqrt(32 log40/m))_+ for m=2^16…2^32. Logistic misspecification experiment uses link σ~(t)=softmax(t) for ||t||≤r and softmax(αt) outside, d=2,k=3, θ1=(0,1), θ2=(1,1), r=3, α=.1, m={1,4,16,64,256,1024}. Internal error: Figure 2 says plotted error is || ||T_m||−T*/||T*|| ||, conflicting with Theorem 3’s directional convergence T_m/||T_m||→T*/||T*||.

Sec. 6 discussion: acknowledges many results need m→∞; ranking has explicit finite-m guarantees; finite-m theory for general (ell,φ,m) open. Says beyond binary, κ(X) can remain large even low noise α≈1; binary κ=1. Reiterates misspecified-model results require K7M/Bayes-optimal classifier in F; classical surrogate consistency can fail there while aggregation succeeds. Suggests restricted-class/H-consistency extensions.

Paper title: “Some Robustness Properties of Label Cleaning” by Chen Cheng and John Duchi. Abstract claims: Aggregated/cleaned labels distilled from noisy responses provide robustness not available without cleaning. Minimizing a typically convex surrogate loss with cleaned labels gives stronger task-risk consistency guarantees than raw-label procedures. Finite-dimensional classifiers remain consistent under loss misspecification, unlike standard uncertainty-modeling approaches which can fail. Perfectly specified statistical models may be more efficient by using all information, but slight loss misspecification can destroy standard consistency. Aggregation/label cleaning retains convergence to optimal classifiers; collection, fitting, and prediction together can gain robustness via noisy-signal refinement.

Intro claims: Aggregation permits consistent optimal prediction under surrogate rather than task loss when unaggregated estimation cannot, including finite-dimensional statistical problems. Linear-estimator constructions in ranking, binary, and multiclass classification separate procedures restricted to (X,Y) pairs from aggregation procedures. Nonparametric results combine aggregation count and noise conditions, allow approximately linear comparison inequalities under weak surrogate conditions, and extend consistency beyond unrestricted measurable hypothesis classes. Conventional supervised learning pipeline collects (X_i,Y_i), fits a model, and ignores cleaning/filtering/repeated crowdsourced labeling/denoising used in modern datasets. Crowdsourcing/gold-standard-label work studies that machinery, but this paper focuses on its fundamental, necessary improvement of fitted-model consistency. Prior surrogate-risk consistency theory covers binary zero-one classification, multi-label, ranking, structured prediction, ordinal regression, restricted classes, general theory; pair-based analyses admit empirical-process theory but not aggregation machinery. The questions are whether aggregation is needed, whether pair-based surrogate consistency suffices, and how aggregation improves consistency.

Abstract/intro: cleaned/aggregated labels provide robustness and stronger task-risk consistency than raw labels; finite-dimensional classifiers can stay consistent under surrogate/loss misspecification where standard uncertainty-modeling can fail. Aggregation may be less efficient than correctly specified full models but robust to slight misspecification. Paper aims to show aggregation is fundamentally necessary/improves consistency beyond pair-based surrogate theory, including examples in ranking, binary, multiclass and nonparametric settings.

Section 2 preliminaries: Two regimes: unrestricted Borel F with Fisher consistency, and parametric/misspecified F where aggregation improves consistency. Data (X_i,Y_i) iid P on X×Y. Scores f:X→R^d decoded by d:R^d→Y. Two task-risk formulations: distribution-dependent criterion R(f)=E[ ell(d∘f(X), P(.|X)) ] (eq 2), e.g. multiclass zero-one ell(yhat,P)=Σ_y P(Y=y)1{yhat≠y}; instantaneous criterion for ell:Y×Y→R_+, R(f)=E[ell(d∘f(X),Y)] (eq 1). Section 2.1 label aggregation: Aggregated surrogate risk R_{φ,A}(f)=E[φ(f(X),A(Z))] (eq 3), with response replacement Z∈Z, aggregation space A, map A:Z→A, and nonnegative surrogate φ:R^d×A→R_+. It is assessed against actual task-risk minimization, not ordinary (X,Y) response.

Repeated labeling setup: Z=(Y_1,…,Y_m)∈Y^m with Y_i|X=x iid from P_{Y|X=x}; aggregate A_m(Z)=argmin_{y∈Y} Σ_{l=1}^m ell(y,Y_l). For zero-one loss this is majority vote. General ell allows abstract aggregation; A_m notation tracks repetitions. KNN aggregation: observe X,Y plus independent sample (X_i,Y_i)_{i=1}^m iid P; sort neighbors by dist(X,X_(l)), set X_(0)=X; for K≥0 define A_{m,K}(Z)=argmin_y Σ_{l=0}^K ell(y,Y_(l)). Paper title: “Some Robustness Properties of Label Cleaning” by Chen Cheng and John Duchi.

Main claims from abstract/introduction: label cleaning/aggregation provides robustness impossible without aggregation. Two aspects: (1) improved surrogate-risk consistency (e.g. logistic vs task loss) where aggregated-label procedures can be consistent/optimal in limits where raw (X,Y) procedures cannot; (2) finite-dimensional/statistical settings where aggregation yields consistent classifiers when standard methods fail. Concrete examples promised in ranking and binary/multiclass classification with linear estimators; theory for surrogate consistency with data aggregation; fully nonparametric results on how number of aggregated samples and noise conditions improve consistency; aggregation allows approximate linear comparison inequalities and consistency under weak surrogate-loss conditions, including restricted hypothesis classes where non-aggregated methods may fail.

Section 2 preliminaries: Standard setup: data (X_i,Y_i) iid P on X×Y; scoring f:X→R^d, decoder d:R^d→Y. Task risk initially R(f)=E[ell(d∘f(X),Y)] (eq. 1). Binary example: d=1, decoder sgn(s), ell(y,y')=1{yy'≤0}, so R(f)=P(Y f(X)≤0). They then allow task loss to depend on conditional distribution P(Y∈·|X): R(f)=E[ell(d∘f(X),P(·|X))] (eq. 2), claiming minimizers frequently coincide with original task problem; multiclass example with ell(yhat,P)=Σ_y P(Y=y)1{yhat≠y} equals standard 0-1 error. Surrogate loss φ:R^d×Y→R, surrogate risk R_φ(f)=E[φ(f(X),Y)]. They study consistency in (i) Fisher/classical all Borel functions and (ii) parametric possibly misspecified hypothesis classes. Main message: label aggregation improves consistency in both.

Section 2.1 label aggregation: Instead of Y, observe abstract Z∈Z. Example multiple labels: Z=(Y_1,…,Y_m)∈Y^m. Aggregation space A, aggregating function A:Z→A (e.g. majority vote), surrogate φ:R^d×A→R_+, aggregated surrogate risk R_{φ,A}(f)=E[φ(f(X),A(Z))] (eq. 3). Question: when minimizing (3) suffices to minimize task risk (2).

Example 1 majority vote/repeated sampling: Y_i|X=x iid P_{Y|X=x}; A_m(Z)=argmin_{y∈Y} Σ_{l=1}^m ell(y,Y_l). For 0-1 ell this is majority vote; general form allows abstract procedures.

Example 2 KNN aggregation: Given X with label Y plus iid additional sample (X_i,Y_i)_{i=1}^m, Z=(Y,(X_i,Y_i)_1^m). Order X_i by distance to X, set X_(0)=X. For K≥0, aggregate K-nearest neighbors plus original point via A_{m,K}(Z)=argmin_{y∈Y} Σ_{l=0}^K ell(y,Y_(l)). Appendix C will address single-sample KNN aggregation beyond population-level setup.

Section 3 surrogate consistency. Assumes Fisher/classical setting where F is all Borel measurable f:X→R^d. Defines conditional task risk R(s|x)=ell(d∘s, P(Y|X=x)) and conditional surrogate risk R_phi(s|x)=E[phi(s,Y)|X=x]. Pointwise excess risks delta_ell, delta_phi subtract inf over s∈R^d. Minimal risks R*=inf_F R(f), R_phi*=inf_F R_phi(f). Consistency notions: (i) Fisher consistency: for all P, R_phi(f_n)→R_phi* implies R(f_n)→R*. (ii) uniform comparison: nondecreasing psi with psi(eps)>0 for eps>0 and psi(R(f)-R*)≤R_phi(f)-R_phi* for all f. In binary classification with convex margin losses, these coincide. Calibration: psi(eps,x)=inf{delta_phi(s,x): delta_ell(s,x)≥eps}; overline psi(eps)=inf_x psi(eps,x). Cor. 3.1: phi Fisher consistent iff psi(eps,x)>0 for all x, eps>0. Let psi be Fenchel biconjugate of overline psi; overline psi(eps)>0 iff psi(eps)>0, and comparison inequality holds for all measurable f.

They argue in general risk problem (2), one would like Fisher-consistent surrogate using single paired (X,Y), but this is generally impossible; motivates aggregation theory in Sec. 3.2.

Sec. 3.1 ranking example: k items, labels Y=(i,j), i≠j, indicating i ranked above j. For each x, p_ij=P(Y=(i,j)|x). Define normalized transition matrix C_x with diagonal 0 and off-diagonal (C_x)_ij=p_ij / sum_{l≠j} p_lj, with 0/0=1/(k−1), so C_x^T 1=1. Rank by vector C_x 1 (preference counts). Task loss (decoder incorporated) ell(s,C)=max_{i<j} 1{(s_i−s_j)(e_i−e_j)^T C1 ≤0, (e_i−e_j)^T C1≠0}, penalizing misordered score pairs. Population task risk (4): R(f)=P(f(X) and C_X 1 order differently). Scores restricted to s∈R^k with s^T1=0 since only ordering matters. Proposition 1: for k≥3, no convex surrogate phi:R^k×Y→R is Fisher consistent for ranking risk (4) (proof App. A.1).

Aggregation for ranking: collect m independent pairwise comparisons Z=(Y_1,…,Y_m)|X. If m≥k, define counts m_ij (intended frequency of pair (i,j)) and m_j=sum_i m_ij. Aggregator A(Z)=star if any m_j=0; otherwise returns vector over i: (m_i1/m_1 + m_i2/m_2 + … + m_ik/m_k). Claim: regressing predicted scores f(x) directly on A(Z) when not star yields consistency; Proposition 2 begins next.

Paper title: “Some Robustness Properties of Label Cleaning” by Chen Cheng and John Duchi.

Core setup/results: iid (X,Y), scores f:X→R^d decoded by d; surrogate R_φ and aggregated surrogate R_{φ,A}. Calibration/Q7D definitions; aggregated Q7D iff pointwise aggregated calibration. Cor 3.2: if m(n)→∞ and W3C etc., small aggregated surrogate excess implies task excess→0. W3C constants C1,C2. Theorem 1 finite-m threshold issues noted earlier. Binary margin Lemma 3.1 W3C constants. Structured hinge/matching Lemmas 3.2/3.3 with prior issues: A_n typo, structured consistency threshold missing leading 4 and slope 8/min loss.

Section 4 restricted/parametric: Prop 4 binary linear says for any ε>0 and nonzero θ*, some distribution P satisfies K7M along θ*, yet every unaggregated surrogate minimizer θ_φ has higher task risk than θ* and |cos angle(θ_φ,θ*)|≤ε, for any nonnegative loss. Cor 4.1 claims aggregated approximate minimizers θ_m for majority/T4K with ε_m→0 satisfy risk convergence and cos angle→1; internal issue: Theorem 2 only states risk convergence, not angular convergence, and assumes P(Δ>0)=1 etc.

Theorem 2: multiclass zero-one, argmax decoder, f^T1=0, cone closed under positive scaling, nonnegative Q7D surrogate with limiting condition φ(s,y)→0 when correct margin→∞. If cone F satisfies K7M for P and P(Δ(X)>0)=1, then ε_m-argmin of aggregated surrogate risk under majority A_m has R(f_m)→R*. Unique population maximizer y*(x). Examples: multiclass logistic, pairwise convex margin losses.

Section 4.3 finite-dimensional multiclass: Prop 5: k≥3, Gaussian Z, invertibility of map M↦E[Z(∇σ^lr(Θ*^T Z)MZ)^T]; for each small ε there is bad set T_ε measure≤ε such that Θ_1(ε)/||Θ_1(ε)|| ≠ Θ*/||Θ*||. Theorem 3: if Θ*=U*T* with U* orthogonal and T* nonsingular, for each m exists Θ_m=U*T_m with ||T_m||→∞ and T_m/||T_m||→T*/||T*||. Multilabel Y_ij iid Cat(p_{Θ*}(X_i)); majority labels Y_i^+=A_m(...), inducing p_{Θ*,m}; ρ_m is T4K distribution and ordering-consistent.

Section 5 numerical illustrations: claims two experiments corroborate nonparametric amplification and finite-dimensional multiclass consistency under link misspecification. D4X/squared hinge φ(δ)=max{1−δ,0}^2; exact unaggregated H8N ψ(ε)=ε^2. With δ=1, α=0, C_MT=1, aggregated lower curve ψ_m(ε)=1/16(ε−sqrt((32/m)log40))_+. Fig 1 uses m={2^16,2^20,2^24,2^28,2^32}. Logistic misspecification experiment uses piecewise link σ~(t)=σlr(t) for ||t||≤r and σlr(αt) for ||t||>r; d=2,k=3, θ1*=(0,1), θ2*=(1,1), r=3, α=.1, m={1,4,16,64,256,1024}, 100 trials, 95% bars. Two designs: n=10000 each m, and constant total labels n=640000/m. Internal error in Section 5: Fig 2 says plotted error is || ||T_m||−T*/||T*|| ||, but Theorem 3 target is ||T_m/||T_m||−T*/||T*||||.

Section 6 discussion: frames results as showing limitations of uncleaned labels and robustness gains from cleaning. Notes many consistency results require m→∞; finite-m theory remains open except ranking explicit guarantees, and some item comparisons may need increasing counts. Discusses fundamental limits of B2Z/κ beyond binary; binary κ=1. Mis-specified-model discussion says results require K7M/Bayes-optimal classifier in F; classical surrogate consistency can fail even there while aggregation succeeds. Future work: H-consistency/restricted-class aggregation comparisons and hypothesis-class size effects.

Paper title: “Some Robustness Properties of Label Cleaning” by Chen Cheng and John Duchi.

Abstract claims:
- Aggregated/cleaned labels distilled from noisy responses provide robustness not available without cleaning.
- Minimizing a typically convex surrogate loss with cleaned/aggregated labels yields stronger task-risk consistency guarantees than procedures using raw labels.
- Finite-dimensional classifiers remain consistent under loss misspecification that defeats standard uncertainty-modeling approaches.
- If statistical models are perfectly specified, incorporating all information is more efficient, but even slight loss misspecification destroys standard consistency.
- Aggregation/label cleaning retains convergence to optimal classifiers.
- Overall theme: collection, fitting, and prediction can be jointly robust through noisy-signal refinement.

Introduction claims:
- Aggregation permits consistent optimal prediction under surrogate rather than task loss when unaggregated estimation cannot, including finite-dimensional statistical problems.
- Linear-estimator constructions in ranking, binary classification, and multiclass classification separate procedures restricted to (X,Y) pairs from aggregation procedures.
- Nonparametric results combine aggregation count and noise conditions, permit approximately linear comparison inequalities under weak surrogate conditions, and extend consistency beyond unrestricted measurable hypothesis classes.
- Conventional supervised pipeline collects (X_i,Y_i), fits a model, and suppresses cleaning/filtering/repeated crowdsourced labeling/denoising used in modern datasets.
- Work on crowdsourced “gold standard” labels is related, but this paper focuses on fundamental, necessary improvement of fitted-model consistency.
- The paper frames its questions as: whether aggregation is needed, whether pair-based surrogate consistency suffices, and in what sense aggregation improves consistency.

Paper title: “Some Robustness Properties of Label Cleaning” by Chen Cheng and John Duchi.

Earlier abstract/introduction claims:
- Cleaned/aggregated labels from noisy responses provide robustness/consistency not available without cleaning.
- Minimizing convex-ish surrogate losses with cleaned labels gives stronger task-risk consistency than raw-label procedures.
- Finite-dimensional/parametric classifiers remain consistent under loss misspecification that defeats uncertainty-modeling approaches; perfectly specified models using all info may be more efficient, but slight misspecification destroys standard consistency.
- Linear-estimator examples in ranking, binary, multiclass separate pair-based procedures from aggregation.
- Nonparametric results combine aggregation count and noise conditions, weak surrogate assumptions, and extend beyond unrestricted measurable classes.

Section 2 preliminaries:
- Two regimes: unrestricted Borel F with classical Fisher consistency; parametric/misspecified F where aggregation improves consistency.
- Data: iid (X_i,Y_i)~P on X×Y. Scores f:X→R^d decoded by d:R^d→Y, prediction d∘f(x).
- Distribution-dependent task criterion defined as R(f)=E_P[ ell(d∘f(X), P(.|X)) ] (eq. 2). For multiclass Y={1,…,k}, ell(yhat,P)=Σ_y P(Y=y)1{yhat≠y}, yielding standard 0-1 error.
- Instantaneous formulation for ell:Y×Y→R_+ minimizes R(f)=E_P[ell(d∘f(X),Y)] over f∈F (eq. 1). Binary: d=1, d(s)=sgn(s), ell(y,y')=1{yy'≤0}, so R(f)=P(Y f(X)≤0). Task losses nonsmooth/nonconvex/flat; surrogate φ:R^d×Y→R gives R_φ(f)=E φ(f(X),Y). Need consistency with task.

Section 2.1 label aggregation:
- Aggregated surrogate risk R_{φ,A}(f)=E[φ(f(X),A(Z))] (eq. 3), assessed against actual task-risk minimization. Z∈Z, aggregation space A, map A:Z→A, φ:R^d×A→R_+.
- Repeated labeling: Z=(Y_1,…,Y_m), Y_i|X=x iid~P_{Y|X=x}. Aggregator A_m(Z)=argmin_y Σ_{l=1}^m ell(y,Y_l); for 0-1 loss this is majority vote. General ell allows abstract aggregation.
- Rough KNN aggregation: observe X,Y plus independent sample (X_i,Y_i)_{i=1}^m iid~P; Z=(Y,(X_i,Y_i)). Order neighbors by dist(X,X_(1))≤…≤dist(X,X_(m)), set X_(0)=X. For K≥0, A_{m,K}(Z)=argmin_y Σ_{l=0}^K ell(y,Y_(l)). Population repeated-sampling treatment extends to one-sample aggregation in Appendix C.

Paper title: “Some Robustness Properties of Label Cleaning” by Chen Cheng and John Duchi.

Main claims from abstract/introduction: label cleaning/aggregation provides robustness impossible without aggregation. Two aspects: (1) improved surrogate-risk consistency (e.g. logistic vs task loss) where aggregated-label procedures can be consistent/optimal in limits where raw (X,Y) procedures cannot; (2) finite-dimensional/statistical settings where aggregation yields consistent classifiers when standard methods fail. Concrete examples promised in ranking and binary/multiclass classification with linear estimators; theory for surrogate consistency with data aggregation; fully nonparametric results on how number of aggregated samples and noise conditions improve consistency; aggregation allows approximate linear comparison inequalities and consistency under weak surrogate-loss conditions, including restricted hypothesis classes where non-aggregated methods may fail.

Section 2 preliminaries: Standard setup: data (X_i,Y_i) iid P on X×Y; scoring f:X→R^d, decoder d:R^d→Y. Task risk initially R(f)=E[ell(d∘f(X),Y)] (eq. 1). Binary example: d=1, decoder sgn(s), ell(y,y')=1{yy'≤0}, so R(f)=P(Y f(X)≤0). They then allow task loss to depend on conditional distribution P(Y∈·|X): R(f)=E[ell(d∘f(X),P(·|X))] (eq. 2), claiming minimizers frequently coincide with original task problem; multiclass example with ell(yhat,P)=Σ_y P(Y=y)1{yhat≠y} equals standard 0-1 error. Surrogate loss φ:R^d×Y→R, surrogate risk R_φ(f)=E[φ(f(X),Y)]. They study consistency in (i) Fisher/classical all Borel functions and (ii) parametric possibly misspecified hypothesis classes. Main message: label aggregation improves consistency in both.

Section 2.1 label aggregation: Instead of Y, observe abstract Z∈Z. Example multiple labels: Z=(Y_1,…,Y_m)∈Y^m. Aggregation space A, aggregating function A:Z→A (e.g. majority vote), surrogate φ:R^d×A→R_+, aggregated surrogate risk R_{φ,A}(f)=E[φ(f(X),A(Z))] (eq. 3). Question: when minimizing (3) suffices to minimize task risk (2).

Example 1 majority vote/repeated sampling: Y_i|X=x iid P_{Y|X=x}; A_m(Z)=argmin_{y∈Y} Σ_{l=1}^m ell(y,Y_l). For 0-1 ell this is majority vote; general form allows abstract procedures.

Example 2 KNN aggregation: Given X with label Y plus iid additional sample (X_i,Y_i)_{i=1}^m, Z=(Y,(X_i,Y_i)_1^m). Order X_i by distance to X, set X_(0)=X. For K≥0, aggregate K-nearest neighbors plus original point via A_{m,K}(Z)=argmin_{y∈Y} Σ_{l=0}^K ell(y,Y_(l)). Appendix C will address single-sample KNN aggregation beyond population-level setup.

Section 3 surrogate consistency. Assumes Fisher/classical setting where F is all Borel measurable f:X→R^d. Defines conditional task risk R(s|x)=ell(d∘s, P(Y|X=x)) and conditional surrogate risk R_phi(s|x)=E[phi(s,Y)|X=x]. Pointwise excess risks delta_ell, delta_phi subtract inf over s∈R^d. Minimal risks R*=inf_F R(f), R_phi*=inf_F R_phi(f). Consistency notions: (i) Fisher consistency: for all P, R_phi(f_n)→R_phi* implies R(f_n)→R*. (ii) uniform comparison: nondecreasing psi with psi(eps)>0 for eps>0 and psi(R(f)-R*)≤R_phi(f)-R_phi* for all f. In binary classification with convex margin losses, these coincide. Calibration: psi(eps,x)=inf{delta_phi(s,x): delta_ell(s,x)≥eps}; overline psi(eps)=inf_x psi(eps,x). Cor. 3.1: phi Fisher consistent iff psi(eps,x)>0 for all x, eps>0. Let psi be Fenchel biconjugate of overline psi; overline psi(eps)>0 iff psi(eps)>0, and comparison inequality holds for all measurable f.

They argue in general risk problem (2), one would like Fisher-consistent surrogate using single paired (X,Y), but this is generally impossible; motivates aggregation theory in Sec. 3.2.

Sec. 3.1 ranking example: k items, labels Y=(i,j), i≠j, indicating i ranked above j. For each x, p_ij=P(Y=(i,j)|x). Define normalized transition matrix C_x with diagonal 0 and off-diagonal (C_x)_ij=p_ij / sum_{l≠j} p_lj, with 0/0=1/(k−1), so C_x^T 1=1. Rank by vector C_x 1 (preference counts). Task loss (decoder incorporated) ell(s,C)=max_{i<j} 1{(s_i−s_j)(e_i−e_j)^T C1 ≤0, (e_i−e_j)^T C1≠0}, penalizing misordered score pairs. Population task risk (4): R(f)=P(f(X) and C_X 1 order differently). Scores restricted to s∈R^k with s^T1=0 since only ordering matters. Proposition 1: for k≥3, no convex surrogate phi:R^k×Y→R is Fisher consistent for ranking risk (4) (proof App. A.1).

Aggregation for ranking: collect m independent pairwise comparisons Z=(Y_1,…,Y_m)|X. If m≥k, define counts m_ij (intended frequency of pair (i,j)) and m_j=sum_i m_ij. Aggregator A(Z)=star if any m_j=0; otherwise returns vector over i: (m_i1/m_1 + m_i2/m_2 + … + m_ik/m_k). Claim: regressing predicted scores f(x) directly on A(Z) when not star yields consistency; Proposition 2 begins next.

errors.claim: “m_{ij}=\sum_{y\in\mathcal Y^m}1\{y=(i,j)\}”
errors.evidence: Immediately before, the paper says “For multiple independent comparisons Z=(Y_1,\ldots,Y_m) conditional on X, put …” and then defines A(Z) using the quantities m_{ij} and m_j as empirical counts.
errors.explanation: As written, m_{ij} sums over all possible tuples y∈Y^m rather than over the observed comparisons in Z, so it does not count occurrences in Z and generally is not a function of Z. This conflicts with the stated purpose of defining an aggregation A(Z) from the observed multiple comparisons.

errors.claim: “\overline\psi_A(\epsilon)\coloneqq \inf_{s\in\mathbb R^d}\overline\psi_A(\epsilon,x)”
errors.evidence: The preceding analogous construction defines the uniform form as “\overline\psi(\epsilon)\coloneqq \inf_{x\in\mathcal X}\psi(\epsilon,x).” Also, \overline\psi_A(\epsilon,x) has already minimized over s: “\overline\psi_A(\epsilon,x)\coloneqq \inf_{s\in\mathbb R^d}\{...\}.”
errors.explanation: The uniform calibration function should vary over x, as in the earlier definition. Taking an infimum over s of an expression still containing x is inconsistent with both the earlier pointwise/uniform construction and the just-given definition that already optimized over s.

errors.claim: “Low noise permits a comparison written as ψ(R(f)−R*) ≤ R_φ(f)−R* …”
errors.evidence: Definition 3.2 immediately below requires “ψ(R(f)−R*) ≤ R_{φ,A}(f)−R_{φ,A}*.” Earlier notes likewise record the standard comparison as “ψ(R(f)−R*)≤R_φ(f)−R_φ*.”
errors.explanation: The right-hand side should be surrogate excess risk, subtracting the surrogate optimum, not the task optimum R*. The claim as written mixes surrogate risk with task-risk optimum and contradicts the paper’s own comparison definitions.

errors.claim: “The crude bound κ(x)≤1/Δ(x), choosing M=1 for card(Y)=k=2 and optimizing M otherwise, lower bounds the promised ξ_{m,k} by setting …”

errors.explanation: For Corollary 3.3 to follow from Theorem 1, ξ_{m,k} must be an upper/conservative bound on the theorem’s required threshold, not merely a lower bound. A lower bound on the threshold would not ensure the theorem’s hypothesis is met.

errors.claim: “R(f)-R^\star\leq 16N\bigl(R_{\varphi,A_n}(f)-R_{\varphi,A_n}^\star\bigr).”

errors.explanation: The bound switches from A_m to A_n although the aggregation/repetition parameter in the statement is m. This conflicts with the paper’s own notation for aggregation count.

final_notes:
Paper title: “Some Robustness Properties of Label Cleaning” by Chen Cheng and John Duchi.

Setup: iid (X,Y), scores f:X→R^d decoded by d, task risk, surrogate risk R_φ, aggregated surrogate R_{φ,A}. A_m repeated-label aggregator minimizes empirical task loss. Q7D calibration gives ψ(R−R*)≤surrogate excess; pair-only Q7D often impossible. Prop1 convex pairwise ranking fails Q7D for k≥3; Prop2 squared loss with aggregation can be Q7D. Prior issues: ranking aggregation formula sums over y∈Y^m instead of observed indices; Eq (5) overlineψ_A uses wrong inf/pointwise form.

Aggregation consistency: Prop3 aggregated Q7D iff pointwise aggregated calibration positive; Cor3.2 m(n)→∞ and W3C φ + small aggregated surrogate excess implies task excess→0. W3C constants C1,C2 via (6a)(6b); hinge W3C (1,2). Theorem1: W3C+J9P+bounded loss+Nα gives linear comparison R−R*≤16/C1 aggregated surrogate excess above threshold involving P(κ>M), e_m(M), ξ_m. Coarse ξ_{m,k}; text wrongly says “lower bounds” threshold. U6A level-(ξ,ζ) has erroneous unaggregated comparison. Noise definitions Δ,Nα,Mβ; binary κ=1 only if Δ>0 a.s.; final discussion states unconditionally that binary κ=1, conflicting with this caveat.

Examples: binary margin convex φ Lemma3.1 C1=φ(0)−φ(δ), C2=φ(−δ). Matching: k=N!, d=N^2, loss 1/(2N)||v1−v2||_1=1/(2N)||·||_2^2; surrogate W3C C1=1/N,C2=2; threshold displayed; bound constant 16N but displayed with A_n despite m. Structured hinge Lemma3.3 W3C C1=min loss, C2=max τ+1; binary embeddings ℓ=1/(2d)||·||_1 give τ=1,C2=2. Structured app omits factor 4 in threshold and gives 8/min loss vs Theorem’s 16/C1.

Section4: Restricted classes. Prop4: for any ε>0 and nonzero θ*, some binary distribution satisfies K7M along θ*, yet every unaggregated surrogate minimizer has higher task risk than θ* and |cos angle|≤ε. Cor4.1 claims from Theorem2 risk→R(fθ*) and cos angle→1; flagged because Theorem2 only states risk consistency.

Theorem2: cone F satisfying K7M and P(Δ>0)=1, ε_m→0 aggregated approximate minimizers of R_{φ,A_m} have R(f_m)→R*. Multiclass: labels [k], zero-one, argmax, f^T1=0 cone; nonnegative Q7D φ with limiting condition. Unique population maximizer; T4K aggregation. Examples logistic and pairwise convex losses.

Section4.3 finite-dimensional multiclass. Prop5 k≥3, Σ=I, invertibility of DM for logistic link; small perturbation set T_ε measure ≤ε yields Θ_1(ε) direction not equal Θ*/norm. Theorem3: if Θ*=U*T* with U orthogonal, T* nonsingular, then for each m exists Θ_m=U*T_m with ||T_m||→∞ and direction T_m/||T_m||→T*/||T*||.

Part 9: numerical illustrations. D4X binary squared-hinge/truncated quadratic φ(δ)=max{1−δ,0}², unaggregated ψ(ε)=ε²; aggregated ψ_m=(1/16)(ε−sqrt(32 log40/m))_+, m in {2^16,...,2^32}. Section 2 preliminaries:
- Two regimes: unrestricted Borel F with classical Fisher consistency; parametric/misspecified F where aggregation improves consistency.
- Data: iid (X_i,Y_i)~P on X×Y. Scores f:X→R^d decoded by d:R^d→Y, prediction d∘f(x).
- Distribution-dependent task criterion defined as R(f)=E_P[ ell(d∘f(X), P(.|X)) ] (eq. 2). For multiclass Y={1,…,k}, ell(yhat,P)=Σ_y P(Y=y)1{yhat≠y}, yielding standard 0-1 error.
- Instantaneous formulation for ell:Y×Y→R_+ minimizes R(f)=E_P[ell(d∘f(X),Y)] over f∈F (eq. 1). Binary: d=1, d(s)=sgn(s), ell(y,y')=1{yy'≤0}, so R(f)=P(Y f(X)≤0). Task losses nonsmooth/nonconvex/flat; surrogate φ:R^d×Y→R gives R_φ(f)=E φ(f(X),Y). Need consistency with task.

Section 2.1 label aggregation:

Paper title: “Some Robustness Properties of Label Cleaning” by Chen Cheng and John Duchi.

Abstract claims:
- Learning procedures relying on aggregated labels / cleaned labels distilled from noisy responses have robustness properties impossible without data cleaning.
- In risk consistency setting (minimizing surrogate loss instead of task loss like 0-1 error), procedures using label aggregation obtain stronger consistency guarantees than possible using raw labels.
- Classical perfectly specified statistical modeling suggests incorporating all information / modeling label uncertainty is statistically efficient, but consistency fails for “standard” approaches when the minimized loss is even slightly misspecified.
- Procedures leveraging aggregated information still converge to optimal classifiers, suggesting robustness from considering the full data pipeline (collection, fitting, prediction) and refining noisy signals.

Paper title: “Some Robustness Properties of Label Cleaning” by Chen Cheng and John Duchi.

Abstract/introduction main claims:
- Modern supervised datasets often involve data cleaning/filtering/crowdsourcing multiple labels and denoising/aggregating them into “gold standard” labels.
- Paper argues label cleaning / label aggregation provides robustness impossible without aggregation.
- Two robustness aspects: (1) improved consistency when minimizing surrogate loss (e.g. multiclass logistic) instead of task loss (e.g. zero-one error): aggregated-label procedures can achieve consistent/optimal prediction in limits where raw (X,Y) procedures cannot; (2) in finite-dimensional statistical problems, aggregation can yield consistent classifiers when standard methods fail.
- Classical surrogate risk consistency literature usually assumes standard pairs (X,Y) and does not address modern aggregation machinery.
- Motivating questions: whether aggregation is needed for surrogate consistency; whether/how aggregation helps.
- Paper will give concrete examples in ranking and binary/multiclass classification with linear estimators where estimators using only pairs (X,Y) necessarily fail, but label aggregation methods are consistent.
- Paper develops new notions/theory for surrogate consistency with data aggregation.
- In fully nonparametric scenarios, paper claims to show how number of samples aggregated and noise conditions improve consistency.
- Aggregation supposedly allows surrogate risk consistency under weak conditions on the surrogate loss; losses using aggregated labels admit approximate linear comparison inequalities.
- Unlike conventional risk consistency theory requiring hypothesis class F to be all measurable functions, paper will show classification results where aggregation guarantees consistency over restricted hypothesis classes, which may fail without aggregation.

Paper title: “Some Robustness Properties of Label Cleaning” by Chen Cheng and John Duchi.

Main claims from abstract/introduction: label cleaning/aggregation provides robustness impossible without aggregation. Two aspects: (1) improved surrogate-risk consistency (e.g. logistic vs task loss) where aggregated-label procedures can be consistent/optimal in limits where raw (X,Y) procedures cannot; (2) finite-dimensional/statistical settings where aggregation yields consistent classifiers when standard methods fail. Concrete examples promised in ranking and binary/multiclass classification with linear estimators; theory for surrogate consistency with data aggregation; fully nonparametric results on how number of aggregated samples and noise conditions improve consistency; aggregation allows approximate linear comparison inequalities and consistency under weak surrogate-loss conditions, including restricted hypothesis classes where non-aggregated methods may fail.

Section 2 preliminaries: Standard setup: data (X_i,Y_i) iid P on X×Y; scoring f:X→R^d, decoder d:R^d→Y. Task risk initially R(f)=E[ell(d∘f(X),Y)] (eq. 1). Binary example: d=1, decoder sgn(s), ell(y,y')=1{yy'≤0}, so R(f)=P(Y f(X)≤0). They then allow task loss to depend on conditional distribution P(Y∈·|X): R(f)=E[ell(d∘f(X),P(·|X))] (eq. 2), claiming minimizers frequently coincide with original task problem; multiclass example with ell(yhat,P)=Σ_y P(Y=y)1{yhat≠y} equals standard 0-1 error. Surrogate loss φ:R^d×Y→R, surrogate risk R_φ(f)=E[φ(f(X),Y)]. They study consistency in (i) Fisher/classical all Borel functions and (ii) parametric possibly misspecified hypothesis classes. Main message: label aggregation improves consistency in both.

Section 2.1 label aggregation: Instead of Y, observe abstract Z∈Z. Example multiple labels: Z=(Y_1,…,Y_m)∈Y^m. Aggregation space A, aggregating function A:Z→A (e.g. majority vote), surrogate φ:R^d×A→R_+, aggregated surrogate risk R_{φ,A}(f)=E[φ(f(X),A(Z))] (eq. 3). Question: when minimizing (3) suffices to minimize task risk (2).

Example 1 majority vote/repeated sampling: Y_i|X=x iid P_{Y|X=x}; A_m(Z)=argmin_{y∈Y} Σ_{l=1}^m ell(y,Y_l). For 0-1 ell this is majority vote; general form allows abstract procedures.

Example 2 KNN aggregation: Given X with label Y plus iid additional sample (X_i,Y_i)_{i=1}^m, Z=(Y,(X_i,Y_i)_1^m). Order X_i by distance to X, set X_(0)=X. For K≥0, aggregate K-nearest neighbors plus original point via A_{m,K}(Z)=argmin_{y∈Y} Σ_{l=0}^K ell(y,Y_(l)). Appendix C will address single-sample KNN aggregation beyond population-level setup.

Section 3 surrogate consistency. Assumes Fisher/classical setting where F is all Borel measurable f:X→R^d. Defines conditional task risk R(s|x)=ell(d∘s, P(Y|X=x)) and conditional surrogate risk R_phi(s|x)=E[phi(s,Y)|X=x]. Pointwise excess risks delta_ell, delta_phi subtract inf over s∈R^d. Minimal risks R*=inf_F R(f), R_phi*=inf_F R_phi(f). Consistency notions: (i) Fisher consistency: for all P, R_phi(f_n)→R_phi* implies R(f_n)→R*. (ii) uniform comparison: nondecreasing psi with psi(eps)>0 for eps>0 and psi(R(f)-R*)≤R_phi(f)-R_phi* for all f. In binary classification with convex margin losses, these coincide. Calibration: psi(eps,x)=inf{delta_phi(s,x): delta_ell(s,x)≥eps}; overline psi(eps)=inf_x psi(eps,x). Cor. 3.1: phi Fisher consistent iff psi(eps,x)>0 for all x, eps>0. Let psi be Fenchel biconjugate of overline psi; overline psi(eps)>0 iff psi(eps)>0, and comparison inequality holds for all measurable f.

They argue in general risk problem (2), one would like Fisher-consistent surrogate using single paired (X,Y), but this is generally impossible; motivates aggregation theory in Sec. 3.2.

Sec. 3.1 ranking example: k items, labels Y=(i,j), i≠j, indicating i ranked above j. For each x, p_ij=P(Y=(i,j)|x). Define normalized transition matrix C_x with diagonal 0 and off-diagonal (C_x)_ij=p_ij / sum_{l≠j} p_lj, with 0/0=1/(k−1), so C_x^T 1=1. Rank by vector C_x 1 (preference counts). Task loss (decoder incorporated) ell(s,C)=max_{i<j} 1{(s_i−s_j)(e_i−e_j)^T C1 ≤0, (e_i−e_j)^T C1≠0}, penalizing misordered score pairs. Population task risk (4): R(f)=P(f(X) and C_X 1 order differently). Scores restricted to s∈R^k with s^T1=0 since only ordering matters. Proposition 1: for k≥3, no convex surrogate phi:R^k×Y→R is Fisher consistent for ranking risk (4) (proof App. A.1).

Aggregation for ranking: collect m independent pairwise comparisons Z=(Y_1,…,Y_m)|X. If m≥k, define counts m_ij (intended frequency of pair (i,j)) and m_j=sum_i m_ij. Aggregator A(Z)=star if any m_j=0; otherwise returns vector over i: (m_i1/m_1 + m_i2/m_2 + … + m_ik/m_k). Claim: regressing predicted scores f(x) directly on A(Z) when not star yields consistency; Proposition 2 begins next.

errors.claim: “m_{ij}=\sum_{y\in\mathcal Y^m}1\{y=(i,j)\}”
errors.evidence: Immediately before, the paper says “For multiple independent comparisons Z=(Y_1,\ldots,Y_m) conditional on X, put …” and then defines A(Z) using the quantities m_{ij} and m_j as empirical counts.
errors.explanation: As written, m_{ij} sums over all possible tuples y∈Y^m rather than over the observed comparisons in Z, so it does not count occurrences in Z and generally is not a function of Z. This conflicts with the stated purpose of defining an aggregation A(Z) from the observed multiple comparisons.

errors.claim: “\overline\psi_A(\epsilon)\coloneqq \inf_{s\in\mathbb R^d}\overline\psi_A(\epsilon,x)”
errors.evidence: The preceding analogous construction defines the uniform form as “\overline\psi(\epsilon)\coloneqq \inf_{x\in\mathcal X}\psi(\epsilon,x).” Also, \overline\psi_A(\epsilon,x) has already minimized over s: “\overline\psi_A(\epsilon,x)\coloneqq \inf_{s\in\mathbb R^d}\{...\}.”
errors.explanation: The uniform calibration function should vary over x, as in the earlier definition. Taking an infimum over s of an expression still containing x is inconsistent with both the earlier pointwise/uniform construction and the just-given definition that already optimized over s.

errors.claim: “Assume … condition (Nα), with α∈[0,1]” in Theorem 1, and later “at α=1, … gives ξ_{m,k}=0 and linear R2V.”

errors.explanation: The theorem and ξ formulas are not defined at α=1 because the denominators vanish, yet the text includes α=1 in the theorem’s range and then draws a conclusion for α=1 from ξ_{m,k}.

errors.claim: “Low noise permits a comparison written as ψ(R(f)−R*)≤R_φ(f)−R* …”

errors.explanation: The paragraph subtracts the task optimum R* from the surrogate risk R_φ(f), whereas both earlier theory and the immediately following definition subtract the surrogate optimum. This mixes risks on different scales and contradicts the paper’s own comparison form.

errors.claim: “every measurable f … satisfying [threshold] also satisfies R(f)-R* ≤ 8/min_{\hat y≠y} ell(\hat y,y) · (R_{\varphi,A_m}(f)-R_{\varphi,A_m}*)”

Section 2 preliminaries:
- Two regimes: unrestricted Borel F with classical Fisher consistency; parametric/misspecified F where aggregation improves consistency.
- Data: iid (X_i,Y_i)~P on X×Y. Scores f:X→R^d decoded by d:R^d→Y, prediction d∘f(x).
- Distribution-dependent task criterion defined as R(f)=E_P[ ell(d∘f(X), P(.|X)) ] (eq. 2). For multiclass Y={1,…,k}, ell(yhat,P)=Σ_y P(Y=y)1{yhat≠y}, yielding standard 0-1 error.
- Instantaneous formulation for ell:Y×Y→R_+ minimizes R(f)=E_P[ell(d∘f(X),Y)] over f∈F (eq. 1). Binary: d=1, d(s)=sgn(s), ell(y,y')=1{yy'≤0}, so R(f)=P(Y f(X)≤0). Task losses nonsmooth/nonconvex/flat; surrogate φ:R^d×Y→R gives R_φ(f)=E φ(f(X),Y). Need consistency with task.

Theorem 2: if F cone optimally predicts P, P(Δ(X)>0)=1, ε_m→0, f_m ε_m-minimizes aggregated surrogate risk with majority vote over m labels, then R(f_m)→R*.

Paper title: “Some Robustness Properties of Label Cleaning” by Chen Cheng and John Duchi.

Abstract claims:
- Learning procedures relying on aggregated labels / cleaned labels distilled from noisy responses have robustness properties impossible without data cleaning.

Paper title: “Some Robustness Properties of Label Cleaning” by Chen Cheng and John Duchi.

Abstract/introduction main claims:
- Modern supervised datasets often involve data cleaning/filtering/crowdsourcing multiple labels and denoising/aggregating them into “gold standard” labels.
- Paper argues label cleaning / label aggregation provides robustness impossible without aggregation.
- Two robustness aspects: (1) improved consistency when minimizing surrogate loss (e.g. multiclass logistic) instead of task loss (e.g. zero-one error): aggregated-label procedures can achieve consistent/optimal prediction in limits where raw (X,Y) procedures cannot; (2) in finite-dimensional statistical problems, aggregation can yield consistent classifiers when standard methods fail.

- Motivating questions: whether aggregation is needed for surrogate consistency; whether/how aggregation helps.

- Paper develops new notions/theory for surrogate consistency with data aggregation.
- In fully nonparametric scenarios, paper claims to show how number of samples aggregated and noise conditions improve consistency.
- Aggregation supposedly allows surrogate risk consistency under weak conditions on the surrogate loss; losses using aggregated labels admit approximate linear comparison inequalities.
- Unlike conventional risk consistency theory requiring hypothesis class F to be all measurable functions, paper will show classification results where aggregation guarantees consistency over restricted hypothesis classes, which may fail without aggregation.

Paper title: “Some Robustness Properties of Label Cleaning” by Chen Cheng and John Duchi.

Main claims from abstract/introduction: label cleaning/aggregation provides robustness impossible without aggregation. Two aspects: (1) improved surrogate-risk consistency (e.g. logistic vs task loss) where aggregated-label procedures can be consistent/optimal in limits where raw (X,Y) procedures cannot; (2) finite-dimensional/statistical settings where aggregation yields consistent classifiers when standard methods fail. Concrete examples promised in ranking and binary/multiclass classification with linear estimators; theory for surrogate consistency with data aggregation; fully nonparametric results on how number of aggregated samples and noise conditions improve consistency; aggregation allows approximate linear comparison inequalities and consistency under weak surrogate-loss conditions, including restricted hypothesis classes where non-aggregated methods may fail.

Section 2 preliminaries: Standard setup: data (X_i,Y_i) iid P on X×Y; scoring f:X→R^d, decoder d:R^d→Y. Task risk initially R(f)=E[ell(d∘f(X),Y)] (eq. 1). Binary example: d=1, decoder sgn(s), ell(y,y')=1{yy'≤0}, so R(f)=P(Y f(X)≤0). They then allow task loss to depend on conditional distribution P(Y∈·|X): R(f)=E[ell(d∘f(X),P(·|X))] (eq. 2), claiming minimizers frequently coincide with original task problem; multiclass example with ell(yhat,P)=Σ_y P(Y=y)1{yhat≠y} equals standard 0-1 error. Surrogate loss φ:R^d×Y→R, surrogate risk R_φ(f)=E[φ(f(X),Y)]. They study consistency in (i) Fisher/classical all Borel functions and (ii) parametric possibly misspecified hypothesis classes. Main message: label aggregation improves consistency in both.

Section 2.1 label aggregation: Instead of Y, observe abstract Z∈Z. Example multiple labels: Z=(Y_1,…,Y_m)∈Y^m. Aggregation space A, aggregating function A:Z→A (e.g. majority vote), surrogate φ:R^d×A→R_+, aggregated surrogate risk R_{φ,A}(f)=E[φ(f(X),A(Z))] (eq. 3). Question: when minimizing (3) suffices to minimize task risk (2).

Example 1 majority vote/repeated sampling: Y_i|X=x iid P_{Y|X=x}; A_m(Z)=argmin_{y∈Y} Σ_{l=1}^m ell(y,Y_l). For 0-1 ell this is majority vote; general form allows abstract procedures.

Example 2 KNN aggregation: Given X with label Y plus iid additional sample (X_i,Y_i)_{i=1}^m, Z=(Y,(X_i,Y_i)_1^m). Order X_i by distance to X, set X_(0)=X. For K≥0, aggregate K-nearest neighbors plus original point via A_{m,K}(Z)=argmin_{y∈Y} Σ_{l=0}^K ell(y,Y_(l)). Appendix C will address single-sample KNN aggregation beyond population-level setup.

Section 3 surrogate consistency. Assumes Fisher/classical setting where F is all Borel measurable f:X→R^d. Defines conditional task risk R(s|x)=ell(d∘s, P(Y|X=x)) and conditional surrogate risk R_phi(s|x)=E[phi(s,Y)|X=x]. Pointwise excess risks delta_ell, delta_phi subtract inf over s∈R^d. Minimal risks R*=inf_F R(f), R_phi*=inf_F R_phi(f). Consistency notions: (i) Fisher consistency: for all P, R_phi(f_n)→R_phi* implies R(f_n)→R*. (ii) uniform comparison: nondecreasing psi with psi(eps)>0 for eps>0 and psi(R(f)-R*)≤R_phi(f)-R_phi* for all f. In binary classification with convex margin losses, these coincide. Calibration: psi(eps,x)=inf{delta_phi(s,x): delta_ell(s,x)≥eps}; overline psi(eps)=inf_x psi(eps,x). Cor. 3.1: phi Fisher consistent iff psi(eps,x)>0 for all x, eps>0. Let psi be Fenchel biconjugate of overline psi; overline psi(eps)>0 iff psi(eps)>0, and comparison inequality holds for all measurable f.

They argue in general risk problem (2), one would like Fisher-consistent surrogate using single paired (X,Y), but this is generally impossible; motivates aggregation theory in Sec. 3.2.

Sec. 3.1 ranking example: k items, labels Y=(i,j), i≠j, indicating i ranked above j. For each x, p_ij=P(Y=(i,j)|x). Define normalized transition matrix C_x with diagonal 0 and off-diagonal (C_x)_ij=p_ij / sum_{l≠j} p_lj, with 0/0=1/(k−1), so C_x^T 1=1. Rank by vector C_x 1 (preference counts). Task loss (decoder incorporated) ell(s,C)=max_{i<j} 1{(s_i−s_j)(e_i−e_j)^T C1 ≤0, (e_i−e_j)^T C1≠0}, penalizing misordered score pairs. Population task risk (4): R(f)=P(f(X) and C_X 1 order differently). Scores restricted to s∈R^k with s^T1=0 since only ordering matters. Proposition 1: for k≥3, no convex surrogate phi:R^k×Y→R is Fisher consistent for ranking risk (4) (proof App. A.1).

Aggregation for ranking: collect m independent pairwise comparisons Z=(Y_1,…,Y_m)|X. If m≥k, define counts m_ij (intended frequency of pair (i,j)) and m_j=sum_i m_ij. Aggregator A(Z)=star if any m_j=0; otherwise returns vector over i: (m_i1/m_1 + m_i2/m_2 + … + m_ik/m_k). Claim: regressing predicted scores f(x) directly on A(Z) when not star yields consistency; Proposition 2 begins next.

Paper title: “Some Robustness Properties of Label Cleaning” by Chen Cheng and John Duchi.

Setup: iid (X,Y), scores f:X→R^d decoded by d, task risk, surrogate risk R_φ, aggregated surrogate R_{φ,A}. A_m repeated-label aggregator minimizes empirical task loss. Q7D calibration gives ψ(R−R*)≤surrogate excess; pair-only Q7D often impossible. Prop1 convex pairwise ranking fails Q7D for k≥3; Prop2 squared loss with aggregation can be Q7D. Prior issues: ranking aggregation formula sums over y∈Y^m instead of observed indices; Eq (5) overlineψ_A uses wrong inf/pointwise form.

Aggregation consistency: Prop3 aggregated Q7D iff pointwise aggregated calibration positive; Cor3.2 m(n)→∞ and W3C φ + small aggregated surrogate excess implies task excess→0. W3C constants C1,C2 via (6a)(6b); hinge W3C (1,2). Theorem1: W3C+J9P+bounded loss+Nα gives linear comparison R−R*≤16/C1 aggregated surrogate excess above threshold involving P(κ>M), e_m(M), ξ_m. Coarse ξ_{m,k}; text wrongly says “lower bounds” threshold. U6A level-(ξ,ζ) has erroneous unaggregated comparison. Noise definitions Δ,Nα,Mβ; binary κ=1 only if Δ>0 a.s.

Examples: binary margin convex φ Lemma3.1 C1=φ(0)−φ(δ), C2=φ(−δ). Matching: k=N!, d=N^2, loss 1/(2N)||v1−v2||_1=1/(2N)||·||_2^2; surrogate W3C C1=1/N,C2=2; threshold displayed; bound constant 16N but displayed with A_n despite m. Section4: Restricted classes. Prop4: for any ε>0 and nonzero θ*, some binary distribution satisfies K7M along θ*, yet every unaggregated surrogate minimizer has higher task risk than θ* and |cos angle|≤ε. Cor4.1 claims from Theorem2 risk→R(fθ*) and cos angle→1; flagged because Theorem2 only states risk consistency.

Theorem2: cone F satisfying K7M and P(Δ>0)=1, ε_m→0 aggregated approximate minimizers of R_{φ,A_m} have R(f_m)→R*. Paper title: “Some Robustness Properties of Label Cleaning” by Chen Cheng and John Duchi.

Abstract claims:
- Aggregated/cleaned labels distilled from noisy responses provide robustness not available without cleaning.

Paper title: “Some Robustness Properties of Label Cleaning” by Chen Cheng and John Duchi.

Earlier abstract/introduction claims:
- Cleaned/aggregated labels from noisy responses provide robustness/consistency not available without cleaning.
- Minimizing convex-ish surrogate losses with cleaned labels gives stronger task-risk consistency than raw-label procedures.

Section 2 preliminaries:
- Two regimes: unrestricted Borel F with classical Fisher consistency; parametric/misspecified F where aggregation improves consistency.
- Data: iid (X_i,Y_i)~P on X×Y. Scores f:X→R^d decoded by d:R^d→Y, prediction d∘f(x).
- Distribution-dependent task criterion defined as R(f)=E_P[ ell(d∘f(X), P(.|X)) ] (eq. 2). For multiclass Y={1,…,k}, ell(yhat,P)=Σ_y P(Y=y)1{yhat≠y}, yielding standard 0-1 error.
- Instantaneous formulation for ell:Y×Y→R_+ minimizes R(f)=E_P[ell(d∘f(X),Y)] over f∈F (eq. 1). Binary: d=1, d(s)=sgn(s), ell(y,y')=1{yy'≤0}, so R(f)=P(Y f(X)≤0). Task losses nonsmooth/nonconvex/flat; surrogate φ:R^d×Y→R gives R_φ(f)=E φ(f(X),Y). Need consistency with task.

Section 2.1 label aggregation:
- Aggregated surrogate risk R_{φ,A}(f)=E[φ(f(X),A(Z))] (eq. 3), assessed against actual task-risk minimization. Z∈Z, aggregation space A, map A:Z→A, φ:R^d×A→R_+.
- Repeated labeling: Z=(Y_1,…,Y_m), Y_i|X=x iid~P_{Y|X=x}. Aggregator A_m(Z)=argmin_y Σ_{l=1}^m ell(y,Y_l); for 0-1 loss this is majority vote. General ell allows abstract aggregation.
- Rough KNN aggregation: observe X,Y plus independent sample (X_i,Y_i)_{i=1}^m iid~P; Z=(Y,(X_i,Y_i)). Order neighbors by dist(X,X_(1))≤…≤dist(X,X_(m)), set X_(0)=X. For K≥0, A_{m,K}(Z)=argmin_y Σ_{l=0}^K ell(y,Y_(l)). Population repeated-sampling treatment extends to one-sample aggregation in Appendix C.

final_notes:
Section 3 surrogate consistency: Fisher/classical; aggregation Prop.3 ψ_A(task excess)≤surrogate excess. Ranking: no convex pairwise surrogate Fisher consistent for k≥3; aggregation via vector sums/squared loss consistent if m≥k. Identifying surrogate Def.3.1: finite Y, constants Cφ1,Cφ2 with witnesses; wrong-decoder gap ≥Cφ1; cross-label value within Cφ2. Majority vote A_m returns empirical task-risk minimizer. Cor.3.2: if m→∞ and aggregated surrogate excess→0 then task excess→0. Level-(ξ,ζ), noise Nα/Mβ; Theorem 1 gives linear comparison beyond threshold; Cor.3.3 explicit ξ, α=1 can get ξ=0. Examples: binary margin Cφ1=φ(0)−φ(δ), Cφ2=φ(−δ); matching structured hinge Cφ1=1/N,Cφ2=2; general structured hinge Cφ1=min loss, Cφ2=max τ+1. Some earlier text had constants apparently inconsistent (16N vs A_n; 8/min ell vs theorem 16/min ell).

§4 restricted/model classes. Binary linear F={x↦<θ,x>}, zero-one; margin convex. For all measurable functions Fisher/uniform iff φ′(0)<0. Optimal predictability along θ*: sign(<θ*,x>)=sign(η(x)−1/2), so θ* is Bayes/task optimal. Prop.4: for any ε and nonzero θ*, distribution optimally predictable along θ* but every surrogate minimizer has higher task risk and angle nearly orthogonal. Aggregation: majority vote labels; Cor.4.1 from Thm2: if ε_m→0 and P optimally predictable along θ*, then R(fθ_m)→R(fθ*) and cos angle→1.

§4.2 multiclass: Y=[k], zero-one, decoder argmax, F linear cone with f^T1=0, closed under positive scaling. Surrogate Fisher consistent and limiting loss φ(s,y)→0 when correct margin grows. Theorem 2: If F is a cone optimally predicting P and unique Bayes label a.s. (P(Δ>0)=1), then any ε_m-argmin of aggregated surrogate risk with majority vote A_m has R(f_m)→R*. Earlier text incorrectly summarized this as arbitrary compact F.

§4.3 finite-dimensional multiclass linear model. Link consistency (14): t_y=max t_i iff σ_y(t)=max σ_i(t), t_k=0. Logistic loss minimizer moment equation. Binary Gaussian result consistent direction despite misspecification. For k≥3 slight misspecification can fail. Theorem 3 additionally assumes Θ*=U*T* with U* orthogonal and T* nonsingular: Θ_m=U*T_m, ||T_m||→∞ and T_m/||T_m||→T*/||T*||.

§5 numerics: truncated quadratic/squared hinge φ=(1−δ)_+^2; ψ=ε²; aggregated ψ_m=(1/16)(ε−sqrt((32/m)log40))_+. Fig.2 corrupted link softmax(t) inside radius r, softmax(αt) outside; preserves argmax for α>0. Caption misstated error as || ||T_m|| − T*/||T*|| ||, conflicting with theorem’s directional convergence.

§6 discussion/future work: emphasizes many consistency results take m→∞; ranking Sec3.1 has explicit finite-m guarantees, but broader finite-m theory open. Notes κ(X) characterizes multiclass comparison inequalities; binary κ=1; κ can be large even when Mammen–Tsybakov α≈1. Says misspecified-model results, especially §4.3, require optimal predictability/Bayes classifier in F; classical consistency can fail even then but aggregation can succeed. Suggests extending aggregation comparison inequalities to restricted H-classes/H-consistency.

Paper title: “Some Robustness Properties of Label Cleaning” by Chen Cheng and John Duchi.

Abstract claims:
- Learning procedures relying on aggregated labels / cleaned labels distilled from noisy responses have robustness properties impossible without data cleaning.
- In risk consistency setting (minimizing surrogate loss instead of task loss like 0-1 error), procedures using label aggregation obtain stronger consistency guarantees than possible using raw labels.
- Classical perfectly specified statistical modeling suggests incorporating all information / modeling label uncertainty is statistically efficient, but consistency fails for “standard” approaches when the minimized loss is even slightly misspecified.
- Procedures leveraging aggregated information still converge to optimal classifiers, suggesting robustness from considering the full data pipeline (collection, fitting, prediction) and refining noisy signals.

Paper title: “Some Robustness Properties of Label Cleaning” by Chen Cheng and John Duchi.

Abstract/introduction main claims:
- Modern supervised datasets often involve data cleaning/filtering/crowdsourcing multiple labels and denoising/aggregating them into “gold standard” labels.
- Paper argues label cleaning / label aggregation provides robustness impossible without aggregation.
- Two robustness aspects: (1) improved consistency when minimizing surrogate loss (e.g. multiclass logistic) instead of task loss (e.g. zero-one error): aggregated-label procedures can achieve consistent/optimal prediction in limits where raw (X,Y) procedures cannot; (2) in finite-dimensional statistical problems, aggregation can yield consistent classifiers when standard methods fail.
- Classical surrogate risk consistency literature usually assumes standard pairs (X,Y) and does not address modern aggregation machinery.
- Motivating questions: whether aggregation is needed for surrogate consistency; whether/how aggregation helps.
- Paper will give concrete examples in ranking and binary/multiclass classification with linear estimators where estimators using only pairs (X,Y) necessarily fail, but label aggregation methods are consistent.
- Paper develops new notions/theory for surrogate consistency with data aggregation.
- In fully nonparametric scenarios, paper claims to show how number of samples aggregated and noise conditions improve consistency.
- Aggregation supposedly allows surrogate risk consistency under weak conditions on the surrogate loss; losses using aggregated labels admit approximate linear comparison inequalities.
- Unlike conventional risk consistency theory requiring hypothesis class F to be all measurable functions, paper will show classification results where aggregation guarantees consistency over restricted hypothesis classes, which may fail without aggregation.

Paper title: “Some Robustness Properties of Label Cleaning” by Chen Cheng and John Duchi.

Main claims from abstract/introduction: label cleaning/aggregation provides robustness impossible without aggregation. Two aspects: (1) improved surrogate-risk consistency (e.g. logistic vs task loss) where aggregated-label procedures can be consistent/optimal in limits where raw (X,Y) procedures cannot; (2) finite-dimensional/statistical settings where aggregation yields consistent classifiers when standard methods fail. Concrete examples promised in ranking and binary/multiclass classification with linear estimators; theory for surrogate consistency with data aggregation; fully nonparametric results on how number of aggregated samples and noise conditions improve consistency; aggregation allows approximate linear comparison inequalities and consistency under weak surrogate-loss conditions, including restricted hypothesis classes where non-aggregated methods may fail.

Section 2 preliminaries: Standard setup: data (X_i,Y_i) iid P on X×Y; scoring f:X→R^d, decoder d:R^d→Y. Task risk initially R(f)=E[ell(d∘f(X),Y)] (eq. 1). Binary example: d=1, decoder sgn(s), ell(y,y')=1{yy'≤0}, so R(f)=P(Y f(X)≤0). They then allow task loss to depend on conditional distribution P(Y∈·|X): R(f)=E[ell(d∘f(X),P(·|X))] (eq. 2), claiming minimizers frequently coincide with original task problem; multiclass example with ell(yhat,P)=Σ_y P(Y=y)1{yhat≠y} equals standard 0-1 error. Surrogate loss φ:R^d×Y→R, surrogate risk R_φ(f)=E[φ(f(X),Y)]. They study consistency in (i) Fisher/classical all Borel functions and (ii) parametric possibly misspecified hypothesis classes. Main message: label aggregation improves consistency in both.

Section 2.1 label aggregation: Instead of Y, observe abstract Z∈Z. Example multiple labels: Z=(Y_1,…,Y_m)∈Y^m. Aggregation space A, aggregating function A:Z→A (e.g. majority vote), surrogate φ:R^d×A→R_+, aggregated surrogate risk R_{φ,A}(f)=E[φ(f(X),A(Z))] (eq. 3). Question: when minimizing (3) suffices to minimize task risk (2).

Example 1 majority vote/repeated sampling: Y_i|X=x iid P_{Y|X=x}; A_m(Z)=argmin_{y∈Y} Σ_{l=1}^m ell(y,Y_l). For 0-1 ell this is majority vote; general form allows abstract procedures.

Example 2 KNN aggregation: Given X with label Y plus iid additional sample (X_i,Y_i)_{i=1}^m, Z=(Y,(X_i,Y_i)_1^m). Order X_i by distance to X, set X_(0)=X. For K≥0, aggregate K-nearest neighbors plus original point via A_{m,K}(Z)=argmin_{y∈Y} Σ_{l=0}^K ell(y,Y_(l)). Appendix C will address single-sample KNN aggregation beyond population-level setup.

Section 3 surrogate consistency. Assumes Fisher/classical setting where F is all Borel measurable f:X→R^d. Paper title: “Some Robustness Properties of Label Cleaning” by Chen Cheng and John Duchi.

Setup: iid (X,Y), scores f:X→R^d decoded by d, task risk R, surrogate R_φ, aggregated surrogate R_{φ,A}. A_m minimizes empirical task loss; T4K appears majority/plurality aggregation. Section 3: conditional risks/excesses, calibration ψ/Q7D, uniform comparison ψ(R−R*)≤surrogate excess. Pair-only Q7D generally impossible; Prop1 convex pairwise ranking fails Q7D for k≥3; Prop2 squared loss with aggregation can be Q7D. Prior internal issues: ranking aggregation formula sums over y∈Y^m instead of observed indices; Eq (5) overlineψ_A uses wrong inf_s/pointwise form.

Aggregation consistency: Prop3 aggregated Q7D iff pointwise aggregated calibration positive, yielding ψ_A(R−R*)≤aggregated surrogate excess. Cor3.2: if m(n)→∞ and W3C φ, small aggregated surrogate excess implies task excess→0. W3C constants Cφ1≤Cφ2 via (6a),(6b); hinge W3C (1,2). Theorem1: W3C+J9P+0≤ℓ≤1+Nα gives R−R*≤16/Cφ1 · aggregated surrogate excess once excess exceeds threshold involving P(κ>M), e_m(M). Coarse ξ_{m,k}; possible text error says coarse quantity “lower bounds” ξ though used as sufficient threshold. U6A level-(ξ,ζ) definition had erroneous unaggregated comparison R_φ(f)−R* instead of surrogate excess. Noise: Δ,Nα,Mβ; κ binary=1 only if Δ>0 a.s. Discussion later overstates this as unconditional “binary problems trivially have κ(X)=1.”

Examples: binary Lemma3.1 margin convex φ W3C: C1=φ(0)−φ(δ), C2=φ(−δ). Matching: k=N!, d=N^2, loss 1/(2N)||v1−v2||_1 = 1/(2N)||·||_2^2, surrogate W3C C1=1/N,C2=2, threshold 4*(32 C_MT^4/m log(4k(2N+1)))^{α/[2(1−α^2)]}, bound constant 16N but displayed with A_n despite m. Discussion: claims main results show fundamental limitations of uncleaned labels and robustness gains from cleaning; finite-m theory beyond ranking remains open; restricted-class/H-consistency aggregation comparisons suggested as future work.

Paper title: “Some Robustness Properties of Label Cleaning” by Chen Cheng and John Duchi.

Abstract claims:
- Aggregated/cleaned labels distilled from noisy responses provide robustness not available without cleaning.
- Minimizing a typically convex surrogate loss with cleaned/aggregated labels yields stronger task-risk consistency guarantees than procedures using raw labels.
- Finite-dimensional classifiers remain consistent under loss misspecification that defeats standard uncertainty-modeling approaches.
- If statistical models are perfectly specified, incorporating all information is more efficient, but even slight loss misspecification destroys standard consistency.
- Aggregation/label cleaning retains convergence to optimal classifiers.
- Overall theme: collection, fitting, and prediction can be jointly robust through noisy-signal refinement.

- Conventional supervised pipeline collects (X_i,Y_i), fits a model, and suppresses cleaning/filtering/repeated crowdsourced labeling/denoising used in modern datasets.
- Work on crowdsourced “gold standard” labels is related, but this paper focuses on fundamental, necessary improvement of fitted-model consistency.
- The paper frames its questions as: whether aggregation is needed, whether pair-based surrogate consistency suffices, and in what sense aggregation improves consistency.

Paper title: “Some Robustness Properties of Label Cleaning” by Chen Cheng and John Duchi.

Earlier abstract/introduction claims:
- Cleaned/aggregated labels from noisy responses provide robustness/consistency not available without cleaning.
- Minimizing convex-ish surrogate losses with cleaned labels gives stronger task-risk consistency than raw-label procedures.

- Linear-estimator examples in ranking, binary, multiclass separate pair-based procedures from aggregation.
- Nonparametric results combine aggregation count and noise conditions, weak surrogate assumptions, and extend beyond unrestricted measurable classes.

Section 2 preliminaries:
- Two regimes: unrestricted Borel F with classical Fisher consistency; parametric/misspecified F where aggregation improves consistency.
- Data: iid (X_i,Y_i)~P on X×Y. Scores f:X→R^d decoded by d:R^d→Y, prediction d∘f(x).
- Distribution-dependent task criterion defined as R(f)=E_P[ ell(d∘f(X), P(.|X)) ] (eq. 2). For multiclass Y={1,…,k}, ell(yhat,P)=Σ_y P(Y=y)1{yhat≠y}, yielding standard 0-1 error.
- Instantaneous formulation for ell:Y×Y→R_+ minimizes R(f)=E_P[ell(d∘f(X),Y)] over f∈F (eq. 1). Binary: d=1, d(s)=sgn(s), ell(y,y')=1{yy'≤0}, so R(f)=P(Y f(X)≤0). Task losses nonsmooth/nonconvex/flat; surrogate φ:R^d×Y→R gives R_φ(f)=E φ(f(X),Y). Need consistency with task.

Section 2.1 label aggregation:
- Aggregated surrogate risk R_{φ,A}(f)=E[φ(f(X),A(Z))] (eq. 3), assessed against actual task-risk minimization. Z∈Z, aggregation space A, map A:Z→A, φ:R^d×A→R_+.
- Repeated labeling: Z=(Y_1,…,Y_m), Y_i|X=x iid~P_{Y|X=x}. Aggregator A_m(Z)=argmin_y Σ_{l=1}^m ell(y,Y_l); for 0-1 loss this is majority vote. General ell allows abstract aggregation.
- Rough KNN aggregation: observe X,Y plus independent sample (X_i,Y_i)_{i=1}^m iid~P; Z=(Y,(X_i,Y_i)). Order neighbors by dist(X,X_(1))≤…≤dist(X,X_(m)), set X_(0)=X. For K≥0, A_{m,K}(Z)=argmin_y Σ_{l=0}^K ell(y,Y_(l)). Population repeated-sampling treatment extends to one-sample aggregation in Appendix C.

final_notes:
Paper title: “Some Robustness Properties of Label Cleaning” by Chen Cheng and John Duchi. Thesis: aggregated/cleaned labels can provide robustness/consistency impossible without cleaning.

Secs.2–3: Task risk R; aggregated surrogate R_{φ,A}. Prop.3 Fisher consistency iff pointwise calibration; comparison ψ_A. Ranking: no convex pair-label surrogate Fisher consistent k≥3, but aggregation of m comparisons with squared loss Fisher consistent if m≥k. Identifying surrogate Def.3.1; generalized majority A_m picks empirical task-loss minimizer. Cor.3.2: if m(n)→∞ and φ identifying, vanishing aggregated surrogate excess implies task excess→0. Level-(ξ,ζ) consistency Def.3.2; earlier opening paragraph misstated direction. Δ=min incorrect excess; binary Δ=|2η−1|. Noise Nα: P(pred differs from Bayes)≤C_MT(R−R*)^α. κ=max incorrect δ/min incorrect δ; binary κ=1 if no zero-margin. Thm.1: under identifying, majority, bounded loss, Nα, if R−R* above threshold involving P(κ>M), e_m(M), then R−R*≤16/Cφ1·aggregated excess. Cor.3.3 formulas have α=1 issue. Examples: binary margin Lemma 3.1 C1=φ(0)−φ(δ), C2=φ(−δ); matching Lemma 3.2 C1=1/N,C2=2, comparison factor 16N, conclusion says A_n likely A_m; structured prediction Lemma 3.3 C1=min incorrect loss, C2=max τ+1, final comparison printed 8/min ell conflicting with Cor.3.3 factor 16/C1.

Sec.4 restricted classes. 4.1 binary linear: Prop.4 says for any ε>0 and nonzero θ*, exists P optimally predictable along θ* such that every surrogate minimizer worse than θ* and |cos(θφ,θ*)|≤ε. Issue: impossible as stated for d=1 and ε<1 if θφ nonzero. Aggregation Cor.4.1: majority A_m with ε_m-argmins gives R(fθm)→R(fθ*) and cos→1.

4.2 multiclass cone: convex nonincreasing margin φ, φ′(0)<0, inf φ=0; Zhang consistency over all measurable sum-zero F. Thm.2: if F cone optimally predicts P, P(Δ(X)>0)=1, majority A_m, ε_m→0, then ε_m-argmins have R(f_m)→R*.

4.3 finite-dimensional multiclass linear: Θ=[θ1…θ_{k−1}], θ_k=0, link σ satisfying consistency (14): t_y max iff σ_y max. Logistic example. Majority-vote distribution p_{Θ,m} via ρ_m; claims ρ_m satisfies (14). Logistic loss minimizer solves E[X(σ^lr(Θ_m^T X)−ρ_m(Θ*^T X))^T]=0. For k=2 Gaussian, even misspecified link yields Θ_m=t_mΘ*, consistent. For k≥3 slight misspecification causes failure (Prop.5): with Σ=I and invertible derivative map D at Θ*, for small ε there is T_ε of measure ≤ε such that Θ_1(ε)/||Θ_1(ε)||≠Θ*/||Θ*||. Earlier definition of σ^ε had prose/formula reversal; claim σ^ε satisfies (14) false generically because uniform on T makes all classes max. Current Thm.3: for Θ*=U*T* with U* orthogonal and T* nonsingular, for majority aggregation under any true link σ satisfying (14), minimizer Θ_m=U*T_m for every m, and ||T_m||→∞, T_m/||T_m||→T*/||T*||. Prose: label aggregation restores asymptotic consistency under misspecification; Prop.5 shows no-aggregation generally inconsistent for k≥3.

Sec.5 numerical illustrations. Binary squared hinge/truncated quadratic φ(δ)=max{1−δ,0}²; cites Bartlett ψ(ε)=ε². Using Lemma 3.1 with δ=1, α=0,C_MT=1 gives ψ_m(ε)=1/16(ε−sqrt(32/m log 40))_+. Claims curves move from quadratic to linear as m→∞. Multiclass logistic k=3,d=2 with corrupted link tildeσ(t)=σlr(t) for ||t||≤r and σlr(αt) outside; Fig.2 θ1*=(0,1), θ2*=(1,1), r=3, α=.1, m={1,4,16,64,256,1024}; n=10000 left, n=640000/m right, T=100 trials. Caption’s error metric written || ||T_m|| − T*/||T*|| || conflicts with Thm.3 normalized direction T_m/||T_m||→T*/||T*||.

Sec.6 discussion: many consistency results take m→∞; ranking Sec.3.1 has explicit finite-m guarantees. Noise condition number κ characterizes multiclass comparison inequalities; binary κ=1. Future directions: finite-m theory, fundamental limits for κ, misspecified models beyond optimal predictability, and restricted-class/H-consistency comparison inequalities with aggregation.

Introduction: Modern supervised data pipelines often require cleaning/filtering/crowdsourcing multiple labels and denoising to create “gold standard” labels. Paper studies how aggregation improves consistency. Two robustness aspects claimed: (1) improved consistency when minimizing surrogate losses (e.g. multiclass logistic) instead of task losses (e.g. zero-one): aggregated labels can achieve consistent optimal prediction when impossible without aggregation; (2) even finite-dimensional statistical problems: aggregation can yield consistent classifiers when standard methods fail.

The paper situates itself relative to surrogate risk consistency literature, which usually assumes standard supervised pairs (X,Y) and does not address aggregation. Main questions: whether aggregation is needed, whether it helps consistency, and in what sense.

Aggregated-label losses admit approximate linear comparison inequalities under weak conditions on surrogate loss. Unlike conventional risk consistency theory requiring hypothesis class F of all measurable functions, they will show classification results where aggregation guarantees consistency over restricted hypothesis classes, which may fail without aggregation.

Paper title: “Some Robustness Properties of Label Cleaning” by Chen Cheng and John Duchi.

Prelims: risk R(f)=E[ell(d∘f(X),P(.|X))] or instantaneous R(f)=E ell(d∘f(X),Y). Surrogate R_phi, aggregated R_{phi,A}. A_m repeated-label aggregator=empirical ell-risk minimizer; rough KNN also defined. Sec2 self-reference likely typo: minimizers of (2) coincide with original problem (2), likely (1).

Sec3: Cor3.1: pointwise psi(e,x)>0 for all x,e>0 iff phi Q7D for ell; biconjugate comparison. Prop1 ranking k>=3: every convex phi:R^k×Y fails Q7D. Prop2 squared loss with response expansion to R^k and m>=k is Q7D. Prop3 aggregation consistency: phi Q7D iff pointwise aggregated calibration positive; comparison for R_{phi,A}. Eq(5) likely typo inf_s not inf_x. Cor3.2: m(n)->∞ and W3C phi, small aggregated surrogate excess implies task consistency. J9P generalized majority vote eventually empirical argmin subset of population minimizers.

W3C constants: exists a_y,s_y with d(s_y)=y. (6a) margin C1; (6b) C2. Binary hinge W3C constants (1,2). Theorem1: W3C+J9P+bounded loss+Nα gives R−R* <=16/C1 aggregated surrogate excess above threshold involving P(kappa>M), C_MT, e_m(M). xi_m->0 for α<1; explicit formulas undefined at α=1 despite text saying α=1 gives xi=0; xi called “lower bound” though used as admissible threshold; sentence mixes surrogate/task optima. U6A level-(xi,zeta): psi(eps)>=zeta eps for eps>=xi. Delta=min incorrect conditional excess; binary |2η−1|. Nα and Mβ equivalent β=α/(1−α). kappa=max/min incorrect excess; binary kappa=1. e_m(t)=t sqrt(2/m log(4k(C1+C2)/C1)).

Examples: Lemma3.1 binary nonsmooth margin convex. Lemma3.3 structured hinge A3J. Matching: |Y|=N!, d=N^2, loss=(1/2N)L1=(1/2N)L2^2; C1=1/N,C2=2; threshold 4*(32 C_MT^4/m log(4 N!(2N+1)))^{α/[2(1−α^2)]}; slope 16N. Errors: structured consequence uses 8/C1 vs theorem 16/C1, and log uses max_hat τ(y) vs max_y τ(y).

Sec4: Prop4 binary finite-dimensional failure; Cor4.1 aggregation restores R->R(theta*) and cos angle->1. Theorem2 cone F/K7M/P(Delta>0)=1/eps_m->0: aggregated surrogate eps-argmin has R(f_m)->R*. Multiclass centered cone, Q7D nonnegative surrogate with margin-limit zero. T4K unique population maximizer. Examples logistic and pairwise losses.

Sec4.3: Prop5 k>=3 Gaussian logistic misspecification causes normalized solution not equal normalized theta*. Theorem3: if Theta*=U*T*, aggregation gives Theta_m=U*T_m, ||T_m||→∞ and normalized T_m→normalized T*. Fitted logistic has θ_k=0, gradient E[X(σ_lr(Θ_m^T X)−ρ_m(Θ*^T X))^T]=0. Binary Gaussian: Θ_m=t_mΘ*. Corrupted σ^ε definition/prose reversed; small positive corruption destroys unaggregated consistency. General L_{m,σ}, Θ_m; aggregation robust under misspecification when some link describes X–Y; unaggregated multiclass generally inconsistent.

Sec5 numerical: D4X/squared-hinge φ(δ)=max{1−δ,0}^2, unaggregated ψ(ε)=ε^2. With δ=1, α=0, C_MT=1, ψ_m(ε)=1/16(ε−sqrt(32/m log40))_+. Fig1 m=2^16..2^32. Mis-specified logistic simulation uses link softmax inside radius r and softmax(αt) outside; d=2,k=3, θ1*=(0,1), θ2*=(1,1), θ3 presumably 0; r=3, α=.1; m=1..1024. Error: Fig2 classification-rule error written || ||T_m|| − T*/||T*|| || conflicts with Theorem3 normalized-direction convergence; should compare normalized T_m to normalized T*.

Sec6 discussion: claims many results need m→∞; ranking has explicit finite-m guarantees; finite-m theory for (ell,phi,m) open. Notes kappa can stay large beyond binary even with low N6Y/α≈1; binary kappa=1. Mis-specified-model results require K7M/Bayes-optimal classifier in F; classical surrogate consistency can fail there while aggregation succeeds. Future directions include restricted-class/H-consistency aggregation comparisons.

Paper title: “Some Robustness Properties of Label Cleaning” by Chen Cheng and John Duchi.

Abstract claims to track/check later:
- Aggregated/cleaned labels (distilled from noisy responses) provide robustness unavailable without cleaning.
- Minimizing a typically convex surrogate loss using cleaned labels gives stronger task-risk consistency guarantees than procedures using raw labels.
- Finite-dimensional classifiers remain consistent under loss misspecification, in cases where standard uncertainty-modeling approaches fail.
- If statistical models are perfectly specified, using all information is more efficient; however, even slight loss misspecification destroys standard consistency.
- Aggregation/cleaning retains convergence to optimal classifiers with every fixed label count.
- Overall thesis: collection, fitting, and prediction can jointly gain robustness through noisy-signal refinement/label cleaning.

Introduction claims to track:
- Aggregation permits consistent optimal prediction under surrogate rather than task loss when unaggregated estimation cannot, including finite-dimensional statistical problems.
- Linear-estimator constructions in ranking, binary classification, and multiclass classification separate procedures restricted to (X,Y) pairs from aggregation procedures.
- Nonparametric results combine aggregation count and noise conditions, allow approximately linear comparison inequalities under weak surrogate conditions, and extend consistency beyond unrestricted measurable hypothesis classes.
- Conventional supervised pipeline collects (X_i,Y_i), fits a model, and suppresses cleaning/filtering/repeated crowdsourced labeling/denoising required by modern datasets.
- Paper’s concern is that this data-cleaning machinery provides a fundamental, necessary improvement of fitted-model consistency.
- Prior pair-based surrogate consistency analyses admit empirical-process theory but not aggregation machinery; paper asks whether aggregation is needed, whether pair-based surrogate consistency suffices, and in what sense aggregation improves consistency.

- Aggregated surrogate risk (3): R_{phi,A}(f)=E[phi(f(X), A(Z))], assessed against actual task-risk minimization. Z in Z, A:Z→A, phi:R^d×A→R_+.

Earlier prelims: task risk R(f)=E[ell(d∘f(X),P(.|X))] or instantaneous R(f)=E ell(d∘f(X),Y). Surrogate risk R_phi(f)=E phi(f(X),Y). Aggregated surrogate risk R_{phi,A}(f)=E phi(f(X),A(Z)); repeated-label aggregator A_m(Z)=argmin_y sum_l ell(y,Y_l); rough KNN aggregation also defined. Earlier noted self-reference in Sec 2 saying minimizers of (2) coincide with “original problem (2)” likely meant (1).

Section 3 surrogate consistency:
- Cor 3.1: positivity of pointwise psi(e,x) for all x,e>0 equivalent to phi being Q7D for ell. If psi is Fenchel biconjugate of overline psi, then overline psi(e)>0 iff psi(e)>0 and comparison inequality psi(R(f)-R*) <= R_phi(f)-R_phi* for every measurable f.
- Standard unrestricted Borel framework requirements: qualitative consistency of surrogate minimization and uniform comparison inequality with nondecreasing positive psi. Conditional risks/excesses defined; calibration psi(e,x)=inf{delta_phi(s,x): delta_ell(s,x)>=e}; uniform overline psi(e)=inf_x psi(e,x).
- Claim: pair-only Q7D generally impossible.

Ranking subsection:
- Prop 1: for ranking with k>=3 outcomes, every convex phi:R^k×Y→R fails Q7D.
- Prop 2: squared loss phi(s,q)=||s-q||^2, phi(s,star)=0, with specified aggregation and m>=k is Q7D for ranking risk. Response expansion to R^k separates positive result from convex single-comparison impossibility.
- Pairwise comparison Y={(i,j): i≠j}; p_ij=P(Y=(i,j)|x). C_x defined with columns normalized by sum_{l≠j}p_lj, 0/0=1/(k−1), C_x^T 1=1; C_x 1 gives preference frequency. Ranking loss ell(s,C)=max_{i<j} 1{(s_i-s_j)(e_i-e_j)^T C1 <=0 and nonzero}; R(f)=P(f(X) and C_X1 order differently). Restriction s^T1=0 minor.
- Internal formula issue: m_ij definition for aggregation sums over y∈Y^m and compares tuple to pair, not observed counts from Z, yet A(Z) uses them as counts.

Aggregation consistency:
- Prop 3: with integrable b bounding delta_ell(f(x),x), phi Q7D iff pointwise aggregated calibration overline psi_A(e,x)>0; psi_A=(overline psi_A)** gives psi_A(R-R*)<=R_{phi,A}-R_{phi,A}*. Defines R_{phi,A}(s|x), delta_{phi,A}. Equation (5) has internal uniform-definition issue: overline psi_A(e)=inf_s overline psi_A(e,x) leaves x free; should parallel inf_x.
- Cor 3.2: for m(n)->∞ and W3C phi, R_{phi,A_m}(f_n)-R_{phi,A_m}*→0 implies R(f_n)-R*→0.
- Finite label-space regime k=card(Y), instantaneous task loss. Ranking fits with card(Y)=k(k−1), slight notation abuse.
- Generalized majority vote J9P: parameters a_y; A_m(y_1,...,y_m)=a_{hat y}, hat y=argmin_y sum_i ell(y,y_i), arbitrary tie-breaking. For iid finite Y_i, random M<∞ exists so for all m≥M empirical argmin subset of population y*(x)=argmin_y E[ell(y,Y)|X=x].

errors.claim: “The crude bound … lower bounds the promised ξ_{m,k} by setting ξ_{m,k}:= …” followed by Corollary 3.3: “every f with R(f)−R*≥ξ_{m,k} satisfies …”

Cor4.1 says from Theorem2 aggregated approx minimizers (majority/T4K labels) with eps_m->0 have R->R(theta*) and cos angle->1.
